name: Asynchronous / unsynchronized / staggered consumer camera rigs (online sub-frame sync, rolling shutter, continuous-time state, latency gain)

cited_work_check.title: VisualSync: Multi-Camera Synchronization via Cross-View Object Motion (NeurIPS 2025)
cited_work_check.note: Offline optimisation. It minimises the epipolar error of moving co-visible points to get per-camera offsets at millisecond accuracy, and has no rendering loop. Its core cue (an epipolar residual of moving points that depends on the time offset) is the same physical cue that ideas 2 and 4 linearise. The novelty therefore lies in making it online, not in the cue.

cited_work_check.title: Dynamic Gaussian Scene Reconstruction from Unsynchronized Videos (AAAI 2026)
cited_work_check.note: Coarse-to-fine per-camera time shift estimated inside per-scene 4DGS optimisation, so it is offline. Correctly characterised.

cited_work_check.title: SyncTrack4D
cited_work_check.note: Uses 4D tracks and FGW optimal transport for frame-level sync, then gets sub-frame sync through a motion-spline 4DGS. Offline. Correctly characterised.

cited_work_check.title: Scanline-Aware Animatable Gaussian Avatars from Rolling-Shutter Videos (RS-Avatar, Aug 2026)
cited_work_check.note: Multi-camera rolling-shutter modelling that composites sub-frame renders scanline by scanline. It is per-subject, avatar-specific and optimisation-based, so 'per-scene, avatar-only' is fair. It already makes the point that each camera in a rig has its own readout schedule, which weakens any claim to be first to model rolling shutter in multi-view Gaussian reconstruction.

cited_work_check.title: SPARK: Scalable Real-Time Point Cloud Aggregation with Multi-View Self-Calibration
cited_work_check.note: Online extrinsic self-calibration plus confidence-driven fusion. The abstract has no time or rolling-shutter modelling. Correctly characterised.

cited_work_check.title: Tele360: Real-Time Feed-Forward Human Reconstruction from Sparse Unposed Cameras
cited_work_check.note: Section 3.1 says the input arrives as synchronised 2K frames. Model latency is about 35 ms; end-to-end latency is about 500-650 ms. The 'assumes sync' claim is accurate.

cited_work_check.title: No Pose, No Problem in 4D (NoPo4D)
cited_work_check.note: Ideas 2 and 4 correctly say it assumes synchronised streams. Idea 3 lists it as an 'unposed and unsynced' baseline, which is wrong: the paper assumes time-synchronised streams and names asynchronous capture as an open limitation. It is also not real-time (under 5 s per scene).

cited_work_check.title: 4DSloMo: 4D Reconstruction for High Speed Scene with Asynchronous Capture (SIGGRAPH Asia 2025)
cited_work_check.note: Staggered hardware trigger delays are known, not estimated. It runs per-scene 4DGS optimisation (7k+7k iterations) with a diffusion artifact fixer, and reports no latency. Correctly characterised as offline with a slow-motion goal.

cited_work_check.title: ASTRA: Asynchronous Spatio-Temporal Reconstruction via Trajectory Alignment
cited_work_check.note: Offline joint optimisation of offsets and a dynamic representation. The v3 page carries a withdrawal notice (the statistical analysis needs re-verification), so it should not be relied on as a baseline.

cited_work_check.title: LiveStre4m
cited_work_check.note: Feed-forward live NVS from unposed views with DiT interpolation. It assumes synchronised streams.

cited_work_check.title: 4D Reconstruction from Sparse Dynamic Cameras
cited_work_check.note: Uses independently moving sparse cameras and is optimisation-based. The abstract does not make it clear whether the 'LetCamsGo' benchmark name comes from this paper; I did not verify it.

threats.title: Synchronization and Rolling Shutter Compensation for Consumer Video Camera Arrays
threats.what_overlaps: The same problem statement: consumer camera arrays with no genlock plus rolling shutter. It treats sync and rolling shutter jointly as a single temporal-shear problem and fixes both with a sub-frame warp along optical flow, using a different time offset per scanline. This is the 'every pixel has a timestamp, advect it along flow' idea of ideas 1 and 4, in 2D.
threats.what_remains_different: Offline post-processing, driven by strobes or flow, with no online offset estimation from 3D fusion residuals, no 3D scene-flow advection of splats, and no live NVS or latency angle. Any rolling-shutter-plus-sync-as-one-timestamp-model claim must cite it and cannot be framed as new.

threats.title: VisualSync: Multi-Camera Synchronization via Cross-View Object Motion
threats.what_overlaps: Its core cue is that moving points violate epipolar geometry in proportion to the time offset while static points constrain pose, which it uses to recover per-camera millisecond offsets for unsynchronised consumer videos. Ideas 2 and 4's key insight is a linearisation of this same cue.
threats.what_remains_different: Batch and offline: it relies on tracklets, off-the-shelf SfM and a global optimisation. It does not use online or recursive estimation, TSDF or depth-fusion residuals, rolling shutter, or in-loop compensation for rendering.

threats.title: Online Temporal Calibration for Monocular Visual-Inertial Systems (VINS-Mono td), and Li & Mourikis 2014 'Online temporal calibration for camera-IMU systems'
threats.what_overlaps: The estimation mechanism of ideas 1, 2 and 4 is established here. A time offset enters the state of an online EKF or sliding-window optimiser, and measurements are shifted by the image-plane feature velocity times td, so the residual is linear in td and the extra cost is negligible.
threats.what_remains_different: These works cover camera-to-IMU offsets for ego-motion (sparse features, static world). The proposal targets camera-to-camera offsets where the scene moves, estimated from dense depth-fusion residuals with a static/dynamic split for pose versus time, and used to compensate rendering. The 'EKF over delta_c with Jacobian = velocity' is therefore a known recipe transplanted, not a new estimator.

threats.title: 4DSloMo: 4D Reconstruction for High Speed Scene with Asynchronous Capture
threats.what_overlaps: Idea 3's 'stagger instead of genlock' premise: deliberately staggered camera triggers turn N cameras at f fps into an effective N*f fps capture for dynamic 3D reconstruction. Classic precursors are Si Lu, 'High-speed Video from Asynchronous Camera Array' (WACV 2019, https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.06034) and Wilburn et al.'s camera arrays.
threats.what_remains_different: Offsets are known from hardware triggers, reconstruction is per-scene 4DGS plus a diffusion fixer, and the goal is slow motion. There is no online state, no unknown-offset estimation, and no display-time or latency objective.

threats.title: Asynchronous Multi-View SLAM
threats.what_overlaps: Idea 3's 'rig as an asynchronous sensor network with a continuous-time state updated per camera frame' is the defining idea of this paper, which uses a continuous-time motion model across asynchronous multi-frames.
threats.what_remains_different: It models ego-motion of a rigid rig in a static world, not a dynamic scene seen by a fixed rig. It has no dense TSDF, no scene flow and no view synthesis.

threats.title: FusionMLS: Highly dynamic 3D reconstruction with consumer-grade RGB-D cameras
threats.what_overlaps: Real-time, GPU-based fusion of several unsynchronised consumer RGB-D cameras. It interpolates depth frames to a common time before volumetric fusion, which is the 'motion-compensate each view to a common timestamp before fusion, live' component.
threats.what_remains_different: It appears to rely on known device timestamps, with no estimation of sub-frame offsets or rolling shutter. The output is meshes, not IBR or NVS, and there is no learned blending or latency study.

threats.title: Scanline-Aware Animatable Gaussian Avatars from Rolling-Shutter Videos (RS-Avatar)
threats.what_overlaps: Multi-camera per-scanline timing inside a Gaussian renderer, where each camera has its own readout schedule.
threats.what_remains_different: Per-subject optimisation of animatable avatars. It is not online, not a generic scene and not a feed-forward pipeline, and offsets are not estimated from fusion residuals.

threats.title: Dynamic Gaussian Scene Reconstruction from Unsynchronized Videos / SyncTrack4D / Humans as a Calibration Pattern / Sync-NeRF / ASTRA
threats.what_overlaps: Per-camera sub-frame offsets estimated jointly with a dynamic 3D representation, with NVS quality as the objective.
threats.what_remains_different: All are per-scene offline optimisations, and none is online or streaming with in-loop compensation.

novelty.remaining_novel_angle:
Almost every component already exists, but I found no 2024-2026 work, among what I could search, that does the following. It estimates per-camera sub-frame time offsets, and optionally rolling-shutter readout, online and recursively, frame by frame. It uses the residuals of a live multi-view depth fusion (image-based TSDF) as the measurement, relying on the static/dynamic pixel split that already separates extrinsic drift (static pixels) from timing (dynamic pixels). It feeds those estimates straight back into a real-time geometry-guided IBR renderer through motion-compensated forward splatting to an arbitrary render or display timestamp.

What is not defensible as new:
- The per-pixel-timestamp view of sync plus rolling shutter with flow warping (Bradley 2009).
- The moving-point epipolar cue (VisualSync).
- Online EKF estimation of a time offset with a velocity Jacobian (VINS-Mono and Li & Mourikis, camera-IMU).
- Staggered capture for temporal resolution (4DSloMo, Si Lu 2019).
- Continuous-time asynchronous multi-camera state (AMV-SLAM).
- Real-time interpolation of unsynchronised RGB-D (FusionMLS).

Secondary defensible contributions:
- A benchmark with exact offset ground truth, built by phase-subsampling high-fps genlocked captures. DyNeRF is 30 fps, so this needs a 120 fps+ source.
- A measured capture-to-photon latency gain from rendering at the display timestamp in multi-camera 3D telepresence. The principle is known from VR timewarp, but it has apparently not been quantified for live multi-view IBR.

Framing must be 'online, in-the-loop, geometry-residual-driven sync for live 3D video', not 'first to model desync or rolling shutter'.
novelty.best_variant:
The best variant combines Idea 4 (SyncFree, fusion-residual reformulation) with Idea 1's rolling-shutter and display-time extensions.

Idea 4's key insight is the most specific and least scooped piece: the image-based TSDF signed-distance residual is already computed and is linear in the offset times the 3D velocity on dynamic pixels, while static pixels inform extrinsics. It ties directly to the base pipeline, and its phase-subsampling benchmark gives exact ground truth.

Idea 1 adds per-row rolling-shutter timing and rendering at the vsync timestamp. Rolling shutter should be an ablation, not the headline, because Bradley 2009 and RS-Avatar pre-empt 'unified RS+sync' novelty.

Idea 2 is weaker. Its epipolar-residual layer is essentially VisualSync's cue made recursive, and a 'differentiable LM layer' mirrors Tele360's pose LM, so a reviewer would call it incremental.

Idea 3's headline, that deliberate staggering reduces latency and raises temporal resolution, collides with 4DSloMo, Si Lu (WACV 2019) and AMV-SLAM's continuous-time state. It survives only as an experiment inside the paper: at equal camera budget, a staggered rig plus a continuous-time state gives measurably lower capture-to-photon latency. Idea 3 also mis-cites NoPo4D as handling unsynchronised input, which it does not.

Related work must cite Bradley 2009, VINS-Mono or Li & Mourikis online temporal calibration, AMV-SLAM and FusionMLS. Otherwise reviewers from graphics or robotics will reject the novelty claims.

sharpened.title: Clocks from Geometry: Online Sub-Frame Synchronization from Depth-Fusion Residuals for Live 3D Video on Unsynchronized Rigs
sharpened.one_liner: The signed-distance residual that a live image-based TSDF already computes is a sensor for each camera's sub-frame clock offset. Estimating those offsets recursively and splatting every view to one common timestamp gives unsynchronized consumer depth units near-genlock 3D video quality at under 5 ms of extra cost per frame, and lets the renderer query the scene at display time.
sharpened.core_claim:
Setup: 6-8 depth-capable units, each self-synced internally (RGB-D, stereo module or phone with LiDAR) but not synced to each other, running at 30 fps with unknown offsets drawn from U(0, 33 ms) plus slow clock drift.

Claim 1 (estimator): a recursive estimator driven only by the pipeline's TSDF residuals on dynamic pixels recovers each camera's offset to a median error under 2 ms (90th percentile under 4 ms). It converges within 1 s of the onset of conversational or gesture motion and tracks clock drift and jumps, all online.

Claim 2 (rendering): motion-compensated forward splatting to a common timestamp recovers at least 75% of the dynamic-region LPIPS/PSNR gap between the uncompensated pipeline and a genlocked oracle. It comes within 0.3 dB of the same pipeline fed offline VisualSync offsets or ground-truth offsets, and adds at most 5 ms per frame.

Claim 3 (identifiability): the offset's Cramér-Rao bound, derived in closed form from depth noise and the distribution of normal-projected scene velocity, predicts the measured offset error within a factor of 2 across motion levels and depth sources.

The claims are falsified if any of the following holds on the phase-subsampled real benchmark:
- offset error exceeds 5 ms;
- compensation recovers less than 50% of the gap;
- the uncompensated gap is itself perceptually negligible (under 0.3 dB and no significant 2AFC preference) at telepresence motion speeds.
sharpened.key_insight:
In an image-based TSDF, the per-ray signed-distance residual between view k and the fused surface can be linearised around the offset. For a dynamic surface point with 3D velocity v it is approximately n^T v · δ_k. For static points it depends only on extrinsic error.

From this follow three things:
- The static/dynamic split that the base pipeline already makes separates time from pose. Static pixels inform the SE(3) drift and moving pixels inform δ.
- The information about δ is Σ (n^T v)^2 / σ_z^2. That gives a closed-form observability test: update the clock only when the scene moves enough, and hold it otherwise, which is harmless because offsets do not matter when nothing moves.
- Once δ is known, the same velocity field that made δ observable also removes its effect. Each pixel-Gaussian is advected by v·(t* − τ_k), and t* can be any query time, including the display vsync.

The cue is the same physical cue as VisualSync's moving-point epipolar error and the estimator is the VINS-Mono t_d recipe. The new part is that the measurement is dense, three-dimensional and free: it comes from the fusion that the renderer already runs. That makes sub-frame sync a by-product of live rendering rather than an offline pre-process.
sharpened.method:
All numbers below are targets for an RTX 4090/5090-class GPU at 960x540 per view, K=6-8.

(1) Per-camera motion. Optical flow between consecutive frames of the same camera uses a fast network (NeuFlow-v2/RAFT-small class, about 3-6 ms batched). Together with that camera's own depth pair it gives per-pixel 3D velocity v and a velocity covariance Σ_v. Depth is always intra-unit synchronized: an RGB-D sensor, a stereo module, or monocular metric depth as a stress test. This removes the chicken-and-egg problem of multi-view stereo across unsynced cameras.

(2) Timestamp model. τ_k(u) = t_k^arrival + δ_k + ρ_k·row(u). The rolling-shutter slope ρ_k is an optional ablation and is known or fixed for global-shutter units. δ_k drifts as a random walk with a small process noise (clock drift of tens of ppm), plus a jump detector for frame drops and clock resets.

(3) Measurement. On about 10-20k subsampled pixels, reuse the pipeline's TSDF signed-distance residuals s_k after advecting view k's points to the fusion time. The Jacobian ∂s_k/∂δ_k = n^T v. A Huber-robust per-camera Gauss-Newton or EKF update over [δ_k, ρ_k] costs well under 1 ms. The reference camera is fixed to remove gauge freedom.

(4) Separating pose from time. Static pixels drive a low-rate (about 1 Hz) SE(3) drift update per camera. The static/dynamic weights are re-derived in scene space from TSDF residual magnitude and velocity, replacing image differencing.

(5) Observability gating. Update only when the accumulated Fisher information exceeds a threshold. Report the Cramér-Rao bound as a per-camera confidence.

(6) Uncertainty-aware motion-compensated forward splatting. Each pixel-Gaussian is displaced by v·(t* − τ_k), and its footprint is inflated by (t* − τ_k)^2 Σ_v so that uncertain motion blurs softly instead of ghosting. The temporal depth filter and TSDF run on the compensated points.

(7) Blend U-Net. Add per-view |t* − τ_k| and velocity-confidence channels. Fine-tune with random offset and rolling-shutter augmentation generated from phase-subsampled or synthetic data, keeping the same L1 + perceptual loss as the base paper.

(8) Display-time mode. Query t* equal to the predicted vsync time, which is short extrapolation of at most one frame interval. Report the latency/quality trade-off curve against capture-time rendering.

No new large network is involved. Total added cost targets 5 ms or less, dominated by flow. The base pipeline must be reimplemented (image-based TSDF, pixel-Gaussian splatting, 4-level U-Net) unless the authors' code is available.
sharpened.why_not_engineering:
Three contributions go beyond a system tweak:
- An identifiability result: a closed-form Cramér-Rao bound on camera-to-camera sub-frame offsets from dense depth-fusion residuals in a dynamic scene, with a static/dynamic decoupling of pose and time. It is validated empirically and predicts when online sync is possible (motion level, depth noise, number of views).
- The coupling of estimation and rendering. The velocity field that makes the clock observable also cancels its effect, and uncertainty-inflated splats turn estimation error into graceful blur rather than ghosting. This yields a principled continuous-time query of the scene, including at display time.
- The first benchmark with exact sub-frame offset ground truth for live multi-view view synthesis, built by phase-subsampling genlocked high-fps capture plus a real unsynced consumer rig with an LED-timecode reference.

Reviewers will still see a strong systems flavour. The paper must lead with the bound and the benchmark, and present the estimator as their consequence rather than as the contribution.
sharpened.differentiation:
Against the main prior work:
- Bradley et al. 2009 (PROCAMS). They treat sync and rolling shutter jointly as per-scanline time with 2D flow warping, offline. We cite it as the origin of the per-pixel timestamp view and claim only the online, 3D, fusion-residual-driven estimation and in-renderer compensation.
- VisualSync (NeurIPS 2025). It uses the same moving-point geometric cue but as an offline batch optimisation over tracklets and SfM, and its reported median sync error is under 50 ms. We are recursive and online, use dense 3D TSDF residuals instead of sparse epipolar distances, and target under 2 ms. VisualSync serves as the offline upper-bound baseline.
- VINS-Mono t_d and Li & Mourikis. We acknowledge the EKF-with-velocity-Jacobian recipe. They estimate camera-to-IMU offset for ego-motion in a static world; we estimate camera-to-camera offsets for a fixed rig observing a moving scene, where the scene itself carries the timing signal. We include a sparse-feature VINS-style transplant as a baseline to show why dense fusion residuals matter.
- Sync-NeRF, 2511.11175, SyncTrack4D and ASTRA. These are per-scene offline optimisations and serve as quality ceilings. ASTRA is withdrawn, so we do not rely on it.
- 4DSloMo and Si Lu (WACV 2019). Staggering for temporal resolution uses known trigger offsets offline. Staggering appears only as one experiment (equal-budget latency), not as a claim.
- AMV-SLAM. Its continuous-time asynchronous state is for ego-motion; we cite it for the continuous-time framing.
- FusionMLS. It does real-time interpolation of unsynced RGB-D using device timestamps, with no offset estimation and no image-based rendering (IBR). It is the direct 'known timestamps' baseline.
- RS-Avatar (2026). It gives per-scanline multi-camera timing inside an avatar optimisation. Rolling shutter is an ablation for us, not a headline.
- Tele360, LiveStre4m and NoPo4D. These are live or feed-forward but assume synchronized streams (NoPo4D does not handle asynchrony, contrary to one of the cluster ideas). Our module is complementary and could plug into them.
- SPARK. It does online extrinsic self-calibration only and has no time modelling.

datasets: Sync-NeRF 'Unsynchronized Dynamic Blender' dataset (https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13356): synthetic with known offsets. Plus our own Blender renders of animated humans (e.g. Mixamo/AMASS-driven) at 240 fps with GT depth and simulated rolling shutter. These give exact offset ground truth and are used for the CRB validation and the 2-week test.

DyNeRF / Neural 3D Video (30 fps): frame-level shifts and synthetic rolling shutter. Sub-frame shifts via interpolation are reported separately and flagged as approximate, because interpolation artifacts leak into the ground truth.
ENeRF-Outdoor: real, uncontrolled sync and colour errors, evaluated at full resolution, which the base paper could not do. There is no GT offset, so report NVS quality only.

DNA-Rendering and CMU Panoptic (hardware-synchronized, dense views, about 30 fps): frame-level plus synthetic sub-frame perturbation, testing generalisation across view counts. Verify frame rate and licence before committing.
D3DMV (base-paper continuity) with the same synthetic perturbation protocol.
4DSloMo staggered-capture data (https://github.com/OpenImagingLab/4DSloMo), only if released. The README I checked still listed the dataset upload as pending, so do not plan around it.

CUSTOM (required): a genlocked 6-8-camera global-shutter rig at 120-240 fps, phase-subsampled to 30 fps per camera to give exact sub-frame GT, with 2 extra genlocked cameras held out for NVS. Plus a real unsynced consumer rig (4-6 RGB-D units or LiDAR phones and webcams) with an LED-timecode panel for GT offsets, and a photodiode for capture-to-photon latency.

experiments.capture_notes:
Public multi-view dynamic datasets are almost all around 30 fps and genlocked. None I could verify offers the 120 fps+ genlocked capture that phase-subsampling needs for exact sub-frame offset GT, and the 4DSloMo data appeared unreleased on its GitHub. Sub-frame GT on public data therefore comes only from synthetic renders (Sync-NeRF Blender set, own Blender humans) or approximate interpolation.

For a credible CVPR/ICCV paper the team should build two rigs:
(a) 6-8 hardware-triggered global-shutter machine-vision cameras at 120-240 fps (roughly USD 3-6k with lenses and a trigger box), calibrated once, capturing about 10-20 sequences of conversational and gesture motion with 2 held-out views.
(b) An unsynced consumer rig of 4-6 RGB-D units, LiDAR phones or webcams, with a visible LED timecode panel (microcontroller-driven, 1 ms resolution) for GT offsets and a photodiode on the display for latency.

The benchmark should be released, since it is a core contribution. Budget 4-6 weeks of student time for rig build, calibration and capture.

review.first_two_week_test:
Week 1: render a Blender scene of 1-2 animated humans with gestures (plus the Sync-NeRF Unsynchronized Dynamic Blender scenes) from 8 fixed cameras at 240 fps, with GT depth and 2 held-out views. Phase-subsample each training camera to 30 fps with a random offset in U(0, 33 ms). Implement a minimal image-based TSDF (projective signed-distance fusion along target rays) and a point/pixel-Gaussian forward splatter. Per camera, use RAFT/NeuFlow flow plus that camera's depth for velocity. Run the per-camera Gauss-Newton/EKF update on δ from dynamic-pixel TSDF residuals.

Week 2: repeat with realistic depth noise (GT depth plus a Kinect-like noise model, and monocular metric depth) and with slower 'talking-head' motion.

Measure:
(i) offset error vs time and vs the closed-form CRB;
(ii) dynamic-region PSNR/LPIPS at held-out views for no compensation, estimated-δ compensation, GT-δ compensation and genlocked capture;
(iii) the size of the uncompensated gap as a function of motion speed.

No blend network is needed; use simple depth-tested weighted blending. That is enough to show whether the residual carries the clock and whether removing the clock error matters.
review.kill_criteria:
Kill the idea, or demote it to a workshop or systems note, if any of these holds:
(1) With realistic depth noise, the median offset error stays above 5 ms (15% of a frame) after 2 s of gesture-level motion, or the CRB is off from the measured variance by more than 3x, meaning the linear-residual model does not describe reality.
(2) Estimated-δ compensation recovers less than 50% of the dynamic-region gap to GT-δ compensation.
(3) The uncompensated half-frame desync gap at telepresence motion speeds (head, torso, hands up to about 1.5 m/s) is below 0.3 dB PSNR and below 0.01 LPIPS on dynamic regions with no visible ghosting. If so, the problem is not worth a paper for telepresence, and offline sync or software timestamps suffice.
(4) A simple software-timestamp + interpolation baseline, or the sparse-feature VINS-style estimator, matches the dense fusion-residual estimator within noise. The contribution would then collapse to engineering.
(5) Before submission, a 2026 paper appears that does online camera-to-camera sub-frame sync inside a live NVS/fusion loop. Re-run the arXiv search, since the novelty hunter's coverage of Jul-Sep 2026 was weakened by rate limits, and mine was too.

reviewer_objections.objection: Just use hardware sync. Genlock or trigger cables for RGB-D sensors and machine-vision cameras are cheap, so this solves a non-problem.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal:
Phones, laptops, webcams and most consumer RGB-D or stereo units cannot be triggered together. UVC and host timestamps jitter by several ms and drift. Cross-device PTP is unavailable on these devices. Even genlocked rolling-shutter rigs have per-row timing.

We will measure the real timestamp jitter and offsets of the consumer rig to back this up. The same machinery also gives display-time rendering, which cuts capture-to-photon latency for synced rigs too, so the contribution does not depend on the rig being unsynced.

reviewer_objections.objection: This is VINS-Mono's online time-offset EKF plus VisualSync's moving-point epipolar cue, transplanted into a renderer. It is incremental engineering.
Chicken-and-egg: depth computed from unsynchronized cameras is itself corrupted, so the residuals are biased.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: The setting is scoped to units whose depth is internally synchronized (RGB-D, stereo modules, LiDAR phones, or monocular metric depth), which is the realistic consumer case. Only the inter-unit clocks are unknown. An ablation over depth sources shows where the linearisation breaks, and the CRB predicts that degradation.

reviewer_objections.objection: Gains appear only for fast motion; telepresence is mostly slow talking heads, and constant-velocity extrapolation fails on sudden gestures.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Results are stratified by motion speed. A half-frame offset at 1.5 m/s hand speed is about 25 mm, which is tens of pixels at 1 m, and the ghosting that causes is exactly what users notice. Compensation interpolates within the frame interval rather than extrapolating, except in the optional display-time mode, where we report an explicit latency/quality Pareto curve. Uncertainty-inflated splats degrade gracefully, and during slow motion the gate keeps the offsets fixed, where they are harmless.

reviewer_objections.objection: Rolling-shutter-plus-sync as per-pixel time is old (Bradley 2009) and multi-camera rolling-shutter Gaussians exist (RS-Avatar); the benchmark relies on synthetic or interpolated offsets.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We claim no novelty for the timestamp model; rolling shutter is an ablation, and both works are cited. The benchmark's real part uses phase-subsampled 120-240 fps genlocked capture with exact GT, plus an LED-timecode consumer rig. Interpolation-based public-data results are labelled approximate and are not used for the headline claims.

effort.months: 6-8 (about 1 month for the base-pipeline reimplementation, 1-1.5 months for rig build and capture, 3-4 months for method, experiments and user study, plus writing)
effort.people: 1 PhD student full-time plus 1 part-time (rig, capture, latency measurement), with an advisor versed in state estimation
effort.compute: Modest: 1-4 RTX 4090/5090-class GPUs. Only the blend U-Net is fine-tuned (tens of GPU-hours). The estimator is classical. Hardware is about USD 3-6k for the genlocked high-fps rig, about USD 1-2k for the consumer rig, and an LED timecode board and photodiode for well under USD 200.

review.venue: ICCV 2027 (deadline around March 2027) if the CRB/identifiability analysis and the exact-GT benchmark are strong. Otherwise IEEE ISMAR 2027 (TVCG journal track) or IEEE VR 2028, where the consumer-rig and latency story is valued. 3DV is a fallback. CVPR 2027 (November 2026) is too soon given the capture needed.
review.synergies:
Synergies with other telepresence directions:
- Glass-to-glass latency, late reprojection and asynchronous spacewarp: the same continuous-time query powers display-time rendering. This gives a natural two-paper series, 'clocks from geometry', then 'render at vsync'.
- Online calibration-drift and self-calibration work (SPARK-style): the static-pixel SE(3) branch unifies time and pose self-calibration into one 'self-maintaining rig' paper.
- Pose-free feed-forward live systems (Tele360, LiveStre4m, NoPo4D): the sync module is a drop-in fix for their synced-stream assumption.
- Long-horizon temporal consistency and recurrent state: clock drift and jumps are a long-horizon robustness axis.
- Heterogeneous rigs with mixed frame rates and sensors, including phones plus RGB-D units, and event cameras: the per-pixel timestamp model generalises directly.
- Bandwidth-aware streaming: staggered, asynchronous arrivals smooth network and compute burstiness, and time metadata supports receiver-side compensation.
- Learned robustness 'fixer' networks trained on synthetic desync, rolling-shutter and extrinsic-jitter degradations: the benchmark supplies their paired training data.

threats.title: Perceptual Quality Assessment of NeRF and Neural View Synthesis Methods for Front-Facing Views (Liang, Wu, Hanji, Banterle, Gao, Mantiuk; CGF 2024)
threats.what_overlaps: The first controlled perceptual QA of NVS methods using reference video sequences, explicitly to expose temporal artifacts that image metrics miss. It benchmarks many image and video metrics against human scores. This already makes the argument that 'NVS metrics are temporally blind; validate against video perception' (Mantiuk group).
threats.what_remains_different: 2D monitor, MOS/JOD scaling only, no threshold psychophysics. It uses offline per-scene NeRFs, not online IBR. It has no binocular or HMD condition, no controlled artifact generators (depth wobble, K-set popping, interocular weight mismatch) and no new metric or loss.

threats.title: Subjective and Objective Quality Assessment of Rendered Human Avatar Videos in Virtual Reality (LIVE-Meta Rendered Human Avatar VQA; Chen, Saha, Chapiro, Häne, Bazin, ..., Bovik)
threats.what_overlaps: Human (telepresence-style 'hologram') avatar videos rated in 6DoF VR headsets. It releases a dataset and a new VQA model (HoloQA), and is Meta-affiliated. It covers 'perceptual metric for 3D human video viewed in an HMD'.
threats.what_remains_different: The distortions are encoding/compression parameters on mesh avatars, not synthesis inconsistencies (temporal depth wobble, blend popping, disocclusion shimmer). It uses MOS rather than JND thresholds, has no binocular-inconsistency factor and does not decompose error into temporal, view-path and binocular channels.

threats.title: Dichoptic Foveation (Kam, Groth, Kang, Saraf, Sun, Chen; SIGGRAPH 2026)
threats.what_overlaps: HMD psychophysics on interocular differences (blur in one eye, sharpening in the other) across retinal eccentricity. It scales to JOD and fits a compact 4D model, then applies it in a VR rendering system. It shows that the 'binocular channel with eccentricity-dependent psychophysical model fitted to JOD' methodology is current and has been done for interocular frequency differences.
threats.what_remains_different: Its interocular differences are deliberate static frequency manipulations for foveation, not temporally varying, structured view-synthesis inconsistencies (different blend weights or hallucinations per eye, disocclusion mismatch). It has no temporal or view-switching channel and does not assess NVS quality.

threats.title: What Makes for a Good Stereoscopic Image? (SCOPE dataset + iSQoE; Tamir et al., Isola, Dekel, Zhang, Farber)
threats.what_overlaps: 2AFC preference annotations collected in VR headsets on real and synthetic stereo images with many common stereo artifacts. It trains a learned stereo QoE model (iSQoE) and reports cross-headset consistency. This covers 'a binocular perceptual metric learned from HMD data'.
threats.what_remains_different: Still images only, with no temporal or view-path component. It does not target IBR/NVS-specific inconsistency generators, fits no thresholds and makes no psychophysical decomposition. It is a learned black box, not an interpretable JND-calibrated model.

threats.title: No-reference quality assessment of DIBR-synthesized videos by measuring temporal flickering (Zhou et al., JVCIR 2018), and related DIBR flicker metrics (TIP 2019, IEEE 2021 reference-free spatio-temporal metric; SIAT/IRCCyN databases)
threats.venue: J. Visual Communication and Image Representation 2018 / IEEE TIP 2019
threats.what_overlaps: A long pre-neural line of work: metrics dedicated to temporal flicker in depth-image-based-rendered synthesized video (flicker region detection, spatio-temporal inconsistency), validated on subjective databases (SIAT: 140 synthesized videos). Stereoscopic 3D VQA with binocular rivalry is also well studied pre-2020. This weakens any claim that 'a temporal-flicker metric for synthesized views' is new.
threats.what_remains_different: Legacy MVD/DIBR codecs on 2D or passive-stereo displays, MOS-only. It has no HMD head-path viewing, no neural blend-weight/K-set popping, no psychophysical (TCSF/Panum) calibration and no differentiable loss.

threats.title: Temporally Aware Objective Quality Metric for Immersive Video (IV-PSNR-YUVM; Stankowski, Sójka, Grajek, Dziembowski)
threats.what_overlaps: Explicitly targets flicker introduced by view synthesis in MPEG immersive video by adding motion information to IV-PSNR, and correlates with subjective scores.
threats.what_remains_different: Engineering metric without psychophysical fit, JND data, HMD or binocular term. It is not tied to neural/IBR telepresence artifacts.

threats.title: Evaluating Human Perception of Novel View Synthesis: Subjective QA of GS and NeRF in Dynamic Scenes
threats.what_overlaps: Dynamic-scene NVS subjective study, with a finding that objective metrics correlate poorly with humans.
threats.what_remains_different: 2D screen, MOS, no thresholds, no stereo, no model or metric.

threats.title: GScomp-QA / 3DGS-VBench / GS-QA / 3DGS-QA (2025-2026 GS quality datasets)
threats.what_overlaps: Video-based subjective datasets for Gaussian splatting quality (compression or reconstruction degradations), with benchmarks of many metrics. 3DGS-QA (arXiv 2511.08032) proposes a no-reference metric on native Gaussians.
threats.what_remains_different: Static scenes, compression and reconstruction distortions, 2D displays, MOS only. No temporal-dynamic synthesis inconsistency, no binocular component, no thresholds.

novelty.remaining_novel_angle: Every ingredient has prior work: NVS video perceptual QA (Liang et al. CGF 2024, 2501.08072), HMD avatar VQA (LIVE-Meta TIP 2024), learned stereo QoE from VR 2AFC (SCOPE/iSQoE), interocular-difference JOD psychophysics in an HMD (Dichoptic Foveation, SIGGRAPH 2026), DIBR temporal-flicker metrics (2018-2021) and motion-aware IV-PSNR (2025). A generic claim such as "first perceptual metric for temporal consistency of synthesized views" or "first HMD perceptual study of 3D human video" is not defensible. The search found no work that does the following, which is the defensible core. (1) Threshold (JND) psychophysics on controlled, parametric generators of image-based / online-NVS inconsistency: temporal depth-noise amplitude and spectrum, K-set blend-weight switching (popping) along a head path, disocclusion boundary jitter, and interocular blend-weight or hallucination decorrelation. It is measured in a stereo HMD as a function of region (face, hands, body), eccentricity and head velocity. (2) A metric that explicitly decomposes error into a motion-compensated temporal channel pooled by a TCSF, a viewer-path/view-switch channel and a disparity-compensated binocular channel thresholded by fusion limits, with each channel calibrated to those thresholds and evaluated leave-one-method-out against TCC, STED, ColorVideoVDP, MEt3R and temporal IV-PSNR. (3) Using the metric to re-adjudicate a concrete null ablation (the base paper's TSDF guidance, PSNR 31.16 vs 31.17), and as a differentiable loss or compute-allocation signal in a live pipeline. Reviewers will expect the related work to cite Liang et al. 2024, LIVE-Meta avatar VQA, SCOPE/iSQoE, Dichoptic Foveation and the DIBR-flicker literature. The binocular channel must be positioned as extending dichoptic/stereo-QoE psychophysics to temporally varying, structured synthesis inconsistency, not as the first binocular study.
novelty.best_variant: Idea 2 ("Seeing Flicker in 3D Video") has the more defensible novelty, strengthened with Idea 1's pipeline-internal perturbation hooks. Idea 2's three-channel decomposition (motion-compensated temporal, view-path/K-set, binocular within fusion limits) is a concrete, testable modelling contribution that none of the found works makes. Its leave-one-method-out and leave-one-artifact-out validation and its use of the metric as a training loss give a benchmark plus method story that vision or graphics venues accept. Idea 1 adds two useful pieces. First, parametric artifact injection through the base pipeline's own depth, weights and masks, which allows clean threshold staircases. Second, region-specific (face, hands) and head-velocity factors that differentiate the work from Dichoptic Foveation and SCOPE. Idea 1's co-presence/Networked-Minds and light-field-display arms dilute the work and add risk, so they should be dropped or kept minimal. Idea 1's claim of the "first threshold-level characterization including interocular inconsistency" must be narrowed, because Dichoptic Foveation (SIGGRAPH 2026) already did HMD interocular-difference JOD psychophysics with an eccentricity model.

sharpened.title: Shimmer Between the Eyes: Threshold Psychophysics and a Three-Channel Visibility Model for Temporal, View-Coupled and Binocular Inconsistency in Online 3D Video
sharpened.one_liner: HMD threshold psychophysics on parametric, pipeline-injected inconsistencies of online image-based 3D video, showing that time-varying interocular inconsistency is the dominant and unmeasured failure mode. The results are distilled into a calibrated, differentiable metric that splits error into temporal, view-path and binocular channels and beats per-eye VDPs on real telepresence methods.
sharpened.core_claim: Claim A (psychophysics): in a stereo HMD, structured synthesis inconsistency that decorrelates between the eyes and changes over time (e.g., independent per-eye blend-weight or hallucination noise at 2-10 Hz) is detected at an amplitude at least 2x lower than (i) the same interocular difference held static and (ii) the same temporal perturbation applied identically to both eyes. Therefore per-eye (monocular) metrics systematically under-predict its visibility. Claim B (metric): a model with explicit motion-compensated temporal, view-path (K-set switch) and disparity-compensated binocular channels, calibrated only on the threshold data, predicts JOD ratings of 8+ real online NVS methods under leave-one-method-out. On the stereo-HMD condition it reaches SROCC at least 0.10 higher than the best existing metric (per-eye ColorVideoVDP / FovVideoVDP), and removing the binocular channel eliminates most of that gain. Both claims are falsified if the threshold ratio is under 1.5x or the leave-one-method-out gain is under 0.05.
sharpened.key_insight: The artifacts of online image-based 3D video are not generic video distortions. They are produced by a handful of internal pipeline variables (per-pixel depth, blend weights, K-set membership, disocclusion masks), and in a stereo HMD each eye's view is synthesised independently from those variables. That makes three things possible. First, the artifacts can be injected parametrically and exactly through the pipeline's own internal variables, so a clean reference exists for every stimulus, even along arbitrary head paths with no captured ground truth. Second, visibility can be modelled with known building blocks: TCSF/elaTCSF for temporal residuals after motion compensation, fusion limits and the known sensitivity to interocular temporal modulation (binocular luster or shimmer) for the binocular channel. Dichoptic-foveation data show that static interocular differences are well tolerated. Third, a per-eye metric is blind to the binocular interaction by construction. This interaction is exactly what telepresence renderers and per-eye generative fixers create when they compute two views independently.
sharpened.method: (1) STIMULUS ENGINE. Reimplement a base-style pipeline (pixel-sized opaque Gaussian forward splat, image-based TSDF with previous-frame depth feedback, small blend U-Net); the base paper has no public code. Also use off-the-shelf ENeRF and GPS-Gaussian(+). Add perturbation hooks: (a) depth noise with controlled amplitude (in mm and in arcmin of disparity) and temporal spectrum (1-15 Hz), in masked regions (face, hands, torso, background); (b) forced K-set switch events with controlled blend discontinuity; (c) disocclusion-mask boundary jitter; (d) per-eye decorrelation of blend weights or depth noise (correlation rho from 1 to 0), static or temporally modulated; (e) background-image flicker. Clean references are the unperturbed renders along the same scripted head path (6DoF traces recorded from people in 3D calls, sampled at 3 head-speed levels). Stimuli are pre-rendered offline as stereo 90 Hz video, so the pipeline does not need to run at HMD rate. (2) PSYCHOPHYSICS. Quest 3 (primary) plus a second HMD (Varjo, Vision Pro or Quest Pro) for transfer. Luminance-calibrated with a photometer, eye tracking logged where available. Experiment 1 measures thresholds: 2AFC with a QUEST+ staircase per generator x region (face/hands/body/background) x eccentricity (0/10/20 deg) x head speed (static/slow/fast) x ocular condition (both-eye identical / interocular static / interocular temporally modulated / monocular-only). Prune the factorial design with a pilot, aiming for about 16-20 participants x 1.5 h. Experiment 2 measures suprathreshold scaling: pairwise comparisons on outputs of real methods plus mixtures of injected artifacts, scaled to JOD with pwcmp/ASAP active sampling, about 20-24 participants. A monitor (2D, mono) condition on a subset lets us show how conclusions change between 2D and HMD viewing. (3) MODEL (JNI: just-noticeable inconsistency). Inputs: the test stereo video, the reference stereo video, the reference depth/disparity and the head path; a reduced-reference variant uses only rendered depth and flow. E_temp: residual after warping frame t-1 to t with reference scene flow and head motion, band-decomposed and pooled through an elaTCSF-style temporal CSF with eccentricity and luminance terms, weighted by gaze/eccentricity. E_view: residual energy time-locked to K-set change events and head angular velocity, i.e. view-coupled popping. E_bino: left image warped to right with reference disparity, interocular residual decomposed into a static part and a temporally modulated part, with a fusion-limit / Panum-area gate and a separate sensitivity for interocular temporal modulation. E_static: ColorVideoVDP on the cyclopean average. Region weights for face and hands are fitted rather than hand-set. Each channel is calibrated to Experiment 1 thresholds, then a pooling of fewer than 10 parameters is fitted to Experiment 2 JOD with nested cross-validation. Everything is in PyTorch and differentiable, with 1080p stereo running at under 1 s per frame on one GPU. (4) APPLICATIONS. (i) Re-adjudicate the base paper's null ablations (TSDF guidance, temporal filter, K) in JOD units under HMD head paths. (ii) Fine-tune the blend net on short DNA-Rendering clips with L = L_rgb + lambda * JNI_temp+bino, versus a warping-error loss and a TCC-style loss at equal PSNR. (iii) Test a cheap stereo-coherent rendering variant, where one blend-weight field is shared across the eyes via disparity reprojection, and the per-eye generative fixer case. Everything is confirmed with a second, independent user study, never by the metric alone.
sharpened.why_not_engineering: The primary deliverable is new perceptual knowledge. It consists of threshold functions for structured synthesis inconsistency, and a specific, falsifiable interaction: time-varying interocular inconsistency is far more visible than either its static or its monocular counterpart. No current NVS metric or dataset contains this. The metric is derived from the psychophysics with interpretable channels, not tuned as a black-box regressor. Its value is shown by changing conclusions: it can reverse or confirm published ablations that PSNR/TCC call null, and it can justify or refute per-eye versus stereo-coherent rendering designs. This is the kind of contribution perception tracks at SIGGRAPH/TOG and IEEE VR review as research.
sharpened.differentiation: Liang et al. (CGF 2024, Mantiuk group) and arXiv 2501.08072 are 2D-monitor MOS/JOD studies of offline NVS. They have no thresholds, no stereo, no controlled generators and no model. We add HMD stereo, head-path viewing, parametric generators and a calibrated model, and we use their protocols and metric benchmarks as baselines. LIVE-Meta avatar VQA (TIP 2024) is HMD MOS for compression of mesh avatars, not synthesis inconsistency, and has no binocular factor. We cite it as the closest telepresence QA and compare HoloQA-style learned VQA where possible. SCOPE/iSQoE (2412.21127) is learned stereo QoE on still images with no temporal dimension. We add time and view-path, and our binocular channel is interpretable and threshold-calibrated. Dichoptic Foveation (SIGGRAPH 2026) is HMD JOD psychophysics of static interocular frequency differences. We explicitly build on it: its finding that static interocular differences are tolerated is the null against which we test our temporal-modulation hypothesis. We make no claim to be the first binocular HMD study. DIBR flicker metrics (JVCIR 2018, TIP 2019) and IV-PSNR-YUVM (2025) are MOS-correlated engineering metrics for MVD codecs, with no HMD, no psychophysical calibration and no binocular-temporal term. They are included as baselines. ColorVideoVDP / elaTCSF are monocular building blocks that we extend, and per-eye ColorVideoVDP is the main baseline to beat. MEt3R and VoluMe's jitter metric are uncalibrated consistency proxies and are included as baselines.

ActorsHQ (160-camera 12MP human capture, public with license): dense-rig pseudo-GT, from a per-sequence offline 4DGS/3DGS fit on all cameras, used to render reference stereo along head paths; sparse subsets are the method inputs.
MVHumanNet++ (large multi-view human video): extra identities and motions for the loss fine-tuning experiment.
Neural 3D Video / DyNeRF (18-21 cameras, kitchen scenes): continuity with the base paper and re-adjudication of its ablation.
ENeRF-Outdoor: one non-human, larger-depth-range condition to test eccentricity and disparity-range effects.
Recorded 6DoF head-trajectory traces from ~10 people in mock 3D calls on Quest 3 (collected in-house; trivial to capture, and released with the dataset).
Optional small custom capture: 6-8 synchronized cameras plus a stereo camera pair at ~63 mm on a slider, giving true stereo ground truth for 10-20 short telepresence clips.

experiments.capture_notes: The core psychophysics does not need custom capture. Stimuli are injected on top of clean renders from public data (DNA-Rendering, ActorsHQ), so every stimulus has an exact reference, including stereo along arbitrary head paths. Real-method validation can use dense-rig pseudo-ground truth, but pseudo-GT from an offline 4DGS fit carries its own artifacts, and reviewers will question this. A small custom capture is therefore recommended but not blocking: 6-8 synced global-shutter cameras plus a true 63 mm stereo pair on a slider or at fixed poses, 10-20 clips of 10-30 s showing talking and gesturing. This gives genuine stereo references at interpupillary baseline. Head-trajectory traces must be recorded in-house on a Quest 3 (cheap). Human-subject work needs IRB/ethics approval (start in week 1) and photometric HMD calibration (a borrowed photometer or spectroradiometer).

review.first_two_week_test: Pilot of Claim A plus a baseline-blindness check. It needs no base-pipeline reimplementation. Days 1-4: take 3 DNA-Rendering (or ActorsHQ) sequences and render clean stereo 90 Hz clips along 2 recorded head paths with any available renderer, e.g. GPS-Gaussian from the released code, or a 3DGS fit on one frame and animated with simple rigid head-path motion. Inject 3 perturbation types directly in image/depth space using the rendered depth: (a) binocularly identical temporal depth-warp noise at 5 Hz; (b) static interocular warp difference; (c) interocular warp difference modulated at 5 Hz. Use 5-6 amplitudes each and face vs torso masks. Days 5-10: run a 2AFC method-of-constant-stimuli test in Quest 3 with 5-6 lab participants (under an existing exempt protocol, or with authors only if IRB is pending), about 45 min each, and fit psychometric functions. Days 8-12, in parallel: compute per-eye ColorVideoVDP, TCC, warping error and MEt3R on the same stimuli and check whether they predict detection probability across the three conditions at matched amplitude. PASS if the threshold for (c) is at least 2x lower than both (a) and (b) (non-overlapping bootstrap CIs across pooled observers), AND per-eye ColorVideoVDP gives (b) and (c) nearly equal predicted visibility or ranks them wrongly. Either outcome supports the binocular-temporal story and shows that the baselines are blind to it.
review.kill_criteria: Drop or downgrade the project if any of these holds. (1) In the pilot, interocular-temporally-modulated thresholds are within 1.5x of the static-interocular and binocular-identical conditions. The binocular channel is then just per-eye flicker and the key novelty disappears; fall back to a monitor-plus-HMD dataset paper at most. (2) Per-eye ColorVideoVDP plus a trivial L/R difference term reaches SROCC within 0.05 of the full model under leave-one-method-out on real-method JOD data (checked at about month 4 on the first 10-12 participants). (3) The artifacts of real online methods all sit far above threshold, so ranking is trivial and PSNR already orders them, or all sit below it, so nothing is visible. Either way the metric has no discriminative role in telepresence. (4) A Mantiuk-group or Meta paper appears with HMD stereo-temporal JOD data for NVS artifacts before month 4. In that case, re-scope to the view-path/K-set channel and the application results.

reviewer_objections.objection: This is ColorVideoVDP plus a few extra channels, and the binocular side was just done by Dichoptic Foveation (SIGGRAPH 2026) and SCOPE/iSQoE. What is new?
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Dichoptic Foveation measures static interocular frequency differences, and SCOPE measures still stereo images. Neither measures interocular differences that change over time and are structured by synthesis variables (blend weights, per-eye hallucination, disocclusion). Our headline result is the interaction that those works cannot see: temporal modulation lowers the interocular threshold by a factor we report. We use their static data as the null condition. The metric gain is shown quantitatively against per-eye ColorVideoVDP under leave-one-method-out, and channel ablations attribute the gain to the new binocular-temporal term.

reviewer_objections.objection: The injected artifacts are synthetic and may not reflect real renderer failures, so thresholds on them do not transfer.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Injection happens through the pipeline's own internal variables (depth, weights, K-set, masks), not through image-space noise. Amplitudes and temporal spectra are matched to statistics measured from real method outputs, i.e. depth-noise PSD and switch rates of ENeRF, GPS-Gaussian and the base pipeline. The model is calibrated only on thresholds and then tested zero-shot on JOD ratings of 8+ real methods, including a per-eye generative fixer, with leave-one-method-out. Transfer is therefore an explicitly tested claim, not an assumption.

reviewer_objections.objection: Small N, one headset, so the results will not generalize; perception studies at CV venues look underpowered.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We use ~16-20 observers for thresholds and ~20-24 for JOD, typical of SIGGRAPH/TOG perception papers, with bootstrap CIs and power computed from the pilot. There are two HMDs with cross-headset transfer tests and a monitor condition. All stimuli, raw responses, head paths and code are released, so others can extend the dataset. The primary venue is a perception-tolerant graphics or VR venue rather than CVPR.

reviewer_objections.objection: There is no ground-truth stereo for real-method validation along head paths, and pseudo-GT from dense rigs biases the metric toward methods resembling the pseudo-GT renderer.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: The threshold experiments need no GT, because the clean render is the exact reference. For real methods we (a) use dense-rig pseudo-GT only at views close to real cameras, and report agreement with true held-out cameras as a sanity check; (b) provide a reduced-reference variant driven by rendered depth and flow; and (c) include a small custom capture with a true IPD stereo pair. We also report whether method rankings differ between pseudo-GT and true-GT subsets.

reviewer_objections.objection: Using the metric as a loss is circular (Goodhart), and the application gains will be marginal.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Every application claim is judged by a second, independent user study with new observers and pairwise JOD, never by JNI itself, and against warping-error and TCC losses at matched PSNR. The stereo-coherent rendering application also gives a cost argument (one weight field for both eyes), so a null perceptual difference is still a useful result.

effort.months: 7-9 (2-week pilot; months 1-2 stimulus engine, base-style reimplementation and IRB; months 3-4 threshold study; months 5-6 JOD study and model fitting; months 7-8 applications and confirmation study; writing)
effort.people: 2: one PhD student on the rendering/stimulus engine and loss experiments, one on psychophysics and modelling. A collaborator with vision-science or psychophysics experience is strongly advised, e.g. for Panum/TCSF modelling and study design credibility.
effort.compute: 2-4 consumer or workstation GPUs (RTX 4090/A6000-class) for offline 4DGS pseudo-GT fits, stereo stimulus rendering and blend-net fine-tuning; under ~1,500 GPU-hours total. Hardware: Quest 3 plus access to a second HMD (Varjo, Vision Pro or Quest Pro), a photometer, and optionally a 6-8 camera rig plus a stereo pair (~$5-15k) for custom capture. Participant payments for ~40-50 people.

review.venue: SIGGRAPH Asia 2027 (ACM TOG, deadline ~May 2027), which fits the timeline best. Alternatives: IEEE VR 2028 journal track (TVCG), or ACM TAP / SAP for a psychophysics-heavy version. CVPR/ICCV only if the loss and application results are strong and the dataset is large; otherwise vision reviewers will call it underpowered.
review.synergies: (1) Stereo-coherent and multi-viewer rendering: the binocular channel directly justifies, and measures, sharing blend weights or TSDF state across eyes and viewers. That both removes rivalry and cuts the base pipeline's 2x-per-viewer cost. It is a natural companion method paper. (2) Learned temporal memory to replace the TSDF/colour-mask heuristic (ConvGRU/TTT state, Stereo Any Video front-ends): JNI serves as both the training loss and the evaluation, and would finally show whether geometry guidance matters perceptually. (3) Rate-distortion-flicker coding of RGB-D or Gaussian streams (Starline-style HEVC depth, DSGS, Tele360 wire formats): JNI provides the perceptual flicker term for bit allocation. (4) Online generative fixers (Difix/DiffusionHarmonizer/Restereo/SyncFix style): per-eye independent fixing is exactly the time-varying interocular inconsistency this work shows is highly visible, so the paper motivates and evaluates synchronized stereo fixers. (5) A long-horizon, head-tracked telepresence benchmark: the released head paths, stimuli and JOD data become its perceptual track. (6) Gaze-contingent or foveated compute allocation: the eccentricity-dependent thresholds decide where temporal filtering and blend-net capacity are needed. The natural series is this perception/metric paper, then a stereo-coherent temporal renderer trained with it, then perceptual rate control.

cited_work_check.note: Diffusion-based and offline. AnyViewBench targets extreme dynamic view synthesis with little input/target overlap. It has no latency budget and no multi-view RGB-D input. Characterisation is accurate.

cited_work_check.title: Amortized Anchor Refinement for Deployable Continuous-Time 4D Gaussian Reconstruction (Stage-Capture)
cited_work_check.note: Submitted 31 Aug 2026. The HTML full text says held-out evaluation is defined at the capture cameras and does not report what a headset shows when the viewer walks around. Free-viewpoint results are qualitative, in the appendix. Minor nuance: the held-out split is odd-indexed frames at the 32 capture cameras (temporal holdout), not held-out cameras. The gap claim holds.

cited_work_check.title: RIFTCast: A Template-Free End-to-End Multi-View Live Telepresence Framework and Benchmark (ACM MM 2025)
cited_work_check.note: Exists (ACM MM 2025, Zingsheim et al., Bonn). Code and a multi-view RGB+mask benchmark are at https://github.com/vc-bonn/RIFTCast. The README documents no moving-camera ground truth or latency-coupled protocol. The RGB-only claim is correct. I could not fully verify the claim that 'latency and quality are not coupled' from the paper text, but nothing indicates otherwise.

threats.title: Towards Streaming Perception (streaming accuracy metric)
threats.what_overlaps: This paper already has the deadline-aware scoring rule, the idea's second 'key insight'. At every time instant, the latest output the algorithm has delivered is scored against the ground truth of that instant, so latency and accuracy collapse into one number. It also argues for Pareto analysis and finds that slow, accurate methods lose. Follow-ups carry the same rule into 3D detection (LASP, https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19115, 2025) and event-based perception (STARE, Nature Communications 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12993040/).
threats.what_remains_different: It covers detection and segmentation only, never view synthesis. For novel-view video, a missed deadline creates two kinds of staleness: the scene is out of date, and the viewer's pose is out of date because the head has moved. Pose staleness can be partly offset by late depth-based reprojection, so the NVS version of the metric has real structure of its own. Still, the scoring rule must be presented as 'streaming accuracy for view synthesis', not as a new idea.

threats.title: MV2: Multi-View Multi-Vehicle Driving Dataset for Novel View Synthesis
threats.what_overlaps: A real dynamic-scene NVS benchmark whose ground truth comes from other moving, synchronized cameras (car, scooter, drone), built specifically to measure extrapolation rather than interpolation. It already states the general claim that existing benchmarks only measure interpolation, and it answers that claim with moving witness trajectories.
threats.what_remains_different: It uses outdoor driving scenes with SfM poses and offline, per-scene methods. There is no fixed calibrated RGB-D rig, no human telepresence content, no binocular pair, no replayed HMD trajectories, no latency protocol and no long takes.

threats.title: M3ISR: A Multi-Modal Multi-View Benchmark for 3D/4D Gaussian Splatting and Feedforward Compression
threats.what_overlaps: A 2026 multi-view dynamic benchmark with depth, masks and a dedicated streaming track that names end-to-end latency, update cost and bandwidth for free-viewpoint video. It covers the 'benchmark for streaming 4D FVV with latency' framing.
threats.what_remains_different: The data is synthetic: 25 scenes, 6 shared-centre 1080p views. Quality and speed are reported side by side rather than coupled through a deadline rule. It has no moving or binocular witness ground truth, no real sensor depth, no telepresence humans and no long takes.

threats.title: Monocular Dynamic View Synthesis: A Reality Check (DyCheck iPhone dataset)
threats.what_overlaps: The best-known precedent for evaluating dynamic NVS against ground truth that is not an interpolated rig view. Training uses a moving handheld camera and testing uses separate wide-baseline cameras. It also critiques benchmarks that inflate scores, similar in spirit to the 'rankings flip' hypothesis.
threats.what_remains_different: The input is monocular, not a fixed multi-view RGB-D rig. Test cameras are static, and the benchmark has no binocular pair, no latency and no long takes.

threats.title: ImViD / Realizing Immersive Volumetric Video: A Multimodal Framework for 6-DoF VR Engagement
threats.what_overlaps: A multi-view dynamic capture at 5K/60 fps with depth and audio, 1-5 minute sequences, designed for 6-DoF VR viewing with immersive user experiments. It removes 'minute-long, depth-equipped, VR-targeted multi-view captures' as a novelty axis.
threats.what_remains_different: Scene-oriented capture from a camera rig. Evaluation is at rig views and user studies, with no moving or binocular witness ground truth, no deadline-coupled scoring and no online-method protocol.

threats.title: ViVo: A Dataset for Volumetric Video Reconstruction and Compression
threats.what_overlaps: Real multi-view RGB-D human capture (14 synchronized Azure Kinect RGB+depth pairs, 30 fps, per-frame calibration) with transparent and reflective content, hair and multi-person scenes. It covers 'multi-view sensor-depth telepresence-like data with non-Lambertian content'.
threats.what_remains_different: Fixed cameras only. It targets reconstruction and compression and has no moving or binocular ground truth, latency protocol, perturbation splits or long-horizon drift metrics.

threats.title: StereoGenBench: A Synthetic Multi-Camera Benchmark for Stereo Generation under Controlled Baseline Regimes
threats.what_overlaps: Provides calibrated right-view ground truth at baselines from inter-pupillary to wide, with metric depth and per-frame poses, for binocular-consistency evaluation. It claims prior resources lack such paired binocular ground truth.
threats.what_remains_different: Synthetic Unreal scenes aimed at mono-to-stereo generation. There is no multi-view rig input, no real capture, no human telepresence content and no latency.

threats.title: Syn4D: A Multiview Synthetic 4D Dataset
threats.what_overlaps: A synthetic, human-centric multi-view 4D dataset with moving cameras, depth and 'any pixel to any time to any camera' ground truth. A reviewer could say synthetic data already gives moving and binocular ground truth for free.
threats.what_remains_different: It is synthetic and targets monocular 4D reconstruction and tracking. It has no real sensor noise, desync or lighting, no telepresence NVS protocol and no latency coupling.

threats.title: PackUV-2B (in PackUV)
threats.what_overlaps: Long takes (up to 30 min) from 50+ synchronized cameras, with substantial motion and disocclusion.
threats.what_remains_different: RGB volumetric-video coding data with no depth-sensor track, no moving or binocular witness and no online, deadline-aware protocol.

threats.title: Bringing Telepresence to Every Desk
threats.what_overlaps: A telepresence RGB-D capture that adds dedicated ground-truth cameras near the viewer's position, instead of only held-out input cameras, and scores video stability with JOD.
threats.what_remains_different: Its two ground-truth cameras are static. There is no head-trajectory replay, binocular pair, latency coupling or benchmark infrastructure.

threats.title: Movi-Cam evaluation set (in Physics-based Human Pose Estimation from a Single Moving RGB Camera)
threats.what_overlaps: Shows how to get per-frame ground-truth poses for a moving camera inside a 120-camera studio: a checkerboard on the moving camera is tracked by the static rig. This is an alternative to the robot-arm pose pipeline and weakens any 'moving witness pose registration is novel' claim.
threats.what_remains_different: It targets human pose estimation, not view synthesis, and its moving camera is the input, not the evaluation target.

novelty.best_variant: There is only one idea (TeleBench-4D). Within it, the component with the most defensible novelty is the real moving and binocular witness-camera ground truth replaying recorded HMD trajectories around a fixed RGB-D telepresence rig, together with the rank-flip study (rig-interpolation scores against moving-viewer and binocular scores). No surveyed work provides this for human telepresence. The deadline-aware score should be demoted to 'streaming accuracy for view synthesis', a clearly credited extension of Li et al. (ECCV 2020), made distinct by scoring pose and scene staleness separately and allowing late reprojection. Minute-long takes and perturbation splits are supporting features, not claims, because PackUV-2B, ImViD and Sync-NeRF-style desync already cover them. For a first CVPR-scale version: one arm-mounted binocular witness plus about 20 takes, the streaming-NVS score and the rank-flip analysis.

sharpened.title: What the Viewer Actually Sees: Streaming, Off-Rig and Binocular Evaluation of Online Multi-View RGB-D Telepresence Synthesis
sharpened.one_liner: A two-tier benchmark built around one finding. Tier 1 re-splits public dense-dome RGB-D captures, grouping test views by how far they sit outside the input rig. Tier 2 is a small custom capture whose genlocked witness cameras follow replayed HMD trajectories, including a 63 mm stereo pair. Methods are scored with a streaming-accuracy rule for view synthesis that penalises scene staleness and pose staleness separately and gives credit for late reprojection. The paper then shows that rankings from rig-interpolation benchmarks do not carry over to what a telepresence viewer sees.
sharpened.core_claim: Take at least 8 online or generalizable NVS methods and rank them by the usual held-out-rig-camera LPIPS/PSNR. That ranking correlates only weakly (Kendall tau at most 0.5) with the ranking on any of these axes: (a) views off the rig hull, (b) moving-viewer views from replayed head trajectories, (c) binocular disparity consistency, (d) streaming score at 33 or 66 ms deadlines. The streaming score also predicts pairwise HMD preference better than PSNR plus a separate runtime column (higher agreement in a 2AFC study with at least 20 participants). The claim is falsified if tau exceeds 0.8 on all four axes, or if the streaming score does not beat PSNR+runtime on preference agreement.
sharpened.key_insight: The errors that matter in telepresence happen off the rig, while the viewer moves, between the two eyes, and after a deadline is missed. All four can be measured against real pixels. Some need no new hardware: dense domes that already include RGB-D sensors can be re-split. The rest need one genlocked stereo witness on an arm or gimbal. For view synthesis, a missed deadline has a structure that detection metrics lack. The scene is stale, but the viewer's pose can be refreshed by depth-based late reprojection. Scoring the two separately rewards methods whose geometry supports timewarp, which a 'latest output vs current GT' detection rule cannot express.
sharpened.method: PROTOCOL (the main contribution; runs on any data). (1) Hull-stratified splits: each test camera gets a signed distance to the convex hull of the input cameras and an angle to its nearest input camera, and scores are reported per bin (interpolation, near-extrapolation at 0-30 cm, far-extrapolation beyond 30 cm). (2) Streaming NVS score. Each method runs in a timing harness on a reference GPU class (e.g. RTX 4090) with fixed I/O. At display time t with viewer pose P_t, the displayed image is built from the newest completed output, which used scene time s < t and render pose P_r. Mode A is the stale image as delivered. Mode B is that output reprojected to P_t with the method's own depth, if it exposes depth (a standard forward-warp plus hole-fill supplied by the harness). The score is the error against GT(t, P_t), averaged over time, at deadlines B = 33, 66 and 100 ms. It is also decomposed into a scene-staleness term (scored against GT(s, P_t)) and a pose-staleness term (scored against GT(s, P_r) vs GT(s, P_t) using the witness). Li et al.'s streaming accuracy is credited as the parent rule. (3) Binocular track: per-eye LPIPS; a disparity-consistency error (RAFT-Stereo or FoundationStereo disparity on the rendered pair compared with the same estimator on the GT pair); a left-right photometric warp error; MEt3R. (4) Temporal and perceptual: flow-warp error and ColorVideoVDP/FovVideoVDP JOD along the moving-viewer paths. (5) Long-horizon: drift slope of per-minute LPIPS over 5-10 minute takes. TIER 1 DATA (public): CMU Panoptic/Kinoptic (10 Kinect v2 RGB-D plus 31 HD and 480 VGA cameras; RGB-D inputs, with many held-out HD/VGA views inside and outside the input hull); DNA-Rendering and ActorsHQ as dense RGB-only domes using stereo-estimated depth; DyNeRF, ENeRF-Outdoor and D3DMV kept for continuity with the base paper. HMD trajectories (about 50 recorded Quest head paths, released) are mapped into dome coordinates. Each frame is scored at the nearest held-out camera within an angular tolerance, which gives a 'discrete moving viewer' with real GT. TIER 2 DATA (custom, small): 8-12 genlocked global-shutter RGB cameras plus 4 RGB-D sensors in a desk or booth telepresence layout, and one genlocked 63 mm stereo witness on a low-cost cobot (e.g. xArm or UR3 class) or a 2-axis motorised gimbal-slider replaying the recorded head paths, including 20-60 cm off the hull. Witness poses come from arm kinematics, then Movi-Cam-style marker tracking by the static rig, then refinement by background SfM, with a sub-pixel reprojection check. The arm is masked in the input views (it is also a realistic occluder). There are about 20 takes of 2-5 minutes: conversation, handover, glasses, phone screens, hair, fast gestures, plus 3 takes with hardware-trigger desync. BASELINES: point-splat from sensor depth; a Starline-style TSDF plus projective texturing; a reimplementation of the base paper (splat + gated temporal TSDF + U-Net blend, flagged as a reimplementation); ENeRF; IBRNet; GPS-Gaussian(+) and EVA-Gaussian where code exists; DepthSplat or MVSplat as feed-forward baselines; 3DGStream as per-frame optimisation; 4DGS as an offline upper bound. RUNTIME BUDGET: this is evaluation, not an online method, but the harness adds under 1 ms of overhead and the reprojection operator runs in under 3 ms at 1080p so that Mode B is realistic.
sharpened.why_not_engineering: The deliverable is a measured scientific claim, not a dataset dump: current NVS benchmarks systematically mis-rank methods for the telepresence use case. The paper names which axis causes the flip (extrapolation, binocular, or deadline) and why (for example, blend-weight networks overfit to the rig's interpolation geometry, and methods without depth cannot use late reprojection). It also introduces a principled extension of streaming accuracy to view synthesis, with a pose/scene staleness decomposition that has no counterpart in detection, and validates that extension against human preference. If the rank flip holds, it changes how the whole online-NVS subfield reports results. The capture rig is a means of falsifying the claim, not the contribution.
sharpened.differentiation: Towards Streaming Perception (ECCV 2020) and its 3D-detection and event successors defined 'score the latest output against current GT'. We credit that rule and extend it to NVS, where pose staleness can be compensated by reprojection and has to be scored separately. MV2 (ECCV 2026) has moving-camera GT but covers outdoor driving, SfM poses, offline methods, with no binocular pair, no RGB-D rig and no latency. Replay (ICCV 2023, arXiv 2307.12067) has static DSLRs plus head-worn GoPros of acted humans, but its NVS benchmark evaluates at static DSLRs (the moving cameras are inputs); it has no depth, no stereo pair, audio-based sync and no latency. DyCheck uses monocular input with static test cameras. M3ISR (2026) has a synthetic streaming track in which latency is reported next to quality but not coupled to it, and no witness GT. StereoGenBench and Syn4D provide synthetic binocular or moving GT but no real sensor noise and no telepresence rig. ViVo, PackUV-2B and ImViD provide real RGB-D or long multi-view takes at fixed cameras only. RIFTCast and Bringing Telepresence to Every Desk evaluate at static cameras. The defensible new pieces are: real off-rig moving plus binocular GT around a fixed RGB-D telepresence rig; the NVS-specific staleness decomposition with reprojection credit; and the rank-flip study with preference validation. Long takes, desync splits and moving-camera registration are credited as supporting features, not claims.
