experiments.capture_notes: Most of the claim (off-hull flip, streaming score, discrete moving viewer, depth-source effects) can be tested on public data, mainly CMU Panoptic/Kinoptic, which pairs real RGB-D inputs with hundreds of held-out cameras. Custom capture is needed only for three things: continuous moving-viewer temporal metrics, true 63 mm binocular GT, and long takes of telepresence content with controlled desync. The minimum viable rig is 8-12 genlocked global-shutter cameras, 4 RGB-D sensors (Femto/ZED class), one genlocked stereo witness (two global-shutter cameras on a 63 mm bar), and a low-cost cobot or a motorised slider plus pan-tilt, for roughly USD 15-40k. Witness pose uses arm kinematics, then marker tracking by the static rig (Movi-Cam style), then background SfM refinement, with a sub-pixel reprojection check. Mask the arm in the input views. Obtain IRB consent and release only consenting participants. If the lab cannot build the rig, publish the Tier-1 protocol plus the streaming score as a smaller 3DV/WACV/TVCG paper and partner with a capture lab for Tier 2.

review.first_two_week_test: Use CMU Panoptic/Kinoptic only; no capture. Days 1-3: choose 3-4 sequences with people talking or gesturing. Use the 10 Kinect RGB-D streams (or 8 HD cameras plus Kinect depth) as the input rig. Bin all remaining HD and VGA cameras by signed distance to the input hull into interpolation, near-extrapolation and far-extrapolation. Days 4-9: run 6 methods that have code or are trivial to build: sensor-depth point-splat, TSDF plus projective texturing, ENeRF, IBRNet, GPS-Gaussian, and DepthSplat or MVSplat. Measure each method's end-to-end latency on one GPU with the same I/O. Days 10-12: compute LPIPS/PSNR per bin. Compute emulated streaming scores at 33 and 66 ms: pick the output from the frame delivered in time, in Mode A (stale) and Mode B (reprojected with the method's depth to the current held-out camera, scored at a later frame with the witness pose set to a snapped head path). Compute pseudo-binocular consistency on the closest VGA camera pairs. Days 13-14: compute Kendall tau between the interpolation ranking and each other ranking, and bootstrap confidence intervals over sequences. Validation: tau at most 0.5 on at least one axis with a CI excluding 0.8, plus at least one qualitative flip explained by a mechanism (for example, an implicit method wins the interpolation bin but loses far-extrapolation or streaming Mode B to TSDF-based IBR).
review.kill_criteria: Kill or downgrade to a short workshop or TVCG protocol note if any of these holds. (1) On Tier-1 public data, with 6 or more methods, Kendall tau between the interpolation ranking and the extrapolation, streaming and binocular rankings all stay above 0.8 with CIs excluding 0.6: then there is no headline, and the benchmark is just another dataset. (2) Streaming Mode B (reprojection credit) changes no ranking relative to Mode A, which makes the NVS-specific extension of Li et al. vacuous. (3) In the pilot HMD 2AFC study (8-10 people, 4 methods), the streaming score agrees with preference no better than PSNR plus a runtime cut-off. (4) Before investing in Tier 2, a synthetic Syn4D-style replay reproduces the Tier-1 rankings exactly (tau above 0.9). Real capture would then add little, so publish the protocol on public and synthetic data only. (5) Witness pose accuracy cannot reach under 1 px mean reprojection error in the first capture week, which invalidates moving-viewer GT.

reviewer_objections.objection: The deadline scoring rule is just Streaming Perception (Li et al., ECCV 2020) applied to images; there is no new idea.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We credit it explicitly as the parent rule. What is new for NVS is that the displayed output has two staleness sources, scene time and viewer pose, and pose staleness can be partly removed by late depth reprojection, which is standard in HMDs. We score Mode A and Mode B and decompose the error. We show this changes rankings (methods with usable depth gain) and correlates with HMD preference better than PSNR plus runtime. None of this can be expressed in the detection formulation.

reviewer_objections.objection: This is a dataset paper by a small lab. Twenty takes and one witness arm are too small compared with PackUV-2B, MVHumanNet or DNA-Rendering.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Scale is not the claim. The contribution is the protocol plus the rank-flip finding, and most of it runs on existing large public datasets (Panoptic, DNA-Rendering, ActorsHQ) through hull-stratified re-splits. The custom tier supplies only what no public dataset has: continuous moving plus true-IPD binocular GT around an RGB-D telepresence rig. We show that the cheap public protocol predicts the expensive one, or show where it fails, so others can adopt it without building a rig.

reviewer_objections.objection: Synthetic data (Syn4D, StereoGenBench) gives moving and binocular GT for free, with perfect poses. Why capture?
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We run the synthetic replay as an ablation. Online RGB-D telepresence methods are dominated by sensor-depth noise, multipath on hair and specular items, sub-frame desync and rolling exposure, and none of these are faithfully simulated. We report whether the synthetic rankings match the real Tier-2 rankings. If they do, we say so and recommend synthetic data. The real capture is justified only by a measured mismatch.

reviewer_objections.objection: Rankings depend on the reference GPU, implementation quality and reimplementations (the base paper has no code), so the streaming score measures engineering effort, not algorithms.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: The harness fixes I/O and precision, and reports rankings on two GPU classes and a deadline sweep, showing where rankings are hardware-stable. All interpolation, extrapolation and binocular tracks are reported without latency too, so algorithmic and systems effects are separable. Reimplementations are flagged, and their interpolation numbers are checked against the published ones on DyNeRF before use. Speed is a first-class property in telepresence, and hiding it in a side table is the status quo we argue against.

reviewer_objections.objection: Moving-witness GT has its own errors: pose error, arm occlusion in the input views, and sync of the witness to the rig. Could these produce spurious flips?
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: The witness is genlocked to the rig. Poses are triple-checked (kinematics, then marker tracking by the static rig, then background SfM) and we release per-frame pose uncertainty. Metrics are masked to foreground regions where pose error keeps reprojection under 1 px. The arm is present in every method's inputs identically. We also report the ceiling of a GT-to-GT consistency check (static scene frames re-rendered from the witness poses) so readers can see the noise floor below which differences are not meaningful.

effort.months: 2-3 for the Tier-1 public protocol, streaming harness and rank-flip study (publishable alone as a smaller paper); 9-12 total including Tier-2 capture, HMD user study and public evaluation server
effort.people: 2 (one on protocol, harness and baselines; one on rig, witness calibration and capture), plus part-time help for the user study and IRB
effort.compute: 4-8 consumer or datacenter GPUs for running about 10 baselines over long sequences (few-hundred GPU-days total, mostly 4DGS/3DGStream upper bounds); 1 reference GPU reserved for timing; hardware about USD 15-40k for the Tier-2 rig, cobot or gimbal, stereo witness and RGB-D sensors, plus a Quest-class HMD for trajectory recording and the user study

review.venue: NeurIPS 2027 Datasets & Benchmarks, the most natural home, with the full two-tier version. Alternatively CVPR 2027 if the rank-flip finding is strong and backed by the user study. IEEE VR / TVCG (journal track) is a good fit if the HMD preference validation and the streaming-with-reprojection analysis are the focus. A Tier-1-only fallback suits 3DV 2027 or WACV.
review.synergies: It is the evaluation backbone for most other directions in the cluster set. (1) Late-reprojection and timewarp methods that reuse the base paper's consistent TSDF depth: Mode B of the streaming score directly rewards them, so a method paper plus this benchmark forms a natural series. (2) Stereo-consistent blending and joint-eye generative fixers (Restereo/SyncFix style) need the binocular track to show gains. (3) Online desync and calibration-drift robustness: the Tier-2 hardware-desync takes give controlled GT perturbations. (4) Long-horizon drift and recovery of temporal filters: the drift-slope metric on multi-minute takes. (5) Perceptual flicker metrics or JOD-calibrated temporal-consistency scores: the HMD 2AFC data doubles as training and validation data for a telepresence-specific quality metric. (6) Off-rig extrapolation methods (generative completion, learned priors): the hull-stratified split measures exactly this. Strategy: release the Tier-1 protocol early so the team's own method papers report on it, which builds adoption before the full benchmark paper.

cited_work_check.note: The abstract confirms an online single-step, temporally conditioned enhancer converted from a pretrained image diffusion model. Search snippets and the CVPR 2026 poster page confirm 212 ms/frame. It is driving-simulation focused and single-view. The ideators' characterisation is fair.

cited_work_check.title: ArtiFixer: Enhancing and Extending 3D Reconstruction with Auto-Regressive Diffusion Models
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: a bidirectional generator trained with an 'opacity mixing' strategy that stays faithful to observed content while extrapolating unseen areas, then distilled into a causal autoregressive model that generates hundreds of frames in one pass. Static per-scene 3D; not live or multi-camera. Note that the opacity-derived observed/unobserved gate is already here, so the gate by itself is not novel.

cited_work_check.title: SyncFix: Fixing 3D Reconstructions via Multi-View Synchronization
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: joint latent bridge matching that synchronises denoising across views, trained on pairs, generalises to N views. The abstract reports no runtime and it is not online, so the claim is accurate.

cited_work_check.title: HAD: Hallucination-Aware Diffusion Priors for 3D Reconstruction (cited as CVPR 2026)
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: pixel-wise hallucination score maps from a feed-forward NVS network, used to mask diffusion-augmented views during progressive per-scene reconstruction. Offline and static. The CVPR 2026 venue was not verified; the arXiv date is May 2026.

cited_work_check.title: View-Structured Conformal Prediction for 3D Gaussian Splatting
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed (posted 2026-09-09). It is closer than the ideator admits. VSCP already factorises the renderer's spatial shape from a transferable view-difficulty factor and calibrates a held-out quantile over views. That is essentially idea 3's 'per view-difficulty bucket' calibration. What remains different is online/adaptive recalibration from live rig cameras, dynamic scenes and a generative component.

cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: a bidirectional video diffusion teacher distilled into a causal autoregressive single-pass student. It has no geometry and no multi-view.

cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: real-time, representation-agnostic, multi-view-aware spatio-temporal transformer inpainting for calibrated multi-camera 3D streaming. This is the direct telepresence speed baseline.

threats.title: DreamStereo: Towards Real-Time Stereo Inpainting for HD Videos
threats.what_overlaps: It already shows the systems claim C04 leans on: one-step (1 NFE) diffusion inpainting of disoccluded regions only (Wan2.1-1.3B with LoRA and a distilled VAE). It prunes to about 25.6% of tokens using the disocclusion mask, so compute scales with hole area (10.7x speed-up). It preserves observed pixels by mask-based blending, is stereo-consistent and temporally consistent, and runs at 40 ms/frame on an A100 and 33 ms on a 4090 at 768x1280. This kills three planks: 'gated one-step diffusion fits a telepresence budget', 'compute scales with disocclusion area', and 'observed pixels are copied, not regenerated'.
threats.what_remains_different: Monocular video with estimated DepthCrafter depth, converted to one fixed right-eye view. It has no calibrated multi-camera rig, no TSDF, no free or off-rig viewpoint, no K-view reference conditioning, no geometry-warped noise, no multi-view provenance classes and no certification.

threats.title: DiffPBR: Point-Based Rendering via Spatial-Aware Residual Diffusion
threats.what_overlaps: Directly anticipates idea 2's 'surface-anchored noise'. It replaces i.i.d. noise with 3D-consistent noise splatted from the point cloud and constrained by scene geometry and visibility, to enforce view consistency under camera motion. It has a one-step variant at about 10 fps.
threats.what_remains_different: Static scene and per-scene re-rendering. No TSDF streaming, no dynamic-surface advection, no stereo-eye or multi-viewer sharing, no causal temporal state, and not under 50 ms.

threats.title: Geometry-Aware Score Distillation via 3D Consistent Noising and Gradient Consistency Modeling (GSD)
threats.what_overlaps: Builds 3D-consistent 2D noise maps that stay exactly standard Gaussian by 3D conditional upsampling of noised point clouds and discrete integration of projected noise. This is the 'area-preserving splat keeps noise i.i.d. Gaussian' machinery idea 2 proposes. MultiDiff (CVPR 2024) similarly warps reference noise into overlapping target views, and a Lacuna direction page lists further works (Flow Score Distillation, Consistent Flow Distillation, MAS, 4D-from-3D) that anchor noise in 3D.
threats.what_remains_different: Built for SDS text-to-3D optimisation, not streaming video, not causal and not a render fixer.

threats.title: Track the Noise, Move the World: 3D-Grounded Motion-Consistent Noise (UniCaMo)
threats.what_overlaps: Lifts diffusion noise into a shared 3D representation: noise is warped along 3D point tracks and a spherical noise field is sampled per viewpoint. This gives noise consistent across camera motion and time, a 3D generalisation of Go-with-the-Flow. CameraNoise (arXiv 2605.30774) likewise warps noise with a geometry-guided reprojection flow.
threats.what_remains_different: Single-video controllable generation, multi-step, with no stereo pair, no metric TSDF surface and no real-time fixer.

threats.title: ArtiFixer: Enhancing and Extending 3D Reconstruction with Auto-Regressive Diffusion Models
threats.what_overlaps: Combines an observed-versus-unobserved generation gate (opacity mixing) with causal autoregressive distillation of a fixer. That is the gate-plus-causal-student recipe in all three ideas.
threats.what_remains_different: Offline trajectories over static per-scene 3DGS. No live rig, no dynamic humans, no TSDF signals, no stereo, no latency budget.

threats.title: DiffusionHarmonizer: Bridging Neural Reconstruction and Photorealistic Simulation with Online Diffusion Enhancer
threats.what_overlaps: An online, single-step, temporally conditioned fixer for neural renders: previous outputs are fed back and temporal consistency is trained in.
threats.what_remains_different: Single view, flow-based alignment (no geometry), 212 ms, no gate, no stereo, no certification.

threats.title: GenRec: Knowing Where to Reconstruct and Where to Generate
threats.what_overlaps: Builds a per-pixel observed/unobserved split from source cameras and depth into the architecture, the loss and the gradient flow. It restores observed pixels faithfully and lets the prior generate only in disocclusions. This is conceptually the provenance and authenticity gate, including the argument that one uniform loss conflates fidelity and hallucination.
threats.what_remains_different: Static sparse-view NVS with monocular-depth masks. Offline, no video, no stereo, no online calibration, no three-class provenance.

threats.title: View-Structured Conformal Prediction for 3D Gaussian Splatting
threats.what_overlaps: Conformal RGB bounds for novel views, using held-out views as calibration and a transferable view-difficulty factor. Idea 3's calibration per view-difficulty bucket is essentially this.
threats.what_remains_different: Static per-scene 3DGS without a generative component. Split conformal, not online or adaptive. No calibration by provenance class, no dynamic stream, and no use of a rig's idle cameras as a live calibration feed.

threats.title: InstantViR: Real-Time Video Inverse Problem Solver with Distilled Diffusion Prior
threats.what_overlaps: A causal, single-pass student distilled from a video diffusion teacher for streaming restoration, explicitly motivated by telepresence and AR/VR latency. FlashVSR, StreamDiffusionV2 and RealCam (Self-Forcing plus DMD, streaming NVS) show the same distillation recipe is mature.
threats.what_remains_different: No geometry conditioning, no multi-view or stereo, no gate.

threats.title: HAD: Hallucination-Aware Diffusion Priors for 3D Reconstruction
threats.what_overlaps: Pixel-wise hallucination scores that mask diffusion output that is inconsistent with the input views.
threats.what_remains_different: Offline and per-scene. Used as a training mask, not a live gate, and gives no guarantees.

threats.title: Transformer-Based Inpainting for Real-Time 3D Streaming in Sparse Multi-Camera Setups
threats.what_overlaps: Real-time, multi-view-aware, spatio-temporal hole inpainting as a post-process for calibrated multi-camera telepresence. It is the same slot in the pipeline.
threats.what_remains_different: Non-generative (it explicitly avoids diffusion). No stereo, no uncertainty or provenance.

threats.title: Restereo / StereoCrafter / Eye2Eye (stereo video diffusion)
threats.what_overlaps: Stereo-consistent generation from a warped view plus a disocclusion mask, and joint left/right restoration.
threats.what_remains_different: Offline and monocular source. No calibrated multi-view rig and no metric TSDF.

threats.title: LiveStre4m: Feed-Forward Live Streaming of Novel Views from Unposed Multi-View Video
threats.what_overlaps: A live multi-view novel-view-synthesis stream that uses a diffusion transformer online.
threats.what_remains_different: The diffusion transformer is used only for temporal interpolation. No gated disocclusion completion, no stereo, no authenticity.

novelty.remaining_novel_angle:
Almost every building block is already published separately:
- Gated one-step diffusion that runs only on disoccluded tokens, preserves observed pixels, is stereo-consistent and runs at 33-40 ms: DreamStereo.
- 3D-anchored or visibility-splatted noise: DiffPBR (ICLR 2026), GSD, MultiDiff, UniCaMo, CameraNoise.
- Observed-versus-generated gating: ArtiFixer's opacity mixing and GenRec.
- Causal one-step streaming fixers: DiffusionHarmonizer and InstantViR, which already cites telepresence.
- Conformal bounds for novel-view synthesis with a view-difficulty factor: VSCP.

What survives:

(1) Online, rig-self-calibrating certification. The N−K idle cameras of a fixed calibrated rig serve as a free, continuous calibration stream. Adaptive conformal inference, stratified by TSDF-derived provenance class (observed / interpolated / generated), gives per-pixel error bounds for a generative 3D-video stream in real time. No searched work does online or adaptive conformal calibration for streaming novel-view synthesis, or stratifies coverage by geometric provenance. VSCP is static, split-conformal and has no generative part.

(2) Using one metric object, the image-based TSDF of a calibrated rig, as the single operator for three things at once: the provenance oracle, reprojection of the previous output, and noise and latent correspondence across time and across the two HMD eyes. This is for a free-viewpoint target inside a live multi-view RGB-D IBR loop. DreamStereo uses monocular estimated depth and a fixed right-eye view; DiffPBR is static and per-scene.

(3) A benchmark and evaluation contribution: hallucination rate on observed pixels, empirical versus nominal coverage, stereo disparity consistency and off-rig extrapolation splits, plus an HMD trust study with injected fabricated gestures.

Surface-anchored noise on its own is not defensible as a headline contribution. It is a straightforward port of DiffPBR/GSD-style 3D-consistent noise to a TSDF, and strongly conditioned one-step fixers may be largely insensitive to noise. The system-level 'first gated causal one-step fixer in an online calibrated multi-view pipeline' claim is technically unclaimed but reads as incremental next to DreamStereo plus DiffusionHarmonizer. It needs hard latency numbers and clear authenticity and certification results to carry a CVPR paper.
novelty.best_variant:
Idea 3 (TRUST-Splat), using idea 1's gate signals and authenticity metric.

Idea 3 is strongest because its distinctive element, online adaptive conformal certification that uses the fixed rig's held-out cameras as free, continuous ground truth and is stratified by TSDF provenance class, has no match in the searched literature. The closest works fall short: VSCP (2609.10307) is static, split-conformal and non-generative, and HAD (2605.16873) is offline with no guarantees. This element also exploits a structural property unique to the base paper's fixed calibrated rig, which monocular or unposed systems (DreamStereo, LiveStre4m, VoluMe) cannot copy. Framing it as trustworthy generative telepresence gives a clean story that reviewers cannot reduce to 'Difix plus a mask'.

The other two ideas are weaker:
- Idea 2's surface-anchored noise is the most exposed. DiffPBR already splats geometry- and visibility-constrained 3D noise and has a one-step variant, while GSD, UniCaMo and CameraNoise cover the Gaussianity-preserving and 3D-lifting machinery. It should be kept only as an ablation (TSDF-warped vs flow-warped vs i.i.d. noise).
- Idea 1's claims that sparse gated compute fits the budget and that observed pixels are preserved are already demonstrated by DreamStereo (2604.12270) for stereo inpainting. They must be positioned as engineering, with DreamStereo cited and ideally used as a baseline adapted to the rig.

Recommended package:
- The TSDF-provenance gate from ideas 1 and 3 (hard composition, with a clamped residual in interpolated pixels).
- A TSDF-reprojected causal one-step student, with stereo handled by joint denoising.
- Online ACI certification from the rig's idle cameras.
- A hallucination-on-observed and coverage benchmark with off-rig splits.
- An HMD trust study.

Before submission, re-check with arXiv and Semantic Scholar: both APIs returned HTTP 429 for most of this session, and the web-search budget was exhausted before the searches on joint stereo denoising and multi-viewer shared noise.

sharpened.title: TRUST-Rig: Provenance-Certified Generative Completion for Live Multi-View 3D Video, Calibrated Online by the Rig's Own Idle Cameras
sharpened.one_liner: A fixed calibrated rig always has cameras that the current view isn't using, and those cameras give free ground truth. We use them to give a live generative 3D-video stream per-pixel error bounds that stay valid, split by whether each pixel was observed, interpolated or generated. The diffusion completer only fills what no camera saw, and the bounds certify that the observed pixels were not altered.
sharpened.core_claim: The claim holds at a nominal level of 90% under three conditions. The data are dense public multi-view dynamic datasets (DNA-Rendering, MVHumanNet, Panoptic, DyNeRF, ENeRF-Outdoor). The sequences are 300-1800 frames long. Calibration uses only the rig's idle cameras, with a camera-dropout difficulty ladder. Under those conditions, provenance-stratified adaptive conformal inference (ACI) reaches three results. (a) Long-run empirical coverage of per-pixel or patch error is within ±3 points of nominal for every provenance class. This holds on held-out on-rig targets and on an off-hull split where the outermost cameras are withheld from both inputs and calibration. (b) Bounds on OBSERVED-class pixels are at least 2x tighter at equal coverage than an unstratified, view-difficulty-only split-conformal baseline (VSCP-style). (c) A gated one-step generator is added. It cuts LPIPS in never-observed regions by at least 15% compared with the base paper's I_BG U-Net. Its certified hallucination rate on OBSERVED pixels is at most 0.5%. It adds at most 25 ms at about 1K on one RTX 4090. The claim is false if coverage breaks on the off-hull split, or if stratifying by provenance gives no tightening over a scalar difficulty covariate.
sharpened.key_insight:
A fixed, calibrated, synchronised rig differs structurally from monocular, unposed or static per-scene settings in three ways, and each one is exploitable.

(1) Free, continuous ground truth. For any target, the N−K cameras that are not selected are real images of the same instant. They form a live stream of labelled calibration points, so conformal calibration can be online and adaptive (ACI, Gibbs & Candès 2021) instead of a one-off split.

(2) Harder calibration points on demand. Dropping the nearest cameras before rendering a held-out camera creates calibration samples of controllable difficulty. This difficulty ladder spans the off-hull regime that on-rig held-out cameras never reach, and it enables covariate-shift-weighted conformal prediction on a difficulty feature.

(3) A metric provenance oracle. The image-based TSDF plus a visibility test in all N cameras classifies every output pixel as OBSERVED (seen by at least 2 of the K selected cameras, photometrically consistent), INTERPOLATED (weakly or singly seen, or seen but inconsistent), or GENERATED (seen by none). This splits the error distribution into regimes with very different spreads. Conformal quantiles stratified by provenance class are therefore much tighter where authenticity matters, and wide exactly where content was invented.

The generator is a vehicle for these certificates, not the claim.
sharpened.method:
BASE. Reimplement the base paper: per-view pixel-sized opaque Gaussians, forward splatting, a colour-gated temporal depth filter, an image-based TSDF with previous-depth feedback, and the blend U-Net. Depth comes from a learned stereo or MVS network on public data, because most datasets lack sensor depth.

(1) PROVENANCE MAP P.
- For each target pixel, take the TSDF ray hit x.
- Run a visibility test of x against the depth maps of the K selected cameras and of all N cameras (tolerance on relative depth).
- Classes: O = visible in at least 2 of the K cameras, colour variance below τ_c. I = visible in exactly 1, or low TSDF weight, or high blend entropy. G = visible in none of the K. An optional sub-class G_rig covers pixels visible in some unselected rig camera. Those pixels are fetched by adding that camera, not generated (retrieve-before-generate).
- Cost: about 2-4 ms, reusing the TSDF raymarch.

(2) GATED GENERATOR (deliberately modest).
- A one-step latent fixer initialised from public Difix3D+ / SD-Turbo weights, with a tiny VAE, fine-tuned on leave-camera-out renders from DNA-Rendering, MVHumanNet and N3DV training splits.
- Inputs: the IBR output, the P map, TSDF depth, and the previous output reprojected by TSDF depth (instead of optical flow), with an occlusion test.
- Composition: I = IBR on O; IBR + clamp(Δ, ±ε) on I; generator output on G. Hard composition means the generator cannot overwrite observations by construction.
- Tile-sparse execution: only tiles containing I or G pixels go through the backbone.
- Stereo: both eyes are run as one batch with cross-eye attention.
- TSDF-warped noise versus i.i.d. noise is an ablation only, not a contribution.
- Losses: L1 + LPIPS on O and I; a DMD or adversarial term on G only; a TSDF-reprojection temporal loss; a left/right disparity-warp loss.
- No Self-Forcing teacher. Short 8-frame on-policy rollouts are enough for exposure bias.

(3) ONLINE CERTIFICATION.
- Every frame, render 1-2 idle rig cameras at quarter resolution, rotating through all cameras. Each is rendered with the same K-selection policy, applied as if it were the target.
- On each, compute a normalised nonconformity score s = e / σ̂. Here e is an 8x8 patch L1 error (or patch LPIPS) and σ̂ comes from a tiny heteroscedastic head predicting local difficulty from P, TSDF weight, blend entropy and view angle.
- Maintain one ACI quantile q_{c,b,t} per provenance class c and difficulty bucket b. Buckets are defined by angular and baseline distance to the nearest input camera.
- Difficulty ladder: with probability p, drop the nearest 1-3 input cameras before rendering a calibration camera, to populate the high-difficulty buckets that off-hull targets fall into. Weight these samples by the density ratio of the difficulty feature (weighted conformal).
- Authenticity guarantee: use conformal risk control on the fraction of O pixels whose error exceeds τ, giving a per-frame certified hallucination-rate bound.
- Output: a per-pixel upper error bound σ̂·q, plus an optional low-salience provenance overlay in the HMD.
- Runtime: calibration renders run asynchronously, off the critical path (+8-15 ms of GPU time, amortisable on a second GPU).

BUDGET TARGETS (4090, about 1K): IBR 40-80 ms as in the base paper; provenance 3 ms; generator at most 25 ms on sparse tiles; certification off the critical path.
sharpened.why_not_engineering:
The contribution is a new statistical capability for a new setting, not a speed-up. The paper will contain:
- A formal online coverage statement (the long-run ACI guarantee under arbitrary shift) for a live generative 3D-video stream.
- Two new calibration mechanisms that only exist on a fixed calibrated rig: the idle-camera feed and the camera-dropout difficulty ladder, which yields calibration data for off-hull extrapolation.
- A geometric stratification (TSDF provenance) shown empirically to be the right conditioning variable.
- A certified authenticity metric (the hallucination rate on observed pixels, with risk control).

Each can be falsified by coverage-versus-nominal plots and width comparisons against the strongest non-generative conformal baseline (VSCP). The certification layer is renderer-agnostic, and it is shown on two generators: the base I_BG U-Net and the gated diffusion fixer. That rules out 'this is just Difix plus a mask'. An HMD trust study with injected fabricated gestures tests whether the certificates matter to humans, which is a question no fixer paper asks.
sharpened.differentiation:
- VSCP (arXiv 2609.10307): static per-scene 3DGS, split conformal, a view-difficulty factor, no generative part. Ours is online and adaptive, uses a live idle-camera calibration feed, stratifies by provenance class, adds the dropout ladder for off-hull coverage, and handles dynamic scenes with a generator. VSCP-style split CP is included as a baseline.
- Conformal image-to-image and diffusion UQ (Angelopoulos et al. 2202.05265; Conffusion 2211.09795; K-RCPS 2302.03791): single images, offline calibration sets, no geometry. We borrow their risk-control machinery and add geometric provenance and online rig calibration.
- HAD (2605.16873) and Hallucination Score (2507.14367): heuristic hallucination scores with no coverage guarantee, offline.
- GenRec (2608.17832) and ArtiFixer (2603.00492): an observed/unobserved gate in static offline NVS. We cite them as prior art for gating and claim nothing about the gate itself.
- DreamStereo (2604.12270): one-step, mask-pruned, observed-preserving stereo inpainting at 33-40 ms from monocular estimated depth. We concede the sparse gated one-step speed claim and use a rig-adapted DreamStereo-style fixer as a baseline or drop-in generator.
- DiffusionHarmonizer (2602.24096) and InstantViR (2511.14208): causal one-step fixers, single view, no geometry, no uncertainty. We replace flow alignment with TSDF reprojection but do not claim it as a headline.
- DiffPBR (ICLR 2026), GSD (2406.16695), UniCaMo (2607.02798), Go-with-the-Flow (2501.08331): 3D-anchored noise. We treat TSDF-warped noise only as an ablation.
- Bonn real-time inpainting transformer (2603.05507): the same pipeline slot, non-generative, no uncertainty. It is both the speed baseline and a second generator we certify.

datasets: DNA-Rendering: 60 cameras, humans with clothing and objects; the main dense rig for the difficulty ladder and off-hull split (public on request)
MVHumanNet / MVHumanNet++: 48 cameras, many subjects; training data for the generator plus a second evaluation rig
CMU Panoptic Studio HD: 31 HD cameras plus 480 VGA cameras; very dense coverage makes true off-hull ground truth possible; multi-person, long sequences
ActorsHQ: 160 cameras at 12 MP; a high-resolution face and hand authenticity test (license on request)
DyNeRF / Neural 3D Video: 18-21 cameras; base-paper protocol, extended to all 300 frames and to a no-kitchen training split
ENeRF-Outdoor: 18 cameras, outdoor dynamic humans; base-paper protocol
Technicolor light field: 4x4 rig; a sparse-rig stress test where the idle-camera pool is small
Optional small custom rig (6-8 synced RGB-D or stereo cameras): only for the live end-to-end latency and HMD trust study, not for the main quantitative claims
baselines: The base paper (Ha et al. 2025), reimplemented, with its I_BG U-Net and no uncertainty
Base + per-frame Difix3D+ (ungated), and base + Difix3D+ with a hard provenance gate (the 'Difix + mask' strawman)
A DreamStereo-style one-step mask-pruned inpainter adapted to rig depth (2604.12270)
A DiffusionHarmonizer-style flow-aligned temporal one-step fixer (2602.24096), reimplemented if code is unavailable
The Bonn real-time multi-view inpainting transformer (2603.05507)
GPS-Gaussian+ / ENeRF as generalisable real-time NVS references

Uncertainty baselines on the same renders: VSCP-style split conformal with a view-difficulty factor (2609.10307); unstratified ACI; K-RCPS-style risk control calibrated offline (2302.03791); HAD-style heuristic hallucination score thresholded (2605.16873); deep-ensemble or MC-dropout variance of the blend net
metrics: Empirical coverage minus nominal, per provenance class and difficulty bucket, as a running window over time on the on-rig, off-hull and camera-failure splits
Mean bound width, or tightness ratio against VSCP-style split CP at equal coverage
Certified and empirical hallucination rate: the fraction of O/I pixels whose error exceeds τ, with the conformal risk-control bound
Fidelity split by provenance class: PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS on O and I; LPIPS, FID and FVD on G
Face and hand identity in the authenticity split: ArcFace similarity and hand-keypoint error, compared between the generated and observed versions
Temporal: tOF / flow-warp error, TSDF-reprojection error, flicker (STED) on moving-camera plus dynamic-scene trajectories
Stereo: left/right disparity-warp error, and MEt3R for multi-view consistency
Latency: mean and p99 time per stage, calibration overhead, end-to-end motion-to-photon time on the custom rig
HMD user study (n of about 24): realism, trust calibration (detecting injected fabricated gestures with and without the provenance overlay), binocular comfort
key_ablations: Stratification: none, difficulty only (VSCP-like), provenance only, provenance x difficulty
Calibration: static split, ACI, ACI + camera-dropout ladder, ACI + ladder + density-ratio weighting (the decisive ablation for off-hull coverage)
Nonconformity: raw L1, patch L1, normalised by learned σ̂, patch LPIPS
Provenance oracle: TSDF visibility vs opacity-only (ArtiFixer-style) vs learned mask (GenRec-style); includes the rate of the dangerous misclassification of G as O caused by depth errors
Composition: soft gate vs hard gate vs hard gate with clamped residual on I, trading authenticity against quality
Generator conditioning: flow-warped vs TSDF-reprojected previous output; i.i.d. vs TSDF-warped noise; stereo cross-attention on or off
Retrieve-before-generate: generating G_rig pixels vs fetching the extra rig camera
Calibration budget: 0.5, 1 or 2 idle cameras per frame at 1/4 or 1/8 resolution, against coverage lag after a distribution shift (lighting change, a new person entering)
experiments.capture_notes:
All core claims (coverage, tightness, hallucination rate, generator quality, off-hull split) can be tested on public dense rigs. DNA-Rendering, Panoptic, ActorsHQ and MVHumanNet have 31-160 cameras, which leaves enough idle cameras for calibration and for an honest off-hull hold-out.

Caveats:
- Most public rigs lack synchronised sensor depth. Depth must come from learned stereo or MVS, and depth errors feed into provenance errors, which is a measured ablation.
- DNA-Rendering and ActorsHQ need license agreements; request them in week 1.

A small custom rig (6-8 cameras, for example ZED or RealSense units or synced machine-vision stereo pairs) is only needed for the live latency and HMD trust study. It could be replaced by replaying Panoptic sequences into the HMD if hardware is unavailable, at the cost of losing true motion-to-photon measurements.

review.first_two_week_test:
No diffusion training.

Days 1-4: build a lightweight proxy of the base renderer:
- MVS or learned-stereo depth, forward-warp IBR from the K=4 nearest cameras, and an image-based TSDF raymarch for the provenance map (O/I/G).
- Data: DyNeRF (public now) and CMU Panoptic HD (public now; about 300 frames each). Add DNA-Rendering if the license arrives.

Days 5-8: run the uncertainty analysis.
- Stream the idle-camera renders, compute patch-L1 nonconformity scores, and run four calibrators: (i) VSCP-style split CP on a difficulty factor; (ii) unstratified ACI; (iii) provenance x difficulty ACI; (iv) (iii) + camera-dropout ladder with density-ratio weights.
- Evaluate on two target sets: on-rig cameras never used for calibration, and an off-hull split (the outermost 20% of cameras, excluded from both inputs and calibration).

Days 9-12: plug in off-the-shelf Difix3D+ (public weights) with a hard provenance gate as the generator.
- Recompute coverage and the empirical hallucination rate on O pixels.
- Measure how much the O-class error distribution shifts between the gated and ungated fixer.

Days 13-14: produce the go/no-go plots: coverage vs nominal per class and split, width ratio vs VSCP-style, and the rate of G pixels misclassified as O.

The result validates the core insight if all three hold:
- ladder-ACI coverage is within ±3 points of nominal on off-hull targets;
- O-class widths are at least 1.5-2x tighter than unstratified;
- the ungated fixer measurably violates the O-class bound while the gated one does not.
review.kill_criteria:
Drop or pivot if any of the following holds after the 2-week test or the first full evaluation.

(1) Off-hull coverage cannot be fixed. With the dropout ladder and weighting, coverage on the off-hull split is still more than 5 points below nominal at 90%. The certificate would then be invalid exactly where telepresence needs it.

(2) Provenance adds nothing. Provenance stratification tightens O-class bounds by less than 1.3x compared with a scalar view-difficulty covariate. VSCP would then already cover it and the novelty collapses.

(3) Bounds are too wide to use. Bounds on O pixels at 90% coverage are uninformative, for example a patch-L1 bound above 0.08 or wider than the error of the naive IBR itself.

(4) Depth errors break the oracle. G-to-O misclassification from depth errors exceeds about 2% of G pixels on human sequences, so the authenticity guarantee rests on a broken oracle.

(5) The certification has no reason to be online. ACI gives no coverage or width benefit over static split CP on 1000+ frame sequences that include shifts (a new person, a lighting change).

Separately, for the generator component: if gated Difix3D+ per frame is within 5% LPIPS on G regions of the trained TSDF-conditioned causal fixer, keep the paper certification-centric and present the generator as off-the-shelf.

Also re-run the arXiv and Semantic Scholar search for 'online / adaptive conformal' plus 'novel view synthesis / generative video' every month. If a live-rig or online conformal NVS paper appears, reposition toward the provenance and HMD trust study.

reviewer_objections.objection: The generator is just DreamStereo / Difix3D+ plus a mask. Gated one-step diffusion that preserves observed pixels and scales with hole area is already published (DreamStereo 2604.12270; ArtiFixer's and GenRec's observed/unobserved gating).
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Agreed, and we say so explicitly. We make no claim about the gate or the one-step speed. The contribution is certification. The certification layer is renderer-agnostic, and we show valid, tight, provenance-stratified coverage for three generators: the base I_BG U-Net, the Bonn transformer inpainter, and the gated one-step fixer. Gated Difix and a DreamStereo-style fixer are included as baselines and as drop-in generators.

reviewer_objections.objection: Conformal guarantees require exchangeability. Temporal video is not exchangeable, and on-rig calibration cameras are distributed differently from off-rig HMD viewpoints, so the 'guarantee' is hollow.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: ACI (Gibbs & Candès 2021) gives a long-run average-miscoverage guarantee under arbitrary distribution shift, with no exchangeability needed. That is the statement we claim, and we state it precisely as marginal coverage per class and difficulty bucket. For the on-rig to off-rig gap, the camera-dropout ladder creates calibration samples in the high-difficulty region, and density-ratio weighting on the difficulty feature adapts them. We report empirical coverage on a true off-hull split whose cameras never enter calibration. If it fails there, the paper says so. That is exactly our pre-registered kill criterion.

reviewer_objections.objection: VSCP (2609.10307) already does view-structured conformal prediction for Gaussian splatting with a transferable view-difficulty factor. This is an incremental online extension.
Per-pixel error bounds on generated regions are meaningless, since generation is not supposed to match ground truth. And do users even care about uncertainty overlays?
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Correct for G pixels. Their wide bounds are the signal that the content is invented, not a quality claim. The guarantee that matters is on O and I pixels: conformal risk control bounds the fraction of truly observed pixels the system altered beyond τ. That is an authenticity certificate no prior telepresence system offers. Whether it matters to people is tested directly in an HMD study (n of about 24) with injected fabricated gestures, measuring detection accuracy and trust calibration with and without the provenance overlay.

reviewer_objections.objection: The base pipeline assumes RGB-D or stereo input, but public dynamic datasets lack sensor depth. With estimated depth the provenance oracle is unreliable, and the latency budget excludes depth estimation.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We use learned stereo or MVS depth, the same regime as the base paper's non-RGB-D experiments. Oracle reliability is measured directly: the rate of G pixels misclassified as O, and how coverage degrades as depth noise is injected. Such misclassification is exactly what the O-class conformal bound catches, since errors from mislabelled pixels widen the O quantile instead of silently passing. Latency is reported end to end, including depth, on the optional small rig. Calibration renders run asynchronously and are reported separately.

effort.months: 8-10 in total. Months 0-1: renderer reimplementation plus the 2-week certification test. Months 2-5: gated one-step generator fine-tuning and stereo. Months 5-7: full evaluation plus off-hull benchmark. Months 7-9: optional small rig plus HMD study. The certification-only version is about 5 months.
effort.people: 2: one PhD student on rendering, generator and systems; one on conformal/statistics, evaluation and the user study. A part-time advisor with conformal-prediction expertise is strongly recommended.
effort.compute: 4-8 A100/H100-class GPUs for about 2-3 months, to fine-tune a Difix3D+/SD-Turbo-class one-step fixer on leave-camera-out renders. This deliberately avoids Self-Forcing distillation of a video teacher, which would need 32+ GPUs. The certification experiments need 1-2 GPUs, and live benchmarks one RTX 4090. The optional rig costs roughly USD 3-8k (6-8 stereo or RGB-D cameras plus sync).

review.venue: ICCV 2027 as the main target (about March 2027 deadline). CVPR 2027 (November 2026) is too soon for the full system. Alternative: SIGGRAPH Asia 2027 / TOG if the HMD trust study is strong. A follow-up focused on the trust study fits IEEE VR / TVCG 2028.
review.synergies:
1. Off-rig extrapolation and moving-viewpoint benchmark: the off-hull split, the difficulty ladder and the coverage metrics are a shared benchmark contribution across the paper series.

2. Active camera selection and rig design: per-bucket conformal widths directly score which K cameras to use for a target, or where to add a camera (next-best-camera for rig design).

3. Long-term background memory and retrieve-before-generate: the G_rig and memory provenance classes route pixels to real past or unselected observations before generation. This combines naturally with a persistent static-background cache.

4. Bandwidth-adaptive streaming and compression: the provenance and bound maps can drive bitrate allocation, spending bits where bounds are wide and sending generation seeds instead of pixels for G regions.

5. HMD stereo rendering and latency work: the same TSDF reprojection serves late-warp at 90 Hz, and certified bounds can modulate foveation.

6. Anti-deepfake and authenticity signalling: the certified hallucination rate plus a provenance overlay or watermark ties into signed-media and consent directions for generative telepresence.

7. Calibration-free and unposed rigs (Tele360, LiveStre4m line): an ablation or future work is whether idle-camera ACI still holds when poses are estimated.

References checked this session: VSCP https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10307; ACI https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.00170; Image-to-Image conformal https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.05265; Conffusion https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09795; K-RCPS https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.03791; Hallucination Score https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.14367; Go-with-the-Flow https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.08331. All other works are from the verified novelty report.

cited_work_check.title: Lyra: Generative 3D Scene Reconstruction via Video Diffusion Model Self-Distillation (ICLR 2026)
cited_work_check.note: Exists and is correctly described as self-distilling a video diffusion model into a feed-forward 3DGS decoder with no multi-view training data. However, the idea's risk section calls Lyra and FlashWorld 'both static or generation-oriented', and that is only half right: the Lyra abstract explicitly extends to dynamic 3D (4D) scene generation from a monocular video. It is generation-oriented but not static-only. Minor mischaracterisation.

cited_work_check.title: Self Forcing: Bridging the Train-Test Gap in Autoregressive Video Diffusion (NeurIPS 2025 spotlight)
cited_work_check.note: Trains on its own KV-cached rollouts with a holistic video-level loss and stochastic gradient truncation. Correctly characterised.

cited_work_check.title: FlashWorld: High-quality 3D Scene Generation within Seconds
cited_work_check.note: Cross-mode distribution-matching distillation from the MV-oriented mode to the 3D-oriented mode. Static scene generation. Correct.

cited_work_check.note: Spatio-temporal 4D human diffusion with sliding iterative denoising, evaluated on DNA-Rendering and ActorsHQ. It is offline (diffusion followed by 4DGS). A plausible teacher, as claimed.

cited_work_check.note: A single-step diffusion fixer whose cleaned pseudo-views are distilled back into a per-scene NeRF/3DGS. Correct.

threats.title: FreeGen: Feed-Forward Reconstruction-Generation Co-Training for Free-Viewpoint Driving Scene Synthesis
threats.what_overlaps: This is the closest match to the core recipe and the ideator missed it. It samples off-trajectory viewpoints (lateral shifts of ±3 m) that have no ground truth and renders them with a generalizable feed-forward 3DGS reconstructor. A frozen video diffusion model refines these renders into pseudo-labels, and the pseudo-labels supervise the feed-forward reconstruction network (auxiliary loss weight 0.1) alongside on-trajectory ground-truth losses. So 'training a generalizable renderer on off-rig views with no GT, using a video-diffusion prior, anchored by real-view GT' is already published.
threats.what_remains_different: FreeGen keeps a diffusion refinement branch at inference, so it is not zero-cost. It uses pseudo-label regression rather than DMD or distribution-level critics. The scenes are static driving scenes: dynamic actors are baked into static Gaussians and it has no recurrent state or on-policy feedback loop. It is not real-time (seconds), not calibrated RGB-D IBR, and not human telepresence.

threats.title: InstantViR: Real-Time Video Inverse Problem Solver with Distilled Diffusion Prior
threats.what_overlaps: Distills a bidirectional video diffusion teacher into a causal autoregressive single-pass student that runs at over 35 FPS. The distillation is prior-driven, needs no paired or clean data, and explicitly targets streaming, telepresence and AR/VR. This covers the claim that a video-diffusion prior can be distilled into a real-time causal network without GT, including streaming inpainting.
threats.what_remains_different: It solves 2D inverse problems with known degradation operators (inpainting, deblur, SR). There is no 3D, no novel viewpoints, no geometry-guided renderer, no multi-view rig and no TSDF feedback.

threats.title: Lyra: Generative 3D Scene Reconstruction via Video Diffusion Model Self-Distillation
threats.what_overlaps: Distills video diffusion into a feed-forward 3DGS decoder with no multi-view GT, and extends to dynamic 4D from monocular video. This covers 'distill a generative prior into a fast 3D-consistent network' in general.
threats.what_remains_different: The task is generation from a single image or video, not faithful reconstruction from a calibrated rig. There is no on-rig fidelity anchor, no recurrent geometric feedback, no real-time online streaming and no moving-viewer protocol.

threats.title: GeoStream: Toward Precise Camera Controlled Streaming Video Generation
threats.what_overlaps: Identifies geometry-induced exposure bias from a self-refreshing 3D cache: depth from its own outputs is unprojected and re-rendered. It fixes this with fully on-policy training that mirrors the inference-time feedback. That is conceptually the idea's claim of 'on-policy training through the recurrent TSDF/previous-depth feedback loop'.
threats.what_remains_different: The student is an AR video diffusion generator, not a deterministic geometry-guided IBR renderer fed real rig frames. It is not calibrated multi-view reconstruction and is not evaluated for fidelity at held-out cameras.

threats.title: MV-Forcing: Long Multi-View Video Generation via 4D-Grounded Spatio-Temporal Self-Forcing
threats.what_overlaps: DMD combined with spatio-temporal self-forcing, with a 4D reconstruction in the loop, for multi-view-consistent dynamic video. This combines Self Forcing with DMD and 4D geometry feedback.
threats.what_remains_different: The student is a few-step diffusion generator of multi-view videos. It is not a real-time deterministic renderer driven by captured rig frames and it is not telepresence.

threats.title: GIFSplat: Generative Prior-Guided Iterative Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting from Sparse Views
threats.what_overlaps: Distills a frozen Difix enhancer's corrections on novel renders into Gaussian-level cues of a feed-forward 3DGS model.
threats.what_remains_different: The enhancer is still used at inference, scenes are static only, and inference takes seconds.

threats.title: DriveX: Driving View Synthesis on Free-form Trajectories with Generative Prior
threats.what_overlaps: A video diffusion model restores renders along novel trajectories that have no GT, and these become supervision for 3DGS, giving real-time rendering on free-form trajectories. The same pattern appears in ReconDreamer, Difix3D+ and 4DGS-Fixer.
threats.what_remains_different: This is per-scene optimization, so it is neither a generalizable nor an online streaming renderer.

threats.title: Transformer-Based Inpainting for Real-Time 3D Streaming in Sparse Multi-Camera Setups
threats.what_overlaps: A real-time (41.6 FPS) spatio-temporal inpainting post-process for sparse multi-camera 3D streaming, trained on DNA-Rendering with L1 plus an adversarial loss. It competes for the disocclusion-at-zero-diffusion-cost claim.
threats.what_remains_different: It uses GT-supervised training at rig cameras, with no diffusion teacher, no off-rig trajectories and no on-policy feedback.

threats.title: Distilling Multi-view Diffusion Models into 3D Generators (DD3G)
threats.what_overlaps: Distills an MV-diffusion ODE trajectory into a feed-forward 3D Gaussian generator (0.06 s).
threats.what_remains_different: It targets object-level image-to-3D generation, not multi-view capture reconstruction and not dynamic scenes.
