novelty.remaining_novel_angle:
The general move is taken. FreeGen (ECCV 2026) already does it for static driving scenes: sample viewpoints off the capture trajectory, supervise a generalizable feed-forward renderer there with a frozen video-diffusion prior, and anchor it with GT on real views. InstantViR (CVPR 2026) already distills a bidirectional video diffusion model into a real-time causal student with no clean data. GeoStream and MV-Forcing already publish on-policy (self-forcing) training through a geometric feedback cache, with DMD.

What remains defensible is the intersection, which no paper I found claims:
(1) The student is a diffusion-free, real-time (40 ms or less), calibrated multi-view RGB-D geometry-guided IBR renderer for dynamic humans or scenes. Unlike FreeGen, GIFSplat and Leveling3D, no diffusion runs at test time.
(2) It is trained on its own unrolled rollouts through a physical recurrent geometry loop (TSDF with previous-frame depth feedback, learnable fusion hyperparameters). The rollouts follow off-rig moving-viewer head trajectories while the scene moves, which targets exposure-bias drift in a deterministic reconstruction loop rather than in a generator.
(3) Training uses a distribution-level critic (DMD, a video discriminator or a consistency reward) instead of pseudo-label regression, gated spatially by the pipeline's own confidence (TSDF weights) so the prior acts only where the rig is uninformative.
(4) A new moving-viewer, moving-scene evaluation protocol uses off-rig GT from dense domes (DNA-Rendering or MVHumanNet++ camera subsets) plus temporal and drift metrics.

Contribution (4) and the on-policy TSDF-feedback ablation are the most defensible. The DMD-into-renderer piece alone would be read as 'FreeGen/Lyra applied to telepresence'. The paper must cite FreeGen, InstantViR, GeoStream and MV-Forcing and show experimentally that DMD or critic training beats FreeGen-style pseudo-label regression, and that on-policy rollouts beat teacher-forced training.
novelty.best_variant:
The cluster has one idea, so the question is which sub-component to lead with. The strongest framing is not 'distill a video diffusion prior into a fast renderer', which FreeGen, Lyra, InstantViR and DriveX largely cover. It is 'on-policy, GT-free training of a deterministic online geometry-guided renderer through its own recurrent depth/TSDF feedback along off-rig moving-viewer trajectories, with a confidence-gated distribution-level critic, plus a moving-viewer benchmark with off-rig GT from dense domes'.

This framing leads with the parts that separate it from FreeGen: a recurrent feedback loop, a dynamic scene, zero inference cost, critic rather than pseudo-label, and the telepresence evaluation. It demotes the generic prior-distillation part to an enabling technique. The minimum required baselines are FreeGen-style pseudo-label distillation (train-time only) and a Difix/Fixer runtime refiner, which are the obvious reviewer asks.

sharpened.title: Train Where You Deploy: On-Policy, Confidence-Gated Critic Training of Online Geometry-Guided Renderers for Moving Telepresence Viewers
sharpened.one_liner: Train a real-time rig-based renderer on unrolled rollouts along moving, off-rig head trajectories, feeding its own previous depth back through the TSDF. A video critic that only acts where rig confidence is low supervises it where no ground truth exists. Measure it on a new moving-viewer benchmark with off-rig ground truth from dense capture domes.
sharpened.core_claim:
The setup is a 4-camera frontal rig subset of dense-dome human captures (DNA-Rendering, ActorsHQ). The student is trained only on rig-camera data, plus off-rig rollouts supervised by a confidence-gated video critic. Three things must hold, at unchanged runtime (40 ms or less) and with at most 0.2 dB PSNR loss at on-rig held-out cameras:
(a) It recovers at least 50% of the off-rig LPIPS/FVD gap between the base single-instant training recipe and an oracle trained with direct dome ground truth at those off-rig cameras.
(b) It beats FreeGen-style pseudo-label regression from the same frozen diffusion prior on off-rig LPIPS and temporal metrics (tLPIPS, TCC).
(c) On-policy unrolled training through the previous-depth/TSDF feedback reduces long-horizon drift by at least 30% compared with teacher-forced training. Drift is measured as the PSNR/tLPIPS decay slope over 1-minute moving-viewer sequences.
If (a) or (c) fails, the paper's thesis fails.
sharpened.key_insight:
Online geometry-guided renderers have a train/deploy mismatch that has never been measured:
- Training uses single time instants at rig cameras with ground-truth geometry inputs.
- Deployment is a continuously moving viewer, off the rig, whose own previous rendered depth is fed back into fusion. That is a recurrent, closed-loop system that suffers exposure bias, the same failure Self Forcing and GeoStream fixed for generators.

Two observations make the regime trainable without per-rig ground truth:
(i) The pipeline itself says where supervision is missing. The TSDF accumulated weight and visibility count are a free per-pixel confidence map.
(ii) Where confidence is high, the rig pixels are the truth. Where it is low (disocclusions, extrapolation), a distribution-level video critic is the right signal, because a pixel-wise pseudo-label from a stochastic prior averages out and causes blur and flicker.

The result is the pipeline unrolled as a generator, a critic masked by the pipeline's own confidence, and fidelity anchored by the rig, with no diffusion at test time.
sharpened.method:
STUDENT
- A reimplementation of the base pipeline (no official code exists): per-view pixel-sized opaque Gaussian forward splatting, then a colour-gated depth filter, then an image-based TSDF with previous-frame novel-view depth feedback, then a U-Net blend with I_BG.
- Upgrade 1: a ConvGRU state in target-view space, warped by the previous rendered depth. Budget: at most 5 ms.
- Upgrade 2: the fusion hyperparameters become learnable through soft relaxations: TSDF truncation tau, feedback gain beta, cap eta, and the colour-mask slope/offset.
- Upgrade 3: a differentiable TSDF zero-crossing. The forward ray-march and bisection stay as they are; the backward pass uses the implicit-function gradient dz/dθ = −(∂s/∂θ)/(∂s/∂z) at the final crossing.
- The recipe is student-agnostic. It is also applied to a second student, a pixel-aligned feed-forward GS predictor such as GPS-Gaussian, to show generality.

ROLLOUTS
- Clips of 16-24 frames along sampled 6-DoF head trajectories: seated lean-in, lateral sway, orbit, and extrapolation up to 2x the rig baseline.
- Trajectory statistics come from public HMD viewing traces where licensable, or otherwise from synthetic paths matched to seated-telepresence head-motion ranges.
- Truncated BPTT with 4-8 frame gradient windows. The state is detached beyond the window, as in Self Forcing's gradient truncation.
- Curriculum: on-rig only, then near-rig, then far off-rig.

LOSSES
- On-rig anchor: L1, SSIM and LPIPS at held-out rig cameras, plus the base depth and mask terms, plus a flow-warped temporal loss.
- Off-rig, gated per pixel by g = 1 − normalize(TSDF weight × visibility):
  (1) Primary, cheap: a conditional spatio-temporal discriminator. Real samples are rig-camera clips; fake samples are rendered off-rig clips. Both are conditioned on the source frames. The discriminator is built on frozen video-backbone features in projected-GAN style.
  (2) Full: DMD with a frozen camera-conditioned multi-view/video diffusion teacher (a SEVA-class model per timestep, or Diffuman4D for humans) and an online-trained fake-score network at reduced resolution.
  (3) A stereo/multi-view consistency term: MEt3R-style, or disparity-warp error between the two eye renders.
- Baseline objective with the identical teacher: FreeGen-style pseudo-label regression (Difix/Fixer-refined renders as L1/LPIPS targets).

RUNTIME
- Unchanged: at most 40 ms at 1K (TensorRT), or at most 45 ms with the ConvGRU.
- No diffusion at inference.

DATA
- Training: DNA-Rendering plus MVHumanNet(++) sequences. Only the 4-6 'rig' cameras are used as inputs and supervision in the GT-free setting.
- The same captures' far dome cameras are reserved for (i) evaluation and (ii) the oracle upper bound.
- DyNeRF and ENeRF-Outdoor are kept for comparability with the base paper, evaluated on-rig plus FVD / user preference off-rig.
sharpened.why_not_engineering:
The paper makes and tests three scientific claims, not a system tweak:
(1) Recurrent geometric feedback in deterministic online renderers causes measurable exposure-bias drift, and on-policy unrolling fixes it. This is a falsifiable, measurable phenomenon that has not been characterised for IBR/TSDF pipelines.
(2) For extrapolated and disoccluded regions, a distribution-level critic gated by reconstruction confidence beats pseudo-label regression from the same prior. This is a head-to-head comparison of supervision types under a fixed student and teacher.
(3) GT-free off-rig training closes a quantified fraction of the gap to a dome-supervised oracle. The oracle bound turns 'looks better' into a calibrated number.

The benchmark, with moving-viewer and moving-scene trajectories, off-rig ground truth from dense domes, and drift metrics over minute-long clips, is a reusable community asset. It exposes a regime that every current online method (the base paper, Tele360, LiveStre4m, NSTM) evaluates nowhere.
sharpened.differentiation:
FreeGen (arXiv 2512.04830):
- FreeGen: static driving scenes; per-frame, with no recurrence; pseudo-label regression; a generation branch at inference; seconds per frame.
- Ours: dynamic humans/scenes, a recurrent TSDF feedback loop trained on-policy, a distribution critic gated by pipeline confidence, zero diffusion at test time, and 40 ms. FreeGen-style pseudo-labelling is a required baseline under an identical teacher.

Lyra (2509.19296) and FlashWorld (2510.13678):
- They distil into generators, starting from one image or a monocular video.
- Ours is faithful reconstruction from a calibrated rig with an on-rig fidelity anchor and a held-out-GT evaluation.

InstantViR (2511.14208):
- It distils a video diffusion model into a causal 2D inverse-problem solver with known degradation operators.
- Ours has 3D, novel viewpoints and a geometry loop. We cite it as evidence that causal real-time distillation is feasible.

GeoStream (2606.15162) and MV-Forcing (2607.05376):
- They address on-policy training through a 3D cache, but for diffusion generators.
- We transfer the exposure-bias diagnosis to a deterministic reconstruction renderer and quantify it with ground truth.

Difix3D+ (2503.01774), 4DGS-Fixer (2609.21176) and DriveX (2412.01717):
- These are per-scene optimisation.
- Ours is generalizable and online. Difix/Fixer are used as runtime-refiner baselines (upper bound on quality at a latency cost).

Transformer inpainting for sparse multi-camera 3D streaming (2603.05507): a GT-supervised runtime post-process, used as a runtime baseline.

MEt3R: used only as a consistency reward/metric.

datasets: DNA-Rendering. The main dataset: roughly 60-camera dome with some Kinect depth. The rig is a 4-6 camera frontal subset; far dome cameras (30-90 deg off-axis) give off-rig ground truth; stereo depth comes from adjacent rig pairs or a multi-view depth foundation model.
ActorsHQ. About 160 high-resolution cameras, few sequences. Used as a held-out test set with dense off-rig ground truth and near-continuous pseudo-trajectories through camera chains.
MVHumanNet / MVHumanNet++. Large-scale multi-view human training data. Check the camera count and minute-long sequences per subset.
CMU Panoptic (HD cameras plus Kinects). Multi-person and close interaction, useful for disocclusion stress tests.
DyNeRF / Neural 3D Video and ENeRF-Outdoor. For comparability with the base paper; on-rig metrics; off-rig scored only with FVD / critic score / user preference because no ground truth exists there.
D3DMV. Optional, to match the base paper's third benchmark.
Public 6-DoF HMD viewing traces for trajectory statistics (verify license), with synthetic seated-telepresence paths as a fallback.
baselines: Base recipe: single-instant training with rig-camera ground truth only (reimplemented).
Base + temporal warp loss only (no off-rig supervision).
Base with teacher-forced multi-frame training (ground-truth depth feedback), versus on-policy.
FreeGen-style pseudo-label regression: the same frozen Difix/Fixer or video-diffusion teacher, used to refine off-rig renders offline into L1/LPIPS targets.
Oracle: direct supervision from far dome cameras (upper bound on what the student can absorb).
Runtime refiners: base + Difix3D+ single-step fixer, base + NVIDIA Fixer, base + transformer spatio-temporal inpainting (2603.05507). Each is reported with its latency.
Feed-forward online competitors where code exists: GPS-Gaussian (retrained), Tele360 / LiveStre4m / NSTM if released. Evaluated under the new moving-viewer protocol.
Second student: the same training recipe applied to a GPS-Gaussian-style pixel-aligned GS predictor.
metrics: Off-rig fidelity at dome ground-truth cameras binned by angular distance from the rig (0-15, 15-30, 30-60, 60-90 deg): PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, plus masked metrics restricted to low-confidence (disoccluded) pixels.
Distributional off-rig quality where no ground truth exists: FVD / FID-style video metrics.
Temporal: tLPIPS, flow-warped error, TCC, STED, SDT along moving-viewer, moving-scene trajectories.
Drift: PSNR/tLPIPS decay slope and time-to-failure over 1-5 minute sequences, with and without keyframe resets.
View/stereo consistency: SDV, EPI stability, MEt3R, disparity-warp error between the two eye renders.
Faithfulness and hallucination: on-rig PSNR regression, face identity similarity at off-rig views, and a hallucination rate in high-confidence pixels (should be about 0).
Latency on the target GPU, end-to-end, reporting depth estimation separately.
HMD user study with free head motion: 2AFC preference and comfort (n≈20).
key_ablations: On-policy unrolled vs teacher-forced training, and rollout/BPTT length (4/8/16).
Critic type: adversarial video discriminator vs DMD vs pseudo-label regression vs combinations, all with the same teacher.
Confidence gating: none vs TSDF-weight gating vs visibility-count gating; effect on on-rig fidelity and hallucination rate.
Learnable vs fixed fusion hyperparameters (tau, beta, eta, mask), and ConvGRU state on/off.
Trajectory distribution: near-rig only vs curriculum up to 2x baseline; synthetic vs HMD-trace-derived paths.
Teacher choice: Difix/Fixer (single-step image) vs SEVA-class multi-view vs Diffuman4D (4D human).
Student capacity: U-Net width vs off-rig gain vs latency (Pareto curve), to settle the capacity-limit objection.
Fraction of the oracle gap recovered as a function of the number of rig cameras (2/4/6).
experiments.capture_notes:
No custom capture is needed for the core paper. Dense-dome human datasets (DNA-Rendering, ActorsHQ, MVHumanNet) provide both rig subsets and far off-rig ground truth, and DyNeRF/ENeRF-Outdoor cover general scenes.

Caveats:
- DNA-Rendering and MVHumanNet need license agreements, which take time.
- Depth for rig subsets must be computed (a stereo foundation model on adjacent pairs, or a multi-view depth foundation model), and its latency reported separately.
- The dome cameras are static, so true moving-camera ground truth does not exist. Approximate it with camera-chain pseudo-trajectories and evaluate per-frame against the nearest dome camera, plus temporal metrics without a reference.

Optional: a small 4-camera desktop rig (about 2-4k USD) would strengthen the HMD user study and the claim of training on a deployment rig without a dome. It is not required for acceptance.

review.first_two_week_test:
A capacity-and-supervision probe that skips DMD entirely.

Days 1-5: build a minimal student on 10-20 DNA-Rendering sequences:
- 4 frontal rig cameras, with depth from a stereo or multi-view depth foundation model, precomputed.
- Per-view forward splatting, then a U-Net blend with I_BG, at 512 px.
- Skip the TSDF at first and use nearest-view depth.

Days 6-12: train four variants for about 30k iterations each, one GPU each:
- (A) Rig-only ground truth: the base recipe.
- (B) A plus FreeGen-style pseudo-labels, made by running a frozen Difix/Fixer on off-rig renders at camera positions 15-60 deg away.
- (C) A plus a conditional patch/video discriminator on the same off-rig renders, gated by visibility count.
- (D) Oracle: A plus direct supervision from real dome cameras at those positions.

Evaluate LPIPS/PSNR on held-out far dome cameras and on disoccluded-pixel masks.

In parallel (days 8-14): add naive previous-depth feedback and unroll 300 frames. Compare teacher-forced against 2k iterations of on-policy fine-tuning (8-frame BPTT) on the drift slope.

Reading the results:
- If D does not beat A, the student has hit its capacity limit; kill the idea or widen the student.
- If C and B both fail to close the A-D gap, the prior cannot help.
- If B closes most of the gap and C does not beat B, the critic claim dies; reposition as a benchmark plus on-policy paper.
- The drift experiment tells you whether exposure bias is even measurable in this loop.
review.kill_criteria:
Drop or reposition if any of the following holds on at least 2 seeds:
(1) Capacity kill. The dome-GT oracle improves off-rig LPIPS by less than 10% relative over the rig-only recipe at 40 ms or less. The fast student cannot absorb off-rig knowledge, so no prior will help. Pivot to a runtime-refiner paper.
(2) Prior kill. Neither critic nor pseudo-label training recovers at least 25% of the rig-only-to-oracle gap on far (30-60 deg) cameras.
(3) Critic kill. The confidence-gated critic fails to beat FreeGen-style pseudo-label regression by at least 0.01 LPIPS or on temporal metrics (tLPIPS/TCC). The contribution then collapses to 'FreeGen for telepresence'; keep only the benchmark plus on-policy parts and target TVCG/IEEE VR.
(4) On-policy kill. Teacher-forced vs on-policy drift over 1-minute sequences differs by less than 10%, meaning exposure bias is not a real phenomenon in this loop. Remove the self-forcing claim.
(5) Fidelity kill. On-rig PSNR regresses by more than 0.3 dB, or the hallucination rate in high-confidence pixels is non-negligible, which is unacceptable for telepresence.
(6) Scoop check before submission: a 2026-27 paper appears that trains an online human or scene renderer with an off-rig diffusion critic and on-policy recurrent rollouts.

reviewer_objections.objection: This is FreeGen / Lyra / DriveX applied to telepresence: distilling a generative prior into a fast renderer on views without ground truth is already published.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal:
The generic move is conceded and cited. What is new, and shown experimentally:
(i) On-policy training through a recurrent geometric feedback loop in a dynamic scene, with measured drift reduction. FreeGen, Lyra and DriveX have no recurrence.
(ii) A head-to-head of the supervision type under an identical teacher and student: the confidence-gated distribution critic beats FreeGen-style pseudo-labels on disoccluded-pixel LPIPS and on temporal metrics.
(iii) Zero diffusion at inference within 40 ms, where FreeGen and GIFSplat keep a generative branch.
(iv) A moving-viewer benchmark with an oracle bound.

reviewer_objections.objection: Dense domes give off-rig ground truth. Why go GT-free? Just supervise with the extra dome cameras.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We do train that oracle, and it is the upper bound. The claim is the fraction of the oracle gap recovered with rig-only data. That matters because deployment rigs (a 4-camera desk rig, a Beam-like booth) have no dome, domes cover only studio humans, and dome cameras are discrete and static, so they cannot supervise continuous moving-viewer video. We also show the combination: oracle plus critic on continuous trajectories between dome cameras beats the oracle alone on temporal metrics.

reviewer_objections.objection: Hallucinating content is dangerous for telepresence fidelity: the critic will invent details and alter identity.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Critic gradients are gated by the pipeline's own TSDF and visibility confidence, and on-rig ground-truth anchoring is kept. We report (a) on-rig PSNR regression of at most 0.2 dB, (b) hallucination rate and error restricted to high-confidence pixels, and (c) face-identity similarity at off-rig views. Ablating the gate shows the fidelity cost that the gate prevents.

reviewer_objections.objection: A tiny per-frame U-Net cannot absorb a video-diffusion prior, and DMD with a strongly conditioned multi-view teacher is unstable and compute-heavy for a small lab.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: A capacity-versus-latency Pareto curve and the dome oracle measure the absorbable headroom directly. We also add a ConvGRU state. The primary critic is a cheap conditional video discriminator on frozen features; DMD is an ablation at reduced resolution. We report seeds, teacher choice (Difix/Fixer vs SEVA-class vs Diffuman4D) and GPU-hours. The paper's claims do not depend on DMD specifically.

reviewer_objections.objection: The base pipeline is dated: a heuristic TSDF, 640 px, no code, and competitors (Tele360, LiveStre4m, NSTM) are pose-free feed-forward. Results may not transfer.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: The recipe is student-agnostic and is shown on two students: the geometry-guided IBR reimplementation and a pixel-aligned GS predictor. Pose-free competitors are evaluated on the new moving-viewer protocol, which none of them reports. The benchmark and the drift finding stand whichever student wins.

effort.months: 7-9 (about 1.5 months reimplementing the base pipeline, since there is no official code, plus about 1 month for data licenses and depth precompute)
effort.people: 2 (one PhD student on the renderer and on-policy training, one on critics/teacher plus the benchmark and user study)
effort.compute: 4-8 GPUs with 80 GB (A100/H100 class), roughly 3-6k GPU-hours in total. The discriminator-only path fits on 4x 48 GB GPUs; the DMD variant with a 1-2B video teacher needs 80 GB cards and dominates the budget.

review.venue: ICCV 2027 (primary). The CVPR 2027 deadline is too close for a reimplementation plus a new benchmark. SIGGRAPH Asia 2027 is the fallback if the HMD user study and system aspects are strong. IEEE VR / TVCG if the result is mainly the moving-viewer benchmark plus the user study.
review.synergies:
- Learned temporal memory and long-horizon drift (the landscape gap on replacing TSDF plus colour-mask heuristics with a ConvGRU or TTT state). This paper supplies the on-policy training that such a memory needs, and the two could merge into one stronger paper: 'recurrent online renderer trained on its own rollouts'.
- Runtime diffusion-fixer direction (Difix/Fixer refiner). It is the natural baseline and teacher, so the two form a series: fixer at runtime versus fixer distilled away.
- Probabilistic/uncertainty-aware fusion. Better-calibrated confidence directly improves the critic gating.
- A unified online-telepresence benchmark (minute-long sequences, desync and lighting stress). The moving-viewer, off-rig-GT protocol here can be its core.
- Stereo/HMD rendering and the split sender/receiver design. Zero added receiver cost suits standalone HMDs and codec-streamed RGB-D or Gaussian maps.
- Pose-free feed-forward live NVS (Tele360, LiveStre4m). The student-agnostic recipe transfers to them.

Sources opened or seen in this review:
- FreeGen https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04830
- Streaming4D https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00610 (a Self-Forcing generator plus incremental reconstruction; not a threat)
- Transformer inpainting for sparse multi-camera 3D streaming https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.05507
- Plus the novelty report's verified URLs: 2509.19296, 2511.14208, 2606.15162, 2607.05376, 2506.08009, 2503.01774, 2609.21176, 2412.01717, 2507.13344
- Landscape entries: Tele360 2609.15032, LiveStre4m 2604.06740, NSTM 2607.15271

The WebSearch budget was exhausted and the arXiv/Semantic Scholar APIs returned 429, so the 2026 human-avatar literature was not re-searched beyond the novelty report.

name: Non-Lambertian / specular robustness: two-layer reflection IBR or probabilistic depth with light-field fallback

cited_work_check.title: IBGS: Image-Based Gaussian Splatting (NeurIPS 2025)
cited_work_check.note: The abstract matches the ideator's description: pixel colour = 3DGS base colour + a learned residual from neighbouring training images, targeting view-dependent and specular effects. It is per-scene optimised and static, and has no reflection depth.

cited_work_check.title: ViewSplat: View-Adaptive 3D Gaussian Splatting for Feed-Forward Synthesis
cited_work_check.note: Exists. v2's title drops 'Dynamic'; the word referred to view-adaptive Gaussians, not dynamic scenes. It is feed-forward from UNPOSED images, with target-view-conditioned MLP residuals that improve specular content. It is static and per-frame and has no temporal filtering, so the ideator's characterisation holds.

cited_work_check.title: Reflection-aware Generative Novel View Synthesis (Ref-GeNVS)
cited_work_check.note: A training-free, mirror-only method: it reflects camera poses across the estimated mirror plane to create virtual views inside a multi-view diffusion model. A Springer LNCS chapter exists (link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-032-37167-6_25), which fits the claimed ECCV 2026 venue. It is generative and offline, as claimed.

cited_work_check.title: MVID: Feed-Forward Multi-View Intrinsic Image Decomposition
cited_work_check.note: A feed-forward multi-view split into albedo, diffuse shading and a non-diffuse residual. It does no view synthesis and has no temporal warping. Accurate.

cited_work_check.title: Stereo Anywhere (CVPR 2025)
cited_work_check.note: Fuses mono VFM priors with a stereo cost volume and is robust on mirrors and transparent surfaces. Its output is depth only. Accurate.

cited_work_check.title: Fast-FoundationStereo: Real-Time Zero-Shot Stereo Matching
cited_work_check.note: Exists and claims real-time zero-shot stereo. I did not verify the ~21 ms TensorRT figure (it is not in the abstract). Its output is a point estimate, as the ideator says.

cited_work_check.title: Stereo Any Video (ICCV 2025)
cited_work_check.note: Temporally consistent video stereo using mono video-depth priors. Exists as described.

cited_work_check.title: Free360
cited_work_check.note: Layered GS for sparse unposed 360-degree scenes, with iterative fusion of reconstruction and generation. It is offline and per-scene. 'Uncertainty-aware' did not appear in the visible abstract text, so that part is mildly loose but not wrong in spirit. It is a weak comparison point in any case.

cited_work_check.title: Image-based rendering for scenes with reflections (Sinha et al., SIGGRAPH 2012)
cited_work_check.note: The classic two-layer (transmitted plus reflected, virtual depth) IBR for static scenes, correctly cited. The ideator OMITS a closer successor: Xu et al., SIGGRAPH 2021, 'Scalable image-based indoor scene rendering with reflections', which also uses a two-layer front/back (reflection) geometric representation.

threats.title: Scalable Image-based Indoor Scene Rendering with Reflections (Xu et al.)
threats.what_overlaps: Idea A's core representational insight: a front layer (RGB-D surface) plus a back layer (reflection geometry at virtual depth), both used for IBR warping and composited to minimise novel-view error. Among published two-layer reflection IBR it is the closest ancestor, closer than Sinha 2012, and the ideator does not cite it.
threats.what_remains_different: It is offline, uses global-mesh-guided alternating optimisation, and targets static indoor scenes. There is no feed-forward inference, no online per-frame reflection depth, no temporal filtering and no dynamic content.

threats.title: Immersive Light Field Video with a Layered Mesh Representation (Broxton et al.)
threats.what_overlaps: A learned (DeepView) feed-forward multi-layer representation from a FIXED camera rig for multi-view VIDEO. It explicitly reproduces view-dependent reflections and semi-transparency by putting content on extra layers at virtual depths, which is the implicit version of Idea A's 'second parallax layer'.
threats.what_remains_different: The layers are generic (MPI/shells collapsed to RGBA+depth). There is no explicit specular detection or reflection-depth estimate, no diffuse/specular split, no layer-specific temporal filtering, no TSDF geometry, and it is not an online telepresence pipeline.

threats.title: Quark: Real-time, High-resolution, and General Neural View Synthesis
threats.what_overlaps: Real-time (1080p, 30 fps) feed-forward layered-depth-map view synthesis from sparse video streams. Semi-transparent layers can represent reflections at virtual depths implicitly. It is the strongest real-time feed-forward baseline for 'more than one depth per pixel'.
threats.what_remains_different: The abstract and project page make no explicit reflection or specular modelling claim and describe no temporal-consistency mechanism. There is no reflection-depth sweep on specular residuals, no specular-aware geometry fusion and no separate temporal filters.

threats.title: Self-Supervised Visibility Learning for Novel View Synthesis
threats.what_overlaps: Idea B's 'probabilistic target-ray fusion': per-source-view visibility builds a consensus volume, and soft ray-casting yields a target-view depth PROBABILITY distribution. Source pixels are warped and blended with it, trained end-to-end from the synthesis loss. That is a learned, differentiable generalisation of hard fusion.
threats.what_remains_different: It is static and per-frame, with no calibrated per-view uncertainty from stereo foundation models, no temporal (Kalman) filtering, no light-field fallback mode and no specular focus.

threats.title: Neural Rays for Occlusion-aware Image-based Rendering (NeuRay)
threats.what_overlaps: Per-input-view pixel features that decode to mixture-of-logistics depth distributions, used to compute per-view visibility along target rays in generalisable IBR. This is essentially 'fuse per-view depth distributions along the target ray'.
threats.what_remains_different: It is NeRF-style volume rendering, not real-time, and static, with no temporal filtering, no light-field fallback and no uncertainty calibration against stereo foundation models.

threats.title: Soft 3D Reconstruction for View Synthesis (Penner & Zhang)
threats.what_overlaps: Idea B's framing: per-view soft depth and visibility probabilities replace hard fused depth, and occlusion uncertainty is propagated into IBR blending. The search snippet also notes that Soft3D's aggregation blurs specular geometry, which is exactly the failure Idea B wants to fix.
threats.what_remains_different: It is hand-crafted, not learned end-to-end, has no light-field fallback, no temporal Kalman filter and no stereo-FM uncertainty.

threats.title: Deep Flow Rendering: View Synthesis via Layer-aware Reflection Flow
threats.what_overlaps: Separate view-independent (texture) and view-dependent (reflection) paths. Reflections are transferred from nearby source views with a learned layer-aware flow, which is IBR-style specular transfer.
threats.what_remains_different: Per-scene optimisation, static, no temporal component, no online or feed-forward capture pipeline.

threats.title: Neural Point Catacaustics for Novel-View Synthesis of Reflections
threats.what_overlaps: Explicit reflected-point geometry (catacaustic trajectories): a separate point cloud for reflections moves with its own parallax, separate from the diffuse cloud.
threats.what_remains_different: Per-scene optimised, static and offline.

threats.title: NeRFReN: Neural Radiance Fields with Reflections
threats.what_overlaps: A transmitted plus reflected two-field decomposition with a reflection mask, which is the neural-field analogue of two-layer IBR.
threats.what_remains_different: Per-scene optimised, static and slow.

threats.title: TraceFlow: Dynamic 3D Reconstruction of Specular Scenes Driven by Ray Tracing
threats.what_overlaps: DYNAMIC specular scenes with an explicit diffuse/specular decomposition, evaluated on dynamic-scene benchmarks that likely include DyNeRF. It shows that the specular-dynamic gap is being attacked.
threats.what_remains_different: Per-scene optimised 2DGS with ray tracing and a dynamic environment Gaussian. It is not feed-forward, not online and not IBR.

threats.title: Learning Stable Canonical Worlds for Novel View Synthesis and Beyond (CanonicalGS)
threats.what_overlaps: Feed-forward GS with uncertainty-aware fusion of view-centric evidence, emphasising reliable observations and suppressing uncertain ones. This is the 'uncertainty is the interface' idea in a feed-forward setting.
threats.what_remains_different: Static multi-view, with no temporal filtering, no light-field fallback and no specular focus.

threats.title: InvSplat: Inverse Feed-Forward Scene Splatting
threats.what_overlaps: Feed-forward multi-view prediction of Gaussians with albedo, metallic and roughness, for more faithful view-dependent effects.

sharpened.title: Highlights Have Their Own Parallax: Online Two-Layer Reflection-Aware IBR with Layer-Specific Temporal Dynamics for Multi-View 3D Video
sharpened.one_liner: Split each geometry-guided IBR frame into a diffuse layer and a specular layer. The diffuse layer is warped by a heavily time-filtered TSDF surface. The specular layer is warped by an online, per-frame virtual reflection depth and uses a low-inertia memory. Highlights then move with the correct parallax and stop both ghosting across views and flickering over time, for about 10 ms extra per frame.
sharpened.core_claim: At equal network capacity and runtime (at most 12 ms overhead over a Ha et al.-style pipeline), four changes together cut view and temporal inconsistency on specular-masked pixels by at least 25%, measured as EPI discontinuity and flow-warped temporal error (tOF/STED) at held-out cameras. The four changes are: (a) a second, reflection-depth-warped specular layer; (b) a layer-specific temporal filter; (c) specular-aware (1 − s) TSDF weighting; (d) an entropy-gated view-conditioned fallback for glossy pixels. Specular-masked PSNR also improves by at least 0.7 dB. Three comparators serve as references: (i) single-layer surface warping, (ii) a view-conditioned residual head of equal capacity (ViewSplat/IBGS-style), and (iii) any single shared temporal filter, which cannot reach the same flicker-versus-lag Pareto point. Full-frame metrics must not regress. The claim is falsified if an oracle two-layer split (GT separation plus best reflection depth) cannot beat single-layer warping by these margins, or if the equal-capacity residual head matches the method on EPI and temporal metrics.
sharpened.key_insight:
Specular appearance fails in geometry-guided IBR because it has different kinematics from the surface, not because the surface depth is noisy. A reflection is a virtual image with its own depth:
- For a planar screen or mirror, the virtual depth is the reflected distance.
- For a convex glossy surface lit from far away (eyeglass lenses, cornea, cheekbones, metal pans), the virtual image sits about R/2 behind the surface, by the mirror equation.
So a per-pixel virtual depth is a physically grounded first-order model of highlight parallax, and it can be estimated online by plane-sweeping only the cross-view-inconsistent residual behind the TSDF surface.

Separating the layers also separates their temporal statistics: surface geometry is slow and should get long memory, while highlights move with the viewer, the lights and small head rotations and need short memory warped by their own depth. A single temporal filter must trade lag against flicker; two filters need not.

Where the reflection-depth cost volume is flat (rough gloss), its entropy is the signal to fall back to view-conditioned angular blending. That fallback absorbs the useful part of the 'probabilistic depth plus light-field fallback' idea without claiming probabilistic fusion as novel.
sharpened.method:
Front end (inside the latency budget, unlike the base paper):
- Per-view depth from Fast-FoundationStereo on automatically chosen neighbour pairs, or from sensor RGB-D.
- A cheap monocular prior (streaming Video Depth Anything or similar) aligned to stereo scale. The mono-stereo disagreement map u_n is kept as an unreliability cue.

(1) Specular and unreliability detection (training-free core plus a tiny CNN):
- Raymarch the base paper's image-based TSDF for each target pixel and reproject the surface point into the K views.
- Compute a robust colour dispersion across views, normalised by exposure and sensor noise, together with saturation, u_n and the reflection-vector alignment dot(reflect(target ray, n), input ray_k).
- A 3-layer CNN maps these features to s ∈ [0,1]. Supervision: synthetic GT glossy-pass masks and a leave-one-view-out consistency loss on real data.

(2) Specular-aware geometry:
- The TSDF fusion weight becomes ω_k·(1 − s_k), so reflections do not pull the surface toward the virtual image.

(3) Layer separation per input view:
- Diffuse D = a robust low quantile or median of the reprojected cross-view samples at the surface (Lambertian consensus).
- Specular residual S = max(I − D, 0), plus a learned correction for the case where highlights cover at least K/2 views.

(4) Reflection depth:
- Only on pixels with s > τ (typically 3-15% of pixels), sweep 24-32 virtual depths behind the surface along the reflected-ray parameterisation, scoring cross-view consistency of S.
- Soft-argmin gives d_r. The normalised cost-volume entropy h is kept.

(5) Rendering:
- The base paper's pixel-sized opaque Gaussians are forward-splatted twice: the diffuse layer with surface depth, and the specular layer (sparse pixels only) with d_r.
- A glossy fallback path blends S with view-angle (Unstructured Lumigraph-style) weights at the surface depth.
- The U-Net blender receives both layers, s, h, normals and the reflection-vector features. It outputs diffuse weights, specular weights and a fallback mix gated by h.

(6) Temporal:
- The diffuse layer keeps the base paper's TSDF feedback and colour-difference-gated filter; a long memory is fine.
- The specular layer keeps a short exponential memory, warped between frames by the flow that d_r induces (not by surface flow). Its learned inertia is conditioned on s and h.

Losses:
- L1 + SSIM + LPIPS, plus a specular-masked loss (weight 2-4x).
- Flow-warped temporal loss applied per layer: the diffuse layer is warped by surface-induced flow and the specular layer by reflection-induced flow.
- Layer-supervision L1 on synthetic GT diffuse and glossy passes.
- A reflection-depth loss on synthetic data, where GT virtual depth is computable from the mirror equation or from path tracing.

Training data:
- The base paper's data: ScanNet, DyNeRF training scenes and Spaces.
- About 200 synthetic PBR multi-view video clips (12-16 cameras, Blender Cycles with separate diffuse and glossy passes): THuman/RenderPeople-style scans wearing eyeglasses, laptop and monitor screens reflecting animated rooms, metal kitchenware, glossy skin shaders, and moving emitters with HDRIs.

Runtime budget:
- Base about 39 ms at 1352x1014 with TensorRT.
- Detector 2 ms, sparse sweep 3-5 ms, second sparse splat 2-3 ms, extra blender channels about 2 ms.
- Target overhead at most 12 ms, with stereo front-end time reported separately and end to end.
sharpened.why_not_engineering:
Four things make this a research contribution rather than a system tweak:

(a) A modelling claim with a physical basis, tested against strong learned alternatives. The claim is that highlight parallax is well modelled by a single virtual depth per pixel (mirror equation, with an R/2 approximation for convex gloss). It is tested with an oracle-headroom study and an equal-capacity view-conditioned residual baseline.

(b) A temporal-dynamics finding: separate layers admit separate optimal temporal filters. This is shown as a Pareto curve (flicker vs lag), a trade-off no single shared filter reaches. Prior two-layer reflection IBR (Sinha 2012; Xu 2021) was static and never exposed this.

(c) A failure analysis explaining when geometry guidance helps. It shows that specular-corrupted TSDF depth is one reason the base paper's TSDF ablation is null (31.16 vs 31.17 dB), because (1 − s) weighting changes geometry exactly where it was wrong.

(d) The first benchmark with held-out-camera GT and view × time consistency metrics restricted to specular regions, on telepresence content (eyeglasses, screens, glossy skin).

No component is just a larger network. The ablations isolate representation, estimator, temporal model and geometry weighting.
sharpened.differentiation:
vs Sinha et al. SIGGRAPH 2012 (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2185520.2185596) and Xu et al. SIGGRAPH 2021 (http://www.cad.zju.edu.cn/home/weiweixu/wwxu2021.files/ReflectiveIBR.pdf):
- Same two-layer (front surface plus virtual reflection geometry) representation. It must be cited as the ancestor and NOT claimed as novel.
- Theirs is offline, static, mesh- and optimisation-based. Ours is feed-forward, estimated per frame online, runs on dynamic video, and adds layer-specific temporal filtering plus specular-aware geometry fusion.

vs Broxton et al. 2020 (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3386569.3392485) and Quark 2024 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.16680):
- Their multi-layer representations capture reflections only implicitly, as generic extra layers.
- They have no explicit specular detection, no reflection-depth estimate, no diffuse/specular split, no layer-specific temporal model and no specular-masked consistency evaluation.
- A Quark-style layered baseline must be included to show that explicit reflection depth beats generic layers on EPI and temporal metrics at equal runtime.

vs IBGS (https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14357) and ViewSplat (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25265):
- Their view-conditioned residuals improve single-frame specular PSNR but carry no parallax model and no temporal term. IBGS is per-scene; ViewSplat is static and per-frame.
- Our key ablation replaces our specular layer with an equal-capacity residual head.

vs Soft3D (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3130800.3130855), Self-Supervised Visibility Learning (https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.15407) and NeuRay (https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13421):
- Probabilistic target-ray depth fusion is established, so we do NOT claim it.
- We use only the cost-volume entropy of the reflection sweep as a gate for the glossy fallback.

vs per-scene dynamic specular methods, NeRF-DS (https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.14435) and TraceFlow (https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10095):
- They are optimisation-based and offline. They serve as quality upper bounds, not competitors.

vs Ref-GeNVS (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05382):
- Generative, mirror-only and offline.

vs Stereo Anywhere (https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04472) and Fast-FoundationStereo (https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.11130):
- Depth sources only. They are used as our front end, and we show that better depth alone does not fix highlight ghosting and flicker. That is baseline 'base + FM stereo'.

experiments.capture_notes:
Public multi-view VIDEO datasets contain little telepresence-relevant specular content with held-out cameras. DyNeRF has pans, pots and glass. Eyeglasses and screens are, at best, incidental in DNA-Rendering / ActorsHQ and need verification. So a small custom capture is needed for the telepresence claim and the benchmark.

Budget:
- About USD 4-10k for 8-12 genlocked global-shutter machine-vision cameras, or sync-cabled RGB-D cameras.
- One capture PC, a colour chart and a calibration board.

Protocol:
- 10-15 sequences with eyeglasses, laptop and monitor screens, glossy skin under a key light, and a glossy desk.
- Several lighting setups, including a moving light.
- 2-4 held-out cameras, including one leave-2-out wide gap so that reflection-parallax errors are not hidden by tiny interpolation baselines.

The synthetic PBR set is essential for layer and reflection-depth GT and for free trajectories. It costs about 2-3 weeks of setup plus render time on a few GPUs.

Consent and privacy: faces of lab volunteers need a signed release before the benchmark is published.

review.first_two_week_test:
A non-learned oracle and estimator headroom study (no network training).

Days 1-4, synthetic data:
- Render 3 short synthetic clips in Blender Cycles: 12 cameras, 60 frames, separate diffuse and glossy passes, GT depth.
- Clip (a): a head with eyeglasses under a moving key light. Clip (b): a monitor reflecting an animated room. Clip (c): a rotating glossy metal pot.

Days 3-6, real depth:
- Compute Fast-FoundationStereo (or RAFT-Stereo) depth on DyNeRF cook_spinach / flame_steak (pan regions) and on the synthetic clips.

Days 5-10, a minimal fixed-weight renderer:
- Image-based TSDF raymarch, K=4 nearest views, forward warp, Unstructured Lumigraph blend weights. Four variants:
  - (i) single-layer surface warp (base-paper-like without the learned blender);
  - (ii) oracle two-layer: GT diffuse/glossy split, glossy pass warped by the best-of-sweep virtual depth chosen with GT, as an upper bound;
  - (iii) estimated two-layer: median-of-K diffuse, residual swept over 32 depths behind the surface, argmin of cross-view variance;
  - (iv) (iii) plus (1 − s) TSDF weighting.

Days 9-12, temporal filters:
- Run an EMA on the specular layer with a sweep of α, versus one shared α on the whole image. Plot flicker (tOF) against lag (highlight-position delay on synthetic data).

Days 12-14, measurement:
- Specular-masked PSNR, EPI discontinuity, tOF and highlight-position error at held-out cameras, including one leave-2-out gap.
- The fraction of real detected specular pixels whose sweep cost volume is peaked (low entropy) rather than flat.

A single student with one GPU can do this.
review.kill_criteria:
Drop the explicit two-layer direction if any of the following holds.

(1) No headroom. The ORACLE two-layer variant beats single-layer surface warping by less than 1 dB specular-masked PSNR AND less than 25% reduction in specular EPI / highlight-position error on the synthetic clips, including the leave-2-out gap. That means reflection parallax is not the dominant error at rig baselines.

(2) Estimator is the bottleneck. The estimated variant (median-of-K plus sweep) recovers less than 40% of the oracle gain at K=4, and still less than 50% at K=8. Median-diffuse separation is then unworkable with telepresence-sized rigs.

(3) Real speculars are almost all glossy. On real DyNeRF pan regions and a quick 4-6 camera phone or webcam test with eyeglasses and a screen, more than 70% of detected specular pixels have a flat reflection-sweep cost volume (entropy above 0.8 of maximum). The contribution would then reduce to a 'gated view-conditioned fallback', which is too thin next to ViewSplat/IBGS.

(4) No temporal benefit. Layer-specific EMA does not dominate every shared-α setting on the flicker-vs-lag Pareto curve.

If (1) and (4) fail but (3) passes, pivot to a benchmark/diagnostic paper: specular view × time consistency for online IBR, plus the (1 − s) geometry-weighting finding. Target a 3DV/TVCG-level venue.

reviewer_objections.objection: Two-layer reflection IBR is Sinha et al. 2012 and Xu et al. 2021 (neither cited by the original idea); this is a known representation made fast, i.e. engineering.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal:
We cite both as ancestors and do not claim the representation. The claims are three:
- Online per-frame reflection-depth estimation inside a feed-forward multi-view video pipeline, which neither ancestor has.
- The temporal finding that separated layers admit separate optimal dynamics, shown as a Pareto improvement over any shared filter, which a static method cannot even pose.
- Specular-aware geometry weighting that measurably repairs TSDF depth.
The oracle-headroom study plus equal-capacity ablations turn this into a tested modelling claim rather than a speed-up.

reviewer_objections.objection: A bigger blend network, or a view-conditioned residual head (ViewSplat/IBGS-style), would absorb specularity without any explicit reflection depth.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: This is our central ablation, run at equal parameters and runtime. The hypothesis, pre-registered in the kill criteria, is that residual heads recover single-frame masked PSNR but not EPI or temporal consistency. They have no model of where a highlight should move, so errors show up as view-sweep discontinuities and flicker, especially at leave-2-out wide gaps and on synthetic free trajectories. If the residual head matches us on EPI and tOF, the paper's claim is falsified and we report that.

reviewer_objections.objection: Most telepresence specularities (skin, rough plastics) are glossy, not mirror-like; a single virtual depth is ill-defined and median-of-4 diffuse estimation fails when highlights span most views.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: The mirror equation gives a first-order virtual depth of about R/2 behind convex glossy surfaces, so highlight parallax is still approximately depth-like for eyeglass lenses, corneas and pans. Where it is not, the sweep's cost-volume entropy gates a view-conditioned fallback. We report results stratified by roughness (synthetic) and by K, including where the method stops helping. We also add a learned correction for the case where highlights cover at least K/2 views and quantify its failure rate.

reviewer_objections.objection: Specular pixels are a tiny fraction of the frame; gains are invisible in standard metrics, and the benchmark (synthetic plus own capture) is self-serving.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We report full-frame metrics with a no-regression requirement, alongside region-masked metrics, which is the established practice for localized artifacts. A 2AFC HMD study measures perceptual salience, since flickering or doubled highlights on glasses and eyes are highly noticeable in faces. The real capture is released with held-out cameras and calibration so others can evaluate. DyNeRF pan regions give a third-party real test.

reviewer_objections.objection: Evaluation at held-out rig cameras between near neighbours hides parallax errors, and the 'online' claim excludes depth estimation (as in the base paper).
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We add leave-2-out wide-gap held-out cameras on the custom and Technicolor rigs, plus synthetic free trajectories with GT. We report end-to-end latency, including the stereo foundation model front end, on a stated GPU, with a per-module breakdown and a target of at most 12 ms overhead over the base pipeline.

effort.months: 9-11 (0.5 headroom study; 1.5 base-pipeline reimplementation, since there is no official code; 1.5 synthetic PBR data plus rig build and capture; 3-4 method; 2 evaluation, user study and writing)
effort.people: 2 (one PhD student on the method, one on the synthetic data, capture rig and benchmark; about 20% of a supervisor's time)
effort.compute: 4-8 GPUs with 24-48 GB (RTX 4090/5090 or A6000/L40-class) for training and Cycles rendering, plus one RTX-class GPU with TensorRT for latency measurement. About USD 4-10k of camera and sync hardware for an 8-12 camera genlocked rig.

review.venue: Primary: SIGGRAPH Asia 2027 / ACM TOG. Alternatives: ICCV 2027 or CVPR 2028. If the result narrows to a benchmark and diagnostic, target IEEE TVCG / IEEE VR 2028 (the user study and HMD evaluation fit well there).
review.synergies:
1. View × time consistency benchmark and metrics cluster: the specular-masked EPI, tOF and lag metrics and the held-out-camera telepresence capture belong to a broader online-telepresence benchmark, so they could be combined into one dataset paper.

2. Stereo foundation model / uncertainty front-end cluster: the mono-stereo disagreement and cross-view dispersion cues (the useful remnant of the cluster's probabilistic-depth idea) double as a general 'unreliable geometry' signal, and the (1 − s) weighting helps explain the base paper's null TSDF ablation.

3. Long-horizon memory and drift cluster: layer-specific memories generalise naturally, e.g. long memory for the static diffuse background and short memory for dynamic or view-dependent layers.

4. Light-field and multi-view display rendering: the sparse specular layer is cheap to re-render per view, so the diffuse layer can be amortised across 32-45 display views.

5. Gaze and eye-contact fidelity: correct corneal and eyeglass highlights are perceptual gaze cues, a natural joint user study.

6. Relighting and compositing for telepresence: the online diffuse/specular split enables approximate lighting harmonisation of the remote person into the local scene.

7. Bandwidth and compression: the specular layer is sparse and could be transmitted at lower resolution or rate, or with a separate codec.

cited_work_check.note: Exists (Jan 2026). A single-image SAM extension for segmentation plus matting, with no multi-view or background-plate constraint. Accurate, but it is a weak comparator; the real matting threats are BGMv2-family and capture-stage matting, which the ideator did not cite.

threats.title: High-quality video view interpolation using a layered representation (Zitnick, Kang, Uyttendaele, Winder, Szeliski)
threats.what_overlaps: Mixed pixels near depth discontinuities in multi-camera video are matted automatically and split into a boundary layer (foreground colour, alpha, depth) and a main layer (background colour and depth), then rendered at interactive rates. This is exactly the 'two-layer mixed-pixel unprojection' contribution, only with Gaussians replaced by layered depth images.
threats.what_remains_different: It has no Gaussian splatting, no learned blending, and no temporal memory of background. Its matting is Bayesian-style at stereo discontinuities rather than known-background difference matting, it runs offline stereo rather than online, and it has no image-based TSDF. The two-Gaussian-per-mixed-pixel idea should be presented as a modern, online re-instantiation of this work, not as a new representation.

threats.title: Capture Stage Matting: Challenges, Approaches, and Solutions for Offline and Real-Time Processing (Droge et al.)
threats.what_overlaps: It explicitly exploits the static background of multi-camera capture stages (40 cameras) by using an empty-stage reference as the background plate for matting, offline and in real time, and feeds the alpha into a NeRF reconstruction. This is the ideator's key insight that a static rig makes matting well posed through a known background.
threats.what_remains_different: The plate is captured once and never updated; the authors note that shadows and reflections cause deviations but do not maintain the background over time. Matting is per view, with no multi-view triangulation of F. Downstream use is offline NeRF, not an online feed-forward two-layer splat renderer. There is no TSDF-driven plate bootstrapping without an empty-scene capture.

threats.title: Real-Time High-Resolution Background Matting (BackgroundMattingV2, Lin et al.)
threats.what_overlaps: This is the canonical real-time 'known background makes matting tractable' method (with Background Matting, CVPR 2020). The proposed 'online matting head taking (I, B, difference)' is essentially BGMv2 conditioning, and BGMv2 is already used in telepresence and multi-view head-capture pipelines.
threats.what_remains_different: It is single-view 2D compositing with a manually captured plate. It has no 3D, no multi-view consistency, no online plate memory and no rendering integration.

threats.title: Guardians of the Hair: Rescuing Soft Boundaries in Depth, Stereo, and Novel Views (HairGuard; Zhang, Mehl, Gross, Schroers et al., DisneyResearch|Studios / ETH)
threats.what_overlaps: It targets hair and soft boundaries in depth-based novel view synthesis explicitly, using the alpha-composition model I = aF + (1-a)B, a depth fixer at soft boundaries, forward warping, a generative painter for disocclusions and a colour fuser. The problem framing (halos and wrong depth at hair under view change) is the same.
threats.what_remains_different: It is single-view, about 95 s per frame and offline. It uses no known background, multi-view rig or temporal memory, and it has no Gaussian or TSDF representation.

threats.title: alphaDepth: Learning Single-Pass Soft Boundary Decomposition for Stereo Conversion (Zhang et al.)
threats.what_overlaps: It predicts layered colour and depth at soft boundaries (hair, defocus) in a single pass, which amounts to per-pixel two-layer FG/BG decomposition with alpha for view synthesis. This is the learned version of the two-layer mixed-pixel idea, and it came out four months before now.
threats.what_remains_different: It is single-view stereo conversion with no known background, no multi-view calibrated rig and no temporal or online memory. It solves the ill-posed natural-matting case with priors, whereas the cluster uses the rig's background memory. It is the strongest baseline the idea must beat on boundary bands.

threats.title: A Multi-Layer System for Ultra-High-Resolution Static 360-Degree Telepresence (Chi, Bruder, Neumann, Cruz-Neira, Reiners)
threats.what_overlaps: This telepresence system keeps a static ultra-high-resolution background layer and composites dynamic people over it using real-time BGMv2 background matting. It argues explicitly that telepresence scenes are static enough to get a clean plate for free. The 'static-rig background plate + online matting for telepresence' framing is taken here.
threats.what_remains_different: It is 2D panoramic (8K 360 plus PTZ) with no 3D novel-view synthesis, and its background is stitched offline rather than kept as an online per-camera colour+depth memory. It has no two-layer 3D mixed-pixel representation and no TSDF.

threats.title: DART: Depth-Enhanced Accurate and Real-Time Background Matting
threats.what_overlaps: Real-time RGB-D background matting that uses a background depth prior (Bayesian refinement) plus a known background, at 125 FPS on a desktop GPU. This covers the 'colour+depth background plate drives alpha' component on RGB-D sensors.
threats.what_remains_different: It is single-view 2D matting with a fixed prior. It does not update the plate from TSDF visibility and does no multi-view rendering or two-layer unprojection.

threats.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis (Elmieh et al.)
threats.what_overlaps: A persistent long-horizon memory used in real time to reconstruct temporarily occluded regions in dynamic NVS. It pre-empts the 'reuse long-term observed background for disocclusion filling' contribution in spirit.
threats.what_remains_different: Its memory is implicit (TTT fast weights), not an explicit per-camera colour+depth+staleness plate, and it is not used for matting or mixed-pixel alpha.

threats.title: Ray tracing-based construction of 3D background model for real-time stereoscopic rendering of live immersive video
threats.what_overlaps: Per the search snippet (full text was behind a redirect and not read), it incrementally builds a 'probable background surface' mesh from live video and renders a probable background image each frame to reduce disocclusions in real-time 3D warping. This is prior art for the explicit, incrementally accumulated background memory used for disocclusion filling.
threats.what_remains_different: It has no matting or alpha, no two-layer mixed pixels and no learned blending. Its details, such as its multi-camera setup, are unverified.

threats.title: CPSL: Representing Volumetric Video via Content-Promoted Scene Layers
threats.what_overlaps: A layered 2.5D volumetric-video representation with soft alpha bands at layer boundaries and a cross-frame edge-depth cache, rendered in real time with alpha compositing.
threats.what_remains_different: It uses saliency and depth layering, not known-background matting, with no multi-view rig fusion or TSDF, and it does not target hair.

threats.title: Tele360: Real-Time Feed-Forward Human Reconstruction from Sparse Unposed Cameras
threats.what_overlaps: A real-time telepresence human reconstruction method that relies on foreground masks and admits sensitivity to matting quality (boundary jitter).
threats.what_remains_different: It uses no alpha or two-layer representation and no background memory. It helps motivate the problem rather than threatening the idea.

novelty.remaining_novel_angle: The first two parts of the core insight are already established. (1) A known background makes matting tractable: Background Matting and BGMv2 (2020-21), DART (RGB-D, 2024), and Capture Stage Matting (2025), which does this explicitly for multi-camera stages. (2) Two-layer boundary-matted representations remove halos and flying pixels in multi-view video view synthesis: Zitnick et al. SIGGRAPH 2004 and Hasinoff et al. 2006, with learned single-view versions in HairGuard (Jan 2026) and alphaDepth (May 2026). A static-background layer with real-time BGMv2 for telepresence also appears at ISMAR 2026, though only in 2D. What remains defensible is a narrower claim: a self-bootstrapped, continuously maintained per-camera colour+depth+staleness background memory, written only where the image-based TSDF says the ray sees at or behind the stored background. It needs no empty-scene capture and handles lighting drift and memory invalidation. One explicit memory serves three consumers inside an online, feed-forward, calibrated multi-view temporal IBR pipeline: known-background matting with multi-view triangulation of F, two-Gaussian mixed-pixel forward splatting, and disocclusion filling with real previously observed content. The alpha-weighted, soft-occupancy image-based TSDF, which stops hair from being fused into a hard surface in Starline-style ray-march fusion, is the most technically distinct sub-component; no search found it. The paper should frame itself as closing the 20-year gap between offline boundary matting for view synthesis and online, rig-based splat IBR. It must beat alphaDepth/HairGuard-style learned soft-boundary decomposition and a BGMv2-with-fixed-plate baseline, and show boundary-band and temporal gains that a static plate cannot give, such as under lighting drift or moved furniture. Novelty rests on the online memory-maintenance and soft-TSDF mechanisms plus the evaluation, not on the 'static rig makes matting well posed' observation, which is not new.
novelty.best_variant: The cluster contains only one idea, so the choice is which sub-components to foreground. The most defensible combination pairs (a) the TSDF-gated online background memory, bootstrapped without an empty-scene plate, robust to lighting drift and able to invalidate stale content, with (b) the alpha-weighted soft-occupancy image-based TSDF. Neither has a direct precedent in the works found: Capture Stage Matting uses a fixed plate, NSTM an implicit memory, and the 2023 VR probable-background work does no matting. The two-Gaussian mixed-pixel unprojection and 'known background makes matting well posed' should be presented as enabling re-instantiations of Zitnick 2004 and BGMv2, not as headline contributions. Disocclusion filling from memory should appear as a secondary benefit with an NSTM comparison.

sharpened.title: Plate Memory: Visibility-Gated Background Memory and Soft-Occupancy Fusion for Online Hair-Faithful Multi-View Telepresence
sharpened.one_liner: In a fixed telepresence rig, a per-camera colour+depth background memory that the pipeline builds and maintains by itself turns online matting at silhouettes into a known-background problem. Two-layer alpha splatting and an alpha-weighted soft-occupancy image-based TSDF then remove halos, flying pixels and 'helmet hair' without an empty-scene capture, and the pipeline reports which pixels come from real past observations and which are hallucinated.
sharpened.core_claim: On fixed-rig multi-view sequences, a self-bootstrapped memory is maintained by writing only where the image-based TSDF shows the ray sees at or behind the stored surface, completing it across views by depth reprojection, and invalidating it through staleness and a gain model. Feeding that memory into known-background matting, two-Gaussian mixed-pixel splatting and a soft-occupancy TSDF has four falsifiable consequences. (i) Boundary-band LPIPS (a 10-px silhouette band) falls by at least 10% relative and boundary flicker (tOF/tLP in the band) by at least 20% relative, compared with the base geometry-guided pipeline retrained on the same data, at no more than +15 ms per frame. (ii) Both beat a fixed empty-scene-plate BGMv2 variant and a per-frame learned soft-boundary decomposition (alphaDepth-style) on the same backbone. (iii) Under lighting drift or a moved background object, alpha SAD degrades by less than half as much as with the fixed plate. (iv) Memory-filled disoccluded pixels have higher PSNR than blend-net hallucination. The claim is false if the retrained base blend net already closes more than half of the boundary-band gap to an oracle-alpha two-layer render.
sharpened.key_insight: A static rig does make matting well posed; that part is known from BGMv2, DART and Capture Stage Matting. The unsolved part is where the plate comes from and when it can be trusted, online, while a person occupies the scene. The geometry-guided pipeline already has what it needs to answer both. Its per-view TSDF ray-march gives a visibility test that decides whether a background write is safe. Its calibrated multi-view depth lets one camera fill another camera's plate behind the head, so the plate bootstraps in seconds even when the subject barely moves. The same explicit memory then serves three consumers: alpha estimation, the background layer of each mixed pixel, and disocclusion fill with real past content. Because it is explicit, it also yields a per-pixel provenance map (observed now, observed earlier with its age, or hallucinated). Implicit memories such as NSTM cannot provide that map, and it matters for trust in telepresence.
sharpened.method: (1) Plate memory per camera: colour, depth, confidence and last-seen timestamp at input resolution. A write at pixel u happens only if the TSDF-rendered foreground depth at u is in front of the observed depth by margin δ, or no foreground exists and the observed depth is at or behind the stored depth. Cross-view completion forward-warps confident background samples from other cameras using the stored depth. Lighting drift is handled by a per-camera, per-tile affine gain/offset fitted online on confidently static pixels. Invalidation uses a depth or colour residual test with hysteresis, plus a staleness decay on confidence. The cost is about 2-3 ms for 4-8 cameras on the GPU. (2) Matting head: a BGMv2-style two-stage network. A low-resolution coarse pass takes (I, B, |I-B|, depth-edge map, plate confidence), and full-resolution patch refinement runs only inside the uncertainty band, predicting α and F. A cross-view consistency term triangulates F by projecting the foreground estimate into neighbouring views. When plate confidence is low the head falls back to its natural-matting prior, and it is trained with plate-dropout augmentation so that it has learned that fallback. (3) Two-layer unprojection: pixels with 0<α<1 emit a foreground Gaussian (colour F, opacity α, depth refined by the temporal filter) and a background Gaussian (colour B, opacity 1, depth taken from memory). Pixels with α≈1 or α≈0 behave as in the base paper. Mixed pixels are only about 3-8% of pixels, which keeps splat overhead small. (4) Soft-occupancy image-based TSDF: SDF samples are weighted by α, and each ray accumulates fuzzy opacity 1-Π(1-α_i). A surface zero-crossing is declared only where the accumulated opacity is above τ. Below τ, hair is rendered as the alpha layer and is not snapped to a hard surface, and the previous-frame depth feedback uses α-weighted depth. (5) Blend net: the base 4-level U-Net gains the extra input channels α, plate render, plate confidence and staleness. It composites foreground over the memory background and predicts its own background image only where plate confidence is low. It also outputs a provenance map. (6) Training: synthetic multi-view composites of strand-hair humans over captured or HDR backgrounds, which provide ground-truth α, F and B and layered depth. The real data are DNA-Rendering and MVHumanNet++ with self-supervised composition loss (I≈αF+(1-α)B using the memory plate), plus end-to-end held-out-view rendering loss with boundary-band weighting and a TSDF-reprojected temporal alpha consistency loss. The runtime target is at most +15 ms over the base 40-100 ms per frame on an RTX 4090 at 1080p with 4-8 views.
sharpened.why_not_engineering: The paper makes a testable claim about how information flows between the parts of the pipeline. Geometry-derived visibility is the missing supervision signal that makes an online known-background prior self-maintaining. When that prior is available, a two-layer alpha representation plus soft-occupancy fusion fixes an artifact class that learned blending cannot fix, because an opaque single-depth Gaussian discards the mixed-pixel information before the blend net ever sees it. The paper backs this with an oracle-alpha upper-bound analysis, a coverage and bootstrapping analysis (how quickly the plate converges as a function of subject motion and the number of views), a failure analysis stratified by foreground-background colour contrast, and a soft-TSDF formulation with no found precedent. It also contributes a real ground-truth-alpha multi-view hair benchmark captured with two backgrounds (triangulation matting), which does not currently exist for telepresence rigs.
sharpened.differentiation: Zitnick et al. SIGGRAPH 2004: offline stereo, Bayesian boundary matting, static LDI layers, no temporal memory. We re-instantiate their boundary layer online on Gaussians and add a known-background memory. BGMv2 (CVPR 2021) and DART (2024): single-view, fixed hand-captured plate, no 3D. We use them as components and baselines. Capture Stage Matting (2507.07623): a fixed empty-stage plate that is never updated, per-view matting, offline NeRF. We need no empty capture and maintain, complete across views and invalidate the plate online. ISMAR 2026 multi-layer 360 telepresence (2608.05570): a 2D panoramic static layer with BGMv2 and no 3D novel view synthesis. HairGuard (2601.03362) and alphaDepth (2606.00386): single-view learned soft-boundary decomposition, which is the ill-posed natural case. We show the rig's memory beats these priors, particularly under temporal evaluation, and include alphaDepth-style decomposition as a baseline. NSTM (2607.15271): implicit fast-weight memory at low resolution with no matting and no provenance. Ours is explicit, at full resolution and auditable. The 2023 VR probable-background mesh (Springer 10.1007/s10055-023-00921-w): background accumulation for disocclusion only, with no alpha or matting. Base paper (2505.18932): opaque isotropic pixel Gaussians and a hard TSDF. We change the representation at mixed pixels, and the soft TSDF also gives its weak TSDF ablation a reason to matter.

experiments.capture_notes: Public multi-view datasets supply rendering GT at held-out cameras and a static background, so the main rendering claims can be tested without capture. None provides real ground-truth alpha, lighting-drift events or moved-background events on a telepresence-like rig, however. A small custom set is needed for two things. The first is a real-alpha benchmark: 4-8 synced cameras such as Orbbec Femto Bolt or ZED X units, or machine-vision cameras with hardware sync, plus a large monitor or two switchable coloured backdrops, with near-static subjects captured against two backgrounds for triangulation-matting alpha on hair and fur. The second is 2-5 minute conversational sessions with scripted light dimming, a moved chair and a person walking behind. Budget roughly $3-8k in hardware and 3-4 weeks of capture and calibration. The synthetic strand-hair data can be generated in Blender and covers training and alpha-GT metrics in the meantime. Release the capture as a benchmark to strengthen the paper.

review.first_two_week_test: This is a training-free go/no-go test on DyNeRF (2-3 scenes) and a CMU Panoptic or DNA-Rendering sequence, using the base-paper protocol with held-out rig cameras. Week 1, the memory-premise test: build per-camera plates online. Gating uses per-view depth from any off-the-shelf stereo or MVS model, and the TSDF can be replaced with a simple multi-view depth-consistency test. Add cross-view completion. Measure plate coverage of the 10-px silhouette band over time, then run pretrained BGMv2 with (a) the online plate, (b) a temporal-median plate and (c) no plate (a pretrained RVM/MatAnyone-class model). Visually and quantitatively check alpha stability (flicker energy) in the band. Week 2, the representation test: implement opaque single-layer vs two-layer alpha forward splatting (a pure CUDA or PyTorch splat) into held-out views with simple depth-weighted compositing. Then train only the base-style 4-level blend U-Net for about one day on the same data with and without α/plate channels, including an oracle variant that uses the best available alpha. Report band LPIPS and band flicker for opaque+blendnet vs two-layer+blendnet vs oracle. Go if the online plate reaches at least 80% band coverage within about 10 s (with cross-view completion), and if two-layer+blendnet improves band LPIPS by at least 8% relative and band flicker by at least 15% over opaque+blendnet, with the online plate closing at least half of the gap to oracle alpha.
review.kill_criteria: Drop the direction, or reduce it to a short workshop or IEEE VR poster, if any of the following hold. (1) Even with oracle or triangulation-quality alpha, the two-layer representation improves held-out-view band LPIPS by less than 5% relative over the retrained opaque base pipeline, meaning the learned blend net already hides mixed-pixel errors and the representation change does not matter. (2) The self-maintained plate reaches less than 70% band coverage after 10-20 s on realistic telepresence sequences, even with cross-view completion, so the memory premise fails in practice. (3) The online plate gives no measurable gain in alpha SAD or band flicker over a strong plate-free video matting model such as MatAnyone/RVM-class, or over alphaDepth-style per-frame decomposition. (4) The overhead of the full system exceeds about 25 ms per frame at 1080p with 4-8 views and cannot be reduced. (5) A 2026 paper appears that does visibility-gated online plate maintenance for multi-view splat IBR. Before committing, re-run a novelty check with the search budget restored, because the check for this report was cut short by rate limits.

reviewer_objections.objection: This is Zitnick et al. 2004 (boundary layer) plus BGMv2 (known-background matting) plus Starline-style TSDF, composed. It is a systems paper, not a research contribution.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Two-layer boundaries and known-background matting are presented explicitly as re-instantiated prior art. The claimed contributions are (a) online visibility-gated plate maintenance with cross-view completion and invalidation, which needs no empty capture (Capture Stage Matting uses a fixed plate), and (b) the soft-occupancy image-based TSDF, for which no precedent was found. Both are isolated by ablations (visibility gating vs temporal median, soft vs hard TSDF) and bounded by an oracle-alpha analysis. The paper also compares directly against a reimplemented Zitnick-style boundary layer and against a fixed-plate BGMv2 variant.

reviewer_objections.objection: The learned blend net in the base paper already suppresses halos, and full-image PSNR barely moves. The gain is cosmetic.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: The base paper's own ablations show that full-frame PSNR hardly responds to geometry changes (31.16 vs 31.17), so we pre-register boundary-band and temporal metrics and add a 2AFC user study. The oracle-alpha experiment shows how much the opaque representation loses. The blend net cannot recover mixed-pixel information that single-depth opaque Gaussians have already destroyed before it sees them, and the ablation with α/plate inputs added to the blend net makes this concrete.

reviewer_objections.objection: The static-background assumption is fragile. Real rooms have lighting changes, moving objects, screens and people walking behind.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: The target is the fixed booth or desk rig, the main telepresence deployment. Robustness is made a measured axis rather than an assumption: gain modelling, residual-based invalidation with hysteresis, staleness decay and plate-dropout training that falls back to a natural-matting prior. The paper reports degradation and recovery curves under scripted light and prop changes, with ENeRF-Outdoor as a stress test, and states the failure regime honestly.

reviewer_objections.objection: There is no real ground-truth alpha, so the matting claims rest on synthetic data, and public multi-view datasets (DyNeRF, DNA-Rendering) do not isolate hair.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: A small real benchmark captured on the rig by two-background triangulation matting gives real GT alpha for hair, fur and eyewear, and it will be released. Public datasets are used for held-out-view rendering metrics on hair-segmented boundary bands. Synthetic strand-hair data is used only for training and for alpha metrics.

reviewer_objections.objection: Difference matting fails when foreground and background colours match (dark hair on a dark wall), which is exactly where hair is hardest.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Results are stratified by foreground-background colour contrast. In that regime the method combines depth-edge cues, multi-view triangulation of F and the learned natural-matting prior, and the analysis shows it degrades gracefully to at least the plate-free baseline rather than below it. The plate-confidence channel lets the network down-weight the difference cue where it is uninformative.
