review.venue: A CVPR/ICCV/3DV paper if the go/no-go test shows clear band-LPIPS and flicker gains and the real-alpha benchmark is released. SIGGRAPH Asia / TOG only with a polished live system demo. IEEE VR / ISMAR / TVCG is the realistic fallback, and a strong one, especially with the user study and provenance map, because the telepresence audience values fringe and flicker quality and auditable hallucination.
review.synergies: (1) Disocclusion inpainting (e.g., the Bonn real-time transformer inpainter, 2603.05507) and diffusion-fixer directions: the provenance map tells a fixer where to act, and memory-filled regions give it real conditioning, which yields a stronger joint paper on authentic vs hallucinated pixels. (2) Long-horizon memory and drift (NSTM-style hybrids): the explicit plate is the static half of a hybrid explicit+learned memory, and minute-scale MVHumanNet++ evaluation serves both. (3) Streaming and compression: the static plate is sent once and only foreground plus the alpha band is streamed per frame, a direct bandwidth win for telepresence and a natural second paper. (4) Foundation-stereo / sensor-depth directions: better per-view depth sharpens visibility gating, and the soft TSDF gives them a fuzzy-geometry output. (5) Human-prior and region-aware enhancement for hair, hands and eyes: the alpha band is the natural region mask for spending an identity-prior budget. (6) A telepresence benchmark effort: the real-alpha hair set plus lighting and prop-change splits slot directly into a unified online-telepresence benchmark with temporal and boundary metrics.

cited_work_check.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis (NSTM)
cited_work_check.note: It exists (Jul 2026). The TTT inner loss is an L2 key-to-value binding on the current input-view tokens, updated every 2 frames (58 ms memorise, 27 ms synthesise). It does not use gradient supervision from held-out rig cameras and does not adapt the renderer's slow weights, so the ideator's 'memorises content, not correcting the renderer' is fair. It is still the closest 2026 'online TTT for multi-view dynamic NVS' system, and reviewers will ask how the two differ.

cited_work_check.title: TTT3R: 3D Reconstruction as Test-Time Training
cited_work_check.note: ICLR 2026, Chen et al. It is a training-free, closed-form, confidence-gated state update for CUT3R, with no rendering objective and no multi-camera rig. Characterised correctly.

cited_work_check.title: Instant Gaussian Stream (IGS)
cited_work_check.note: CVPR 2025. It uses an anchor-driven motion network plus key-frame refinement at about 2 s/frame, and is not continual adaptation of a real-time renderer. Characterised correctly.

cited_work_check.title: 3DGStream
cited_work_check.note: CVPR 2024. It optimises Gaussians per frame (about 12 s/frame) and appeared in the search results. Characterised correctly.

cited_work_check.title: Geometry-guided Online 3D Video Synthesis with Multi-View Temporal Consistency (base)
cited_work_check.note: This is the base paper, with frozen networks. The CVPR 2025 poster page appeared in the search results.

threats.title: Continual Adaptation for Deep Stereo (MADNet / MAD++; CVPR 2019 'Real-time self-adaptive deep stereo', extended in TPAMI)
threats.what_overlaps: The deployment-time paradigm itself: a real-time network continually adapts online, without labels, from self-supervision in the deployment stream (photometric warping between rig cameras). It adapts only part of the network (modular) to fit the latency budget, and later work adds handling of forgetting and domain change. The ideator does not cite this, and it is the canonical prior art for 'the system gets better the longer it runs'. Federated Online Adaptation for Deep Stereo (arXiv 2405.14873, 2024) continues the line.
threats.what_remains_different: Its task is stereo disparity only. The self-supervision is left-to-right reprojection, not novel-view rendering from held-out cameras. There is no blending or TSDF renderer and no analysis of extrapolation to off-rig views.

threats.title: IBRNet: Learning Multi-View Image-Based Rendering (per-scene fine-tuning by treating one input view as target)
threats.what_overlaps: The core supervision signal: fine-tune a generalisable image-based-rendering blending network on a new scene with its own captured views, holding one out as target and using the rest as sources. The same objective is used for pretraining and adaptation. Deep Blending (SIGGRAPH Asia 2018) likewise learns blend weights from held-out real photos. Leave-one-view-out rendering self-supervision is therefore not new.
threats.what_remains_different: It fine-tunes offline, once per static scene, taking hours. It is not continual or streaming, has no dynamic content, forgetting safeguards, or latency decoupling, and does not adapt geometry through a fused TSDF.

threats.title: LookinGood: Enhancing Performance Capture with Real-time Neural Re-Rendering
threats.what_overlaps: It mounts extra 'witness' cameras on a live telepresence or performance-capture rig. They are excluded from the real-time pipeline and serve as self-supervised ground truth for the neural re-renderer. This is the telepresence-specific version of 'the rig's spare cameras are free novel-view targets'. LookinGood-pi (arXiv 2112.08037) makes it person-independent.
threats.what_remains_different: The witness cameras are used only for offline training (per person in v1), not for continual adaptation at deployment. The re-renderer is a 2D post-process, and the geometry is not adapted.

threats.title: Fast Spatial Memory with Elastic Test-Time Training (FSM / ETTT)
threats.what_overlaps: It stabilises continual test-time-training updates for 4D reconstruction and novel-view/novel-time rendering against catastrophic forgetting with a Fisher-weighted elastic (EWC) prior around an EMA anchor. This pre-empts the 'EWC + EMA forgetting safeguard' component of the proposed recipe.
threats.what_remains_different: It is LaCT-style fast-weight memory inside a large transformer, not adaptation of a deployed geometry-guided renderer's slow weights. Its supervision is not held-out rig cameras, and it studies no installation or long-horizon deployment.

threats.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic NVS (NSTM)
threats.what_overlaps: It does gradient-based test-time updates during online multi-view dynamic NVS (telepresence-style stereo-pair inputs). Updates are decoupled from the per-frame synthesis path (memorise at a lower rate, synthesise every frame), which is the same idea as the proposed background adaptation thread with hot-swap.
threats.what_remains_different: Its inner loss is key-value binding on input tokens (memory), not photometric loss on held-out real cameras. It is representation-free and low resolution (256-512 px), and there is no correction of the geometry or blending networks or domain-adaptation study.

threats.title: MVS-TTA: Test-Time Adaptation for Multi-View Stereo via Meta-Auxiliary Learning
threats.what_overlaps: Self-supervised test-time adaptation of a learned multi-view depth network with cross-view photometric consistency on calibrated images. It uses meta-auxiliary (MAML-style) training so that a few adaptation steps help, which pre-empts the optional 'meta-trained for adaptation' initialisation.
threats.what_remains_different: It adapts per scene on static MVS. It is not continual or streaming, has no renderer or blend network, and uses no held-out-view rendering loss.

threats.title: Free Geometry: Refining 3D Reconstruction from Longer Versions of Itself
threats.what_overlaps: Test-time LoRA adaptation of a feed-forward multi-view reconstruction model. It masks a subset of views and supervises the partial-view model with the full-view model (a leave-some-views-out self-supervised task).
threats.what_remains_different: Its consistency losses are at feature and geometry level, not a rendering loss. Adaptation is one-off (under 2 minutes per dataset), not continual, and covers static scenes with no renderer.

threats.title: Self-Geometry: GT-Free Plug-and-Play TTA for 3D Vision Foundation Models
threats.what_overlaps: Ground-truth-free test-time adaptation of geometry foundation models with multi-view and epipolar consistency as supervision.
threats.what_remains_different: It does geometry only, per scene, with no streaming, rendering or deployment loop.

threats.title: Reconstruct, Inpaint, Test-Time Finetune (CogNVS)
threats.what_overlaps: Self-supervised test-time fine-tuning of a novel-view synthesis model on the target video.
threats.what_remains_different: It works on monocular video, is offline, uses a diffusion inpainter, and has no multi-camera held-out supervision or real-time loop.

novelty.remaining_novel_angle: None of the searched work does this. The pretrained models of a real-time, feed-forward, geometry-guided multi-view dynamic renderer (depth network plus blend network, adapted through a differentiable image-based TSDF) are adapted continually at deployment, for minutes to hours, from photometric loss on spare, time-synced rig cameras held out of the render set. Adaptation runs in a background thread decoupled from the latency-critical path. Each piece is established on its own: leave-one-view-out rendering supervision (IBRNet, Deep Blending), witness cameras as self-supervised targets on a telepresence rig (LookinGood, offline only), continual online self-supervised adaptation of a real-time depth network (MADNet/MAD++), EWC/EMA-stabilised continual TTT (FSM 2026), meta-learned TTA for MVS (MVS-TTA 2025) and decoupled update and render rates (NSTM 2026). The core insight that spare rig cameras are free targets for continual adaptation is therefore not new as a principle. What remains defensible and publishable is empirical and systems-level. (1) A study of whether and when adaptation supervised by interpolated in-rig views transfers to extrapolated, off-rig viewpoints, and when it hurts them, plus the cycle-consistency or virtual-view regulariser that makes it transfer. (2) Gradient flow into geometry through a soft image-based TSDF, so that specular or outdoor depth errors are corrected by the rendering loss rather than by stereo reprojection alone. (3) A long-horizon deployment benchmark and protocol that reports quality over time, forgetting, change of person or scene, and a camera held out from both adaptation and evaluation. The paper should cite MADNet, IBRNet, Deep Blending and LookinGood prominently and frame itself as bringing continual self-adaptation from stereo to full novel-view rendering. It should not claim that self-supervision from spare cameras is new.
novelty.best_variant: The cluster contains a single idea, 'The Rig Is Its Own Teacher'. Its most defensible sub-contributions are (i) the interpolation-to-extrapolation transfer analysis with the off-rig cycle-consistency regulariser, and (ii) adapting geometry through a differentiable image-based TSDF under a rendering loss. Neither was found in prior work, and together they separate the paper from MADNet-style stereo self-adaptation and IBRNet-style per-scene fine-tuning. Replay, EWC, EMA-teacher and MAML initialisation should be presented as engineering borrowed from continual learning (FSM/ETTT, Online-LoRA, MVS-TTA), not as contributions. The long-horizon deployment benchmark is a useful secondary contribution, but it needs a camera excluded from both adaptation and evaluation. DyNeRF and ENeRF-Outdoor already use their spare cameras for evaluation, so the protocol has to be redesigned, for example on rigs with 15+ cameras such as DNA-Rendering or PackUV.

sharpened.title: Does the Rig Teach Beyond Itself? Continual Held-Out-Camera Adaptation of Real-Time Geometry-Guided 3D Video, and When It Transfers Off-Rig
sharpened.one_liner: A deployed multi-camera renderer adapts its depth and blending networks online from photometric loss on rig cameras it is not rendering from. We show when this self-supervision on interpolated views transfers to extrapolated, off-rig viewpoints, when it hurts them, and that a rendering loss sent through a soft image-based TSDF corrects geometry better than MADNet-style stereo reprojection adaptation.
sharpened.core_claim: Setup: out-of-domain rigs (ENeRF-Outdoor, a Panoptic/ActorsHQ dome subset) with three disjoint camera sets: a supervision pool S, unsupervised interpolated cameras E_int inside S's hull, and unsupervised extrapolated cameras E_ext outside it. (1) Continual leave-one-camera-out adaptation of a geometry-guided real-time renderer, with an off-rig cycle regulariser, improves E_int by at least 1.0 dB PSNR and E_ext by at least 0.5 dB PSNR (or at least 10% LPIPS) within 10 minutes of streaming, measured on future frames never replayed. Forgetting on earlier content stays under 0.3 dB after 30 minutes. (2) Naive leave-one-camera-out adaptation without the regulariser improves E_int but gives no significant gain on E_ext, or degrades it. (3) Adapting the depth network with a rendering loss through a differentiable soft image-based TSDF gives higher E_int/E_ext quality than MADNet/MAD++-style stereo reprojection self-adaptation, at equal compute. (4) All three still hold, with smaller gains, when the base model is pretrained on large multi-view human data (DNA-Rendering-scale). Any of (1)-(3) failing falsifies the paper's thesis.
sharpened.key_insight: A fixed rig at deployment has time-synced real images at viewpoints the renderer is not using, so every frame gives task-aligned supervision (rendering a novel view) indefinitely. That signal is known (IBRNet per-scene fine-tuning, LookinGood witness cameras, MADNet online stereo adaptation). What is not known is whether it improves the viewpoints a telepresence viewer actually uses. Those lie off the rig, in the head box in front of the display, where no ground truth exists. There are two insights. (a) Leave-one-camera-out tasks are wider-baseline and more interpolative than deployment queries, so naive adaptation specialises to rig-camera poses. A render-virtual-then-re-render-real cycle, which sends held-out-camera error back through an off-rig virtual view, turns on-rig ground truth into gradient signal for off-rig views. (b) The deployment objective is view quality, not disparity. So supervising the depth network through the soft TSDF puts corrections where depth errors are visible in the render (specular, low-texture, far outdoor background), unlike reprojection losses, which ignore them or reward matching specular highlights.
sharpened.method:
Renderer, a reimplementation of the base paper since no code has been released: per-view depth from a real-time stereo network (Fast-FoundationStereo or Lite Any Stereo V2 class, about 20-50 ms), opaque pixel-sized splats, a soft image-based TSDF, and a 4-level blend U-Net predicting weights plus a background image. The difference-gated temporal depth filter is kept.

Soft TSDF: along each target ray, sample about 32-64 depths. Per-view truncated SDF is tanh((D_n(proj) - z_n)/tau_n), with tau_n learnable and depth-dependent (tau = tau0 + tau1*z^2, which fixes the base paper's fixed 0.02 m). Views are fused with confidence weights, and surface depth is the soft zero-crossing, a NeuS-style logistic-density expectation. This is differentiable with respect to input depths, confidences and tau.

Adapted parameters, under 1M in total: (i) per-camera 3x4 colour affines as a separate nuisance absorber, reported on their own; (ii) rank-8 LoRA on the blend U-Net; (iii) LoRA on the stereo network's final refinement/upsampling head only; (iv) tau0, tau1 and the confidence scale.

Adaptation loop in a background thread: a reservoir replay buffer of (time, all-camera frames) at 1-2 Hz. Each step samples t, a target c in S and inputs = K nearest in S\{c}. Losses: L1 + 0.2 LPIPS on I_c, with a validity mask. Cycle regulariser: render I_v at a virtual pose v sampled in the deployment head box outside S's hull, re-render camera c using {I_v, D_v} plus a reduced source set, then apply L1/LPIPS against real I_c. This sends on-rig error back into the off-rig render. There is also a small EMA-teacher LPIPS anchor at v to limit drift.

Safeguards, presented as borrowed engineering (EWC/EMA as in FSM/ETTT; replay): an L2/EWC prior to the pretrained weights, a sentinel camera never trained on that triggers rollback if its PSNR drops by more than 0.3 dB, and scene/person-change detection that resets the learning-rate warmup.

Runtime: the render path runs in TensorRT fp16 at about 40-60 ms per frame. Adaptation runs at 2-5 steps/s on a low-priority CUDA stream (single-GPU setting) or on a second GPU. LoRA is merged and hot-swapped every 10 s. p50/p99 render latency is reported with and without adaptation.

Pretraining: ScanNet + DyNeRF (the base recipe), plus a scaled variant with DNA-Rendering/MVHumanNet++ for the 'does scale kill TTA' test. Optional MAML-style initialisation is an ablation only.
sharpened.why_not_engineering: The paper is organised around research questions that controlled camera splits can falsify, not around a system. Q1: does self-supervision from on-rig interpolated views transfer to extrapolated off-rig views, and under which baseline or hull geometry? We give an empirical transfer map (gain as a function of the angular distance of an evaluation camera from S's hull). Q2: which supervision signal should adapt geometry for view synthesis, rendering loss through a soft TSDF or stereo reprojection? This is a direct, compute-matched comparison with MADNet/MAD++. Q3: does test-time adaptation still pay once pretraining data scales? Negative and mixed results, such as naive leave-one-camera-out hurting E_ext or colour-only recovering X% of the gain, are reported as findings. The cycle regulariser is the one algorithmic contribution, and its value is measured on E_ext, which no prior streaming NVS work evaluates. If only 'fine-tuning helps on held-out cameras' came out, it would be engineering; the paper stands or falls on Q1 and Q2.
sharpened.differentiation: MADNet/MAD++ (arXiv 2007.05233; CVPR'19/TPAMI) do continual self-adaptation of stereo disparity with reprojection loss. We adapt the full renderer (depth and blending) with a novel-view rendering loss and compare against their loss directly as a baseline arm for the depth network. IBRNet (2102.13090) and Deep Blending hold out a view to fine-tune a blend network offline, once per static scene. We do it continually on dynamic streams with forgetting control and latency decoupling, and study off-rig transfer, which they never evaluate. LookinGood (1811.05029) uses witness cameras on a capture rig for offline training of a 2D re-renderer. We use them for deployment-time adaptation that includes geometry, and add an installation-time variant in which temporary witness cameras are removed after adaptation. NSTM (2607.15271) runs test-time-training memory that binds input-view keys to values at low resolution, decoupled from synthesis. Its loss is memorisation, not held-out-camera photometric error, and it does not adapt geometry. The decoupled-rate idea is shared and credited. FSM/ETTT (2604.07350) is the source of the EWC/EMA stabiliser, which is cited and used, not claimed. MVS-TTA (2511.18120), Free Geometry (2604.14048) and Self-Geometry (2608.10708) do per-scene, geometry-only test-time adaptation with no renderer and no streaming. StreamTTO (2603.01765) does sensor-depth-supervised test-time optimisation and does not render. 3DGStream (2403.01444) and IGS (2503.16979) optimise per frame in seconds and appear as the quality-at-cost ceiling. The paper explicitly does NOT claim that spare-camera self-supervision is new.

experiments.capture_notes: The core claims can be tested on public data. Panoptic Studio and ActorsHQ provide dome cameras outside a frontal telepresence-like supervision arc, which gives real ground truth for extrapolated views. Panoptic also has Kinect depth and multi-minute takes for forgetting and horizon studies, and ENeRF-Outdoor provides the out-of-domain outdoor setting. Public datasets lack deliberate lighting changes, strongly specular props and a real 'installation' (booth, display-mounted cameras, many different users over days). A small 8-12-camera booth capture (machine-vision or synchronized consumer cameras, about USD 5-10k, 1-2 weeks) with lamp or daylight changes and specular objects is recommended for the telepresence story and the installation-time witness-camera variant, but it is not needed to validate the thesis. The base paper has no code release, so a reimplementation (2-3 months) is on the critical path. ENeRF or GPS-Gaussian public code can serve as a stand-in renderer for early experiments.

review.first_two_week_test: Use public ENeRF (generalizable DTU-pretrained checkpoint; differentiable depth plus blending) as a stand-in for the base renderer, and skip the soft TSDF for now. Run on two streams: ENeRF-Outdoor, and one Panoptic HD (or ActorsHQ) sequence. Split cameras into a frontal supervision arc S (about 8 cameras), interleaved unsupervised E_int (2-3) and E_ext (3-4 outside S's hull, at 20-60 degrees beyond it). Simulate streaming offline: a reservoir buffer over the first 60-120 s, leave-one-camera-out adaptation on S, and evaluation only on frames after the adaptation window at E_int and E_ext. Five arms: frozen, colour-affine-only, blend/final-layer LoRA, depth+blend LoRA, and offline full fine-tune (upper bound). Add a 1-day sixth arm: the cycle regulariser with virtual views in a head box. Also run a MADNet-style reprojection-loss arm on the depth module. Cost: about 1 GPU for 2 weeks, 1 student. Success signal: E_int improves by at least 1 dB over frozen AND colour-only on future frames, E_ext shows a positive, non-trivial gain (at least 0.3-0.5 dB or at least 5% LPIPS) with the regulariser, and naive leave-one-camera-out is measurably worse on E_ext than on E_int.
review.kill_criteria: Drop or fold into another project if any of these holds on at least 2 out-of-domain datasets. (a) E_ext gain on future frames stays under 0.3 dB PSNR and under 5% LPIPS after 10 minutes, even with the cycle regulariser: the off-rig transfer thesis fails. (b) Colour-affine-only adaptation recovers at least 70% of the total gain: the result is photometric calibration, not renderer adaptation. (c) Gain on unseen future frames is under 50% of the gain on replayed frames: this is memorisation, NSTM territory. (d) With DNA-Rendering/MVHumanNet-scale pretraining the gain collapses below 0.3 dB: scale beats test-time adaptation, so publish as a short negative-result or workshop paper at most. (e) Rendering-loss depth adaptation through the soft TSDF is not better than compute-matched MADNet-style reprojection adaptation. In that case drop the geometry claim, and the paper collapses to blend-network fine-tuning, which is not publishable at a top venue. Also kill if the 30-minute forgetting exceeds 0.5 dB despite the safeguards, since then a deployed system cannot use it.

reviewer_objections.objection: Not novel: leave-one-view-out fine-tuning is IBRNet/Deep Blending, witness cameras are LookinGood, and online self-supervised adaptation of real-time depth is MADNet/MAD++. This is a combination of known pieces.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Agreed on the signal, and the paper says so in the introduction and cites all of them prominently. The contributions are findings none of them report: (i) the interpolation-to-extrapolation transfer map on real off-rig ground truth, showing naive leave-one-camera-out does not transfer and the cycle regulariser does; (ii) a compute-matched head-to-head showing that a rendering loss through a soft TSDF corrects geometry better for view synthesis than MADNet's reprojection loss; (iii) a deployment protocol with disjoint supervision, interpolation and extrapolation camera sets and forgetting over time. The prior works are run as baseline arms, not just discussed.

reviewer_objections.objection: The gains are just colour calibration or white balance, or overfitting to the current person or pose.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Colour-affine-only adaptation is a separate baseline and the paper reports the fraction of gain it explains. All evaluation is on future frames never in the replay buffer. Subject-change streams (DNA-Rendering sequences concatenated) measure both retention and speed of re-adaptation. Kill criterion (b) was set in advance.

reviewer_objections.objection: Held-out rig cameras are near the supervision cameras, so interpolated gains are trivial. The viewpoints that matter in telepresence are off-rig, where you have no ground truth.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: This is the central question of the paper. Dome datasets (Panoptic HD, ActorsHQ) let us supervise with a frontal telepresence-like arc and evaluate on real cameras 20-60 degrees outside its hull. We plot gain against angular distance from the hull and report where it turns negative. The E_ext result is the headline, not E_int.

reviewer_objections.objection: Real telepresence booths do not have spare cameras, and adaptation steals GPU time from a latency-critical renderer.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Leave-one-camera-out needs only N = K+1, and we sweep |S| from 4 to 12. In an installation-time witness-camera variant, extra cameras are present only for the first minutes and then removed, and we measure retained gain. For compute, we report p50/p99 render latency with adaptation on a low-priority stream on the same GPU, plus dB per adaptation GPU-second, and compare with 3DGStream/IGS, which spend seconds per frame.

reviewer_objections.objection: Why not simply pretrain on more data (DNA-Rendering, MVHumanNet++)? Test-time adaptation gains usually vanish with scale.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We include a scaled-pretraining variant and report the remaining gain honestly. The expected residual is installation-specific: lighting, the camera ISP, backgrounds, specular props and outdoor far-field depth, which no pretraining set covers. If the gain collapses, that is a kill criterion, not something to hide.

effort.months: 8-10 (2-3 months reimplementing the base pipeline plus the soft TSDF, since no code is released; 1 month stand-in ENeRF study; 3-4 months adaptation loop, protocol and experiments; 1 month writing and demo)
effort.people: 2 (one PhD student on the renderer and differentiable TSDF, one on the adaptation loop and benchmark protocol), with part-time advisor support
effort.compute: 2-4 GPUs of 24-80 GB for about 3-4 GPU-weeks of pretraining (more for the scaled DNA-Rendering/MVHumanNet variant, about 2-3 GPU-weeks extra). Adaptation experiments are cheap (1 GPU per stream, real-time or faster in offline simulation). Optional 8-12-camera booth rig at USD 5-10k.

review.venue: ICCV 2027 (main track; deadline about March 2027). Fallback: 3DV 2027, or ISMAR 2027 (TVCG journal track) if the paper leans on the installation-time booth study and latency measurements. CVPR 2027 (November 2026 deadline) is too early given the reimplementation.
review.synergies: C09 (a learnable recursive, differentiable image-TSDF trained over video): the same soft-TSDF module is shared, so build it once. C09 gives a principled fusion state, and C08 gives the deployment-time signal that tunes it (tau, confidences). Together they make a stronger joint or two-paper series. C05 (off-rig self-forcing with 4D/video diffusion priors): the most natural merge. Real held-out cameras supervise on the rig, and a distilled generative prior regularises off the rig, replacing or complementing the cycle loss. 'Real teacher on-rig, prior teacher off-rig' is a compelling unified story if C08's E_ext gains alone are modest. C03 (deadline-aware benchmark with long takes and moving/binocular ground truth): the disjoint S/E_int/E_ext split and forgetting-over-time protocol can become a track of that benchmark. C06 (specular robustness): test-time adaptation of depth through a rendering loss is a data-driven complement to explicit two-layer reflection models, and the specular-region masks and metrics can be shared. C02 (perceptual consistency metric): improves the evaluation of flicker introduced by weight hot-swaps. C01 (unsynchronized consumer rigs): held-out-camera photometric loss can also adapt the sync offsets and colour calibration online.

name: Principled learnable recursive geometry state: motion-compensated Bayesian image-TSDF, stability/contraction analysis, differentiable TSDF trained over video

cited_work_check.title: TTT3R: 3D Reconstruction as Test-Time Training (ICLR 2026)
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed. It gives a closed-form, confidence-derived learning rate for CUT3R state updates that fixes length generalisation. Single moving camera, no rendering.

cited_work_check.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis (NSTM)
cited_work_check.note: Exists, and 'implicit state, no explicit geometry' is right. 'No stability analysis' is mischaracterised. NSTM runs a memory stress test over time, reports degradation at T=4/30/60 (LaCT drops 5.47 dB), has a long-horizon-stability ablation (L2 vs dot-product loss), adds a memory-caching regulariser against weight drift, and admits primacy bias. What it lacks is formal theory and flicker/JOD metrics, which it does not report.

cited_work_check.title: Self Forcing (NeurIPS 2025)
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: on-policy autoregressive rollout training for video diffusion.

cited_work_check.title: GeoStream (2026)
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed, but the ideator understates it. GeoStream names a 'second-order geometric feedback loop': errors propagate through the depth estimator into reprojections and compound over time. It trains fully on-policy, rendering the geometric conditioning from the model's own outputs. That is the same train/test-mismatch argument idea 2 makes, although in generative video.

cited_work_check.title: GRVS: Generalizable and Recurrent Monocular Dynamic View Synthesis (2026)
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: recurrent, generalisable, monocular. It reuses previously generated renderings.

cited_work_check.title: MoRGS (2026)
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: online per-Gaussian motion reasoning with flow cues, trained by per-frame optimisation.

cited_work_check.title: FUSE-Flow (2026)
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: real-time confidence-based multi-view point-cloud fusion. Its abstract argues against temporal accumulation.

cited_work_check.title: elaTCSF (2025)
cited_work_check.note: Exists and is a flicker-detection TCSF model. The claim that it was 'never used as a training loss' may hold for elaTCSF itself, but TCSF-weighted temporal losses already exist: an NVIDIA patent (US10810455) uses one for denoising. ColorVideoVDP (arXiv 2401.11485) also presents itself as a differentiable spatio-temporal loss.

cited_work_check.title: FrameVGGT (2026)
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: bounded-memory streaming geometry.

cited_work_check.title: Temporally Consistent Stereo Matching / TC-Stereo (ECCV 2024)
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: projects the previous disparity for temporal completion, then refines iteratively. Single stereo pair.

threats.title: FILT3R: Latent State Adaptive Kalman Filter for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
threats.what_overlaps: Recasts the recurrent-state update of streaming 3D reconstruction as Kalman filtering. It keeps a per-element variance and an online-estimated process noise, and the resulting gain shrinks as uncertainty contracts and rises on scene change. The explicit aim is long-horizon stability beyond the training horizon, and overwrite/gating policies are recovered as special cases. This is the conceptual core of ideas 1 and 2: a Kalman gain replacing heuristic gating, justified by stability.
threats.what_remains_different: It filters latent CUT3R tokens from a single moving camera. It has no pixel/image-space depth state, no scene-flow motion compensation, no multi-view TSDF, no rendering or NVS, and no flicker metrics.

threats.title: Temporally Consistent Online Depth Estimation Using Point-Based Fusion (Khan, Penner, Lanman, Xiao; the base paper's group)
threats.what_overlaps: Already replaces a hand-set static/dynamic blend with a learned dynamic mask alpha. It fuses depths in image space with weights from learned aleatoric uncertainty (exp(-Phi)) and carries a persistent global point-cloud state. This removes idea 1's 'learned variance replaces hand-tuned weights' and 'learned gate' claims, and idea 3's 'learned gate'.
threats.what_remains_different: Moving regions simply take the current estimate (no motion-compensated prediction and no Kalman/innovation test). It is monocular or stereo depth only, with no multi-view image-space TSDF, no novel-view rendering, no variance-derived truncation, and no stability analysis.

threats.title: CODD: Temporally Consistent Online Depth Estimation in Dynamic Scenes
threats.what_overlaps: Its motion network predicts per-pixel SE3 transforms (scene flow) that align previous observations, and a learned fusion network then aggregates past and current disparity for temporal consistency in dynamic regions. This is the motion-compensated recursive depth filter of idea 1, including its 'learned ConvGRU gain' variant.
threats.what_remains_different: It works on a single stereo pair with no explicit Gaussian variance or chi-squared innovation gate. It has no cross-camera TSDF fusion, no rendering, and no long-horizon stability study.

threats.title: Rethinking the State Update Gate for Long-Sequence Recurrent 3D Reconstruction
threats.what_overlaps: Profiles the gates of recurrent 3D reconstruction as a memory system and derives an effective memory horizon of about 3 frames per state token from gate magnitudes. It then proposes a principled frame-level gate (a relaxation of keyframe selection) and evaluates on sequences of up to 4,541 frames. This is methodologically close to idea 2's 'ghost half-life from gate/spectral radius' diagnostic.
threats.what_remains_different: It is training-free, uses latent state from a single moving camera, and targets pose and depth rather than rendered appearance. It has no explicit TSDF, no rendered-depth feedback loop, no contraction bound, and no flicker or ghost metrics.

threats.title: TTT3R / TTSA3R / ReCal3R / Mem3R family (confidence-calibrated state updates for streaming reconstruction)
threats.what_overlaps: Together they establish that confidence- or reliability-gated state updates fix long-horizon drift and forgetting, with long-sequence drift curves as the evaluation. Idea 2's 'confidence-gated state update fixes drift' is therefore already the standard recipe.
threats.what_remains_different: All operate on latent tokens for pose and pointmap estimation. None has explicit image-space geometry, rendering, multi-view capture rigs, or formal contraction guarantees.

threats.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis (NSTM)
threats.what_overlaps: Minute-scale online multi-view NVS with an explicit drift-versus-time analysis (T=4/30/60), a memory-stress test, a long-horizon-stability loss ablation, and regularisation against weight drift. Idea 2 would not be the first to evaluate long-horizon drift in online multi-view NVS.
threats.what_remains_different: Its state is implicit TTT fast weights with no explicit geometry. It runs at 256-512 px and evaluates 60 subsampled frames at 1.2 FPS (not real-time frame rates) with no flicker, ghost or TCC metrics. There is no theory.

threats.title: GeoStream: Toward Precise Camera Controlled Streaming Video Generation
threats.what_overlaps: Explicitly identifies a geometric feedback loop: errors in the model's own outputs propagate through depth into reprojected geometry and compound. It fixes this with fully on-policy training in which the geometric conditioning is rendered from the model's own outputs. This takes the 'on-policy training for a geometry feedback loop' element of idea 2.
threats.what_remains_different: It is a generative video model, not faithful multi-view capture. It has no TSDF, no stability theory, and no telepresence rig.

threats.title: Video stereo foundation models: Stereo Any Video, PPMStereo, TC-Stereo
threats.what_overlaps: They deliver temporally consistent per-pair depth with learned temporal memory, which may absorb most of the flicker idea 1 targets. Idea 1 itself flags this.
threats.what_remains_different: None does cross-camera fusion, explicit variance, rendering, or minute-scale stability.

threats.title: Learned depth fusion (NeuralFusion CVPR 2021, RoutedFusion, VisFusion CVPR 2023) + ColorVideoVDP as a differentiable loss (2401.11485) + NVIDIA TCSF temporal-loss patent (US10810455)
threats.what_overlaps: Learned, differentiable TSDF fusion weights already exist for static reconstruction, and a psychophysically grounded spatio-temporal metric (ColorVideoVDP) is marketed as a differentiable training loss. This undercuts idea 3's 'first learned TSDF weights' and 'first perceptual flicker loss' framing.
threats.what_remains_different: None trains an image-space (per-target-ray) TSDF unrolled over video for NVS. None calibrates a telepresence-specific flicker threshold (face, hands, eccentricity, HMD) on real IBR artifacts.

threats.title: Evaluating Human Perception of NVS in Dynamic Scenes (subjective QA of GS/NeRF)
threats.what_overlaps: Human-perception study of temporal quality in dynamic NVS, showing that objective metrics correlate poorly with human judgements.
threats.what_remains_different: Offline methods only, with no HMD flicker-threshold psychophysics, no telepresence-specific artifacts, and no training loss.

novelty.remaining_novel_angle:
Each building block of C09 is already published elsewhere. Kalman-gain state updates for long-horizon stability are taken (FILT3R, ECCV 2026). Motion-compensated recursive depth fusion is taken (CODD). Learned dynamic masks with aleatoric-uncertainty fusion weights are taken, by the base paper's own group (Khan et al., CVPR 2023). Gate-derived memory-horizon analysis is taken (Rethinking the State Update Gate, 2026). On-policy training through a geometric feedback loop is taken (GeoStream). Minute-scale drift analysis for online multi-view NVS is taken (NSTM). Differentiable learned TSDF fusion (NeuralFusion) and differentiable perceptual video losses (ColorVideoVDP) are taken.

What remains defensible is the explicit, pixel-space version for geometry-guided IBR. The state is a closed-loop recursion over (per-camera filtered depth, image-space TSDF weight, re-injected previous novel-view depth). Its posterior variance does three jobs at once: it sets TSDF weights, it sets a depth-dependent truncation, and it supplies a geometric (not photometric) innovation gate that tells motion from relighting. That recursion then gets a provable contraction or ghost-half-life bound that is validated at real frame rates over minutes, with flicker and ghost metrics, under a moving viewer. No found work analyses the feedback of rendered novel-view depth into a fusion state, and none gives stability guarantees for an explicit-geometry online NVS pipeline. A secondary independent angle is a telepresence-specific psychophysical flicker threshold (HMD; face, hands, eccentricity; real IBR artifacts) used both as a metric and as a loss.
novelty.best_variant:
Idea 2 ('Minutes, Not Frames'), merged with idea 1's variance machinery, is the most defensible. Latent-token state filtering and gate-horizon analysis are crowded as of 2026 (FILT3R, TTT3R, ReCal3R, TTSA3R, the gate-rethinking paper), but all of it is for pose and pointmaps from a single moving camera. None of it covers explicit-geometry, calibrated-rig, real-time NVS whose rendered output is fed back into its own geometry state. The contribution should be framed as 'Kalman image-TSDF with a provable contraction and ghost-persistence bound plus a minute-scale flicker and ghost benchmark for online 3D video'. FILT3R, CODD and Khan'23 must be cited and positioned against directly; the paper cannot claim Kalman gating or learned uncertainty fusion as new.

Idea 1 alone is the weakest: it amounts to CODD plus Khan'23 plus a Matthies-Kanade Kalman filter inserted into the base pipeline, and video-stereo foundation models may erase its delta.

Idea 3's differentiable image-space TSDF is only incremental over NeuralFusion-style learned fusion. Its HMD flicker psychophysics metric is novel enough to stand alone as an IEEE VR or TVCG contribution, but its 'first perceptual flicker loss' claim must be dropped given ColorVideoVDP and TCSF-weighted temporal losses.

sharpened.title: Flicker, Lag and Ghosts: Consistent Recursive Geometry State for Minute-Long Online 3D Video
sharpened.one_liner: Keep a motion-compensated Kalman depth posterior in each fixed rig camera and fuse it into the image-space TSDF so that no evidence is counted twice. The result sits on a predictable flicker-lag-ghost Pareto frontier that the base paper's colour-gated EMA plus η-capped novel-view feedback cannot reach.
sharpened.core_claim: We test on minute-long multi-view human sequences (Panoptic Kinect, ActorsHQ/DNA-Rendering with stereo depth, synthetic event-injected Blender sequences) and on held-out and moving virtual cameras. At a matched lag or ghost half-life, the consistent recursive state reduces flicker in the dynamic face and hand regions by at least 25% relative to the base recursion (flow-warped temporal error of both rendered RGB and TSDF depth). It also stays at least 15% better when every pipeline, the stateless baseline included, is given a temporally consistent video-stereo front end. PSNR and LPIPS stay within 0.2 dB / 0.01 of the base, and the added cost is at most 5 ms per frame. Finally, the closed-form ghost half-life and steady-state flicker predicted from (process noise Q, measurement variance R, gate false-negative rate) match the values measured after injected events (lights switched, objects removed, textureless motion) to within ±30%. The base recursion instead shows either under-smoothing (flicker) or overconfidence (persistent ghosts after lighting and occlusion events), depending on β and η. If either of the first two numbers fails, the claim is falsified.
sharpened.key_insight: The base paper's temporal machinery is two uncoordinated recursions. The first is a colour-gated per-camera EMA; its mask floor M ≥ 0.6 means it barely filters, so the moving person gets essentially no smoothing and flickers. The second feeds the previous rendered novel-view depth back into the TSDF with weight up to η = 15 against per-view weights of at most 1. That rendered depth is a deterministic function of the same per-camera measurements already in the TSDF. Feeding it back is therefore 'data incest' (the double counting known from decentralised estimation): it inflates confidence without new information, and that overconfidence is what makes errors persist as ghosts after events a colour mask misses. The state also lives in the moving target view, so it is undefined for a moving viewer or for two eyes. The fix is to put the state where the rig is fixed, in each source camera's pixel grid, as a motion-compensated per-pixel posterior (μ, σ²). One posterior variance then does three jobs: it sets the TSDF weight ω = 1/σ², a per-sample truncation τ = cσ (removing the metric 0.02 m constant), and a geometric χ² innovation gate that separates 'moved' from 're-lit'. The novel-view feedback is either removed or admitted only as a covariance-intersection pseudo-measurement, which provably cannot shrink variance below the per-camera posteriors. The flicker-lag-ghost behaviour of the loop then follows from the steady-state Riccati gain, so it can be predicted and tuned, not hand-set.
sharpened.method:
State: for each fixed rig camera n, a per-pixel posterior (μ_n, σ²_n, age, running innovation statistics) at the depth resolution.

(1) Measurement. Two front ends are used. (a) A fast stereo network (for example RAFT-Stereo-realtime) fine-tuned with a Laplace/Gaussian NLL variance head on synthetic data plus the rig's own data. (b) Sensor depth (Kinect/Orbbec) with a standard depth-dependent noise model σ ∝ z² plus an edge term.

(2) Prediction. Optical flow per camera (RAFT-small or a similar fast flow network) plus the posterior depth gives 3D scene flow. Forward-splat μ and σ² with soft z-buffering. Process noise is Q = q0 + q1·‖scene flow‖² + q2·flow-uncertainty. Disoccluded pixels reset to a prior with σ² = ∞.

(3) Update. Gain K = σ²_pred/(σ²_pred + R). A χ² innovation gate (1 dof, p = 0.99) resets σ² on failure (topology change or occlusion), with a Student-t variant for robustness. Colour change is used only to inflate Q, never to decide which pixels are static.

(4) Image-space TSDF, the Starline/base raymarch kept. Per-sample weight ω_k = 1/σ²_k (clamped), per-sample truncation τ_k = clip(c·σ_k, τmin, τmax), and the returned surface also carries a fused variance σ²_TSDF.

(5) Feedback, three variants: (A) none; (B) the base paper's η-capped feedback, as the reference; (C) covariance intersection of the reprojected previous novel-view depth with the fused per-camera estimate, reprojected through the TSDF depth using the target-camera motion.

(6) Blend U-Net as in the base paper, with σ_TSDF and innovation maps as extra inputs. It is trained on 8-frame clips with the base losses plus a flow-warped temporal L1 (single-instant training is the base paper's gap). The filter itself stays closed-form. A learned-gain ConvGRU (trained on on-policy rollouts) is an ablation, not the headline.

(7) Theory. Per pixel, the loop is a switched linear system x_{t+1} = (1 − K_t)x_t + K_t z_t (+ a feedback term). The steady-state Riccati gain K∞(Q, R) gives ghost half-life h = ln2 / −ln(1 − K∞) and steady-state flicker variance K∞R/(2 − K∞). The same algebra for the base recursion is expressed in terms of (mask floor, β, η, Σω_k, mask false-negative rate p). A proposition shows that without covariance intersection (CI) the feedback fraction η/(η + Σω_k) acts as a positive-feedback confidence term, with persistence growing as p → 1. With CI the loop is contractive, with spectral radius ≤ 1 − K_min.

Runtime budget: flow at quarter resolution plus splatting of the posterior plus the update is about 3-5 ms for 4 views at 1352x1014 on an RTX 4090-class GPU, against about 40 ms for the base pipeline with TensorRT. Depth estimation is reported separately and honestly, unlike in the base paper.
sharpened.why_not_engineering: The contribution is not 'we inserted a Kalman filter'. It rests on three things. (i) A diagnosis: recursive image-based-rendering pipelines that feed rendered geometry back into their own fusion double-count evidence, and this, rather than depth noise, sets the ghost-persistence and flicker behaviour. The claim is formalised and falsifiable on event-injected sequences. (ii) A single variance that replaces four unrelated hand-set constants (mask 0.7/0.6, the 0.001 confidence weight, τ = 0.02 m, η = 15) and yields closed-form predictions of ghost half-life and flicker. (iii) The first minute-scale, event-injected evaluation of an explicit-geometry online NVS pipeline, reporting a flicker-lag-ghost Pareto frontier rather than 100-frame PSNR. Reviewers can check the theory-versus-measurement plot. An engineering tweak would not come with a quantitative prediction that can fail.
sharpened.differentiation: FILT3R (arXiv 2603.18493, ECCV 2026) and TTT3R/ReCal3R/TTSA3R apply Kalman or confidence gating to latent CUT3R tokens from a single moving camera for pose and pointmaps. We do not claim Kalman gating. Our state is explicit, lives in pixels of a fixed calibrated rig, is fused across cameras into an image-space TSDF, and is fed back through rendered novel-view depth. That feedback loop and its double-counting are absent from all of these works. CODD (2111.09337) and Khan et al. CVPR'23 (2304.07435, the base paper's group) already do motion-compensated or learned-uncertainty temporal depth fusion for a single stereo or mono stream. We cite both as the per-camera building block and differ by cross-camera TSDF fusion, variance-derived truncation, consistent novel-view feedback and rendering. 'Rethinking the State Update Gate' (2605.16981) derives memory horizons from gate magnitudes for latent recurrent reconstruction. We derive half-life for an explicit estimator and validate it against injected events in rendered output. NSTM (2607.15271) already analyses minute-scale drift for online multi-view NVS, with implicit TTT memory at 256-512 px and about 1 FPS memorisation. We do not claim the first long-horizon evaluation, only the first for explicit-geometry real-time IBR with flicker, ghost and lag metrics and theory. We add NSTM-style memory as a baseline if code is available. GeoStream (2606.15162) names the geometric feedback loop in generative video and fixes it with on-policy training. We fix it analytically (covariance intersection), with no generative model, for faithful capture. Stereo Any Video / TC-Stereo / Video Depth Anything give per-camera temporal consistency. We use them as front ends and report the residual gain from cross-camera consistent state.

datasets: CMU Panoptic Studio: HD cameras plus synced Kinect v2 RGB-D, minute-long sequences. Real sensor depth, the Holoportation/Starline-like RGB-D case, used for the long-horizon RGB-D tests.
ActorsHQ: 160 cameras, multi-minute single-actor sequences at high resolution. Stereo pairs are selectable and the face and hands are large, used for face and hand flicker.
DNA-Rendering and MVHumanNet++: many-camera human video. MVHumanNet++ is used by NSTM for minute-scale tests, so it allows a head-to-head. RGB only; depth from stereo pairs chosen among rig cameras.
Neural 3D Video / DyNeRF: all 300 frames, not only the first 100, for comparability with the base paper (flame = lighting-change case).
ENeRF-Outdoor and D3DMV: the base paper's test sets, as a sanity check that short-horizon PSNR is not lost.
PackUV-2B (sequences up to 30 min, 50+ cameras): the drift stress test if download size permits. RGB only.

Synthetic Blender sequences with ground-truth depth and ground-truth ghost onset: animated scanned humans (THuman or similar scans with retargeted motion) in rooms, with injected events (lights on/off, auto-exposure ramps, objects appearing and removed, textureless moving objects, a camera dropped for N frames). Needed because ghost half-life requires ground truth.
Optional custom capture: 4-6 Orbbec/Azure Kinect cameras for 2-3 five-minute sessions with scripted light switches. It strengthens the telepresence story but is not needed for the core claim.
baselines: The base paper (Ha et al. CVPR'25), faithfully reimplemented since no code is released. Includes colour-gated EMA plus η-capped feedback, swept over β and η to trace its own frontier.
Stateless: the same splat, TSDF and blend pipeline with no temporal state (lower bound on lag, upper bound on flicker).

The base pipeline with a temporally consistent video-depth front end (Stereo Any Video or TC-Stereo per pair; Video Depth Anything streaming scaled to stereo). This is the key 'is the state still needed' baseline.

A CODD / Khan'23-style per-camera temporal fusion (motion-compensated, learned uncertainty) plugged into the TSDF without cross-camera consistency. Isolates the gain from the fused and fed-back state.
Keyframe-reset heuristic (periodic or residual-triggered resets).
A learned ConvGRU gain trained on rollouts (Self-Forcing-style on-policy inputs), testing whether learning beats the closed form.
Where runnable: GPS-Gaussian+ or a comparable per-frame feed-forward human renderer (stateless), and NSTM (implicit memory) if code is released, on MVHumanNet++ at its resolution.
metrics: Flow-warped temporal error of rendered RGB and of TSDF depth, overall and in face, hand and background masks (from off-the-shelf human parsing).
TCC / STED / SDT, as in the base paper, for comparability.
Ghost half-life and recovery time after injected events: frames until the depth/RGB error in the event region drops below 50% and 10% (synthetic ground truth; real sequences with scripted events).
Drift slope: regression of error against time over 1-10 minutes.
Lag: phase delay of the depth response to ground-truth motion onset (synthetic), plotted against flicker to form the flicker-lag Pareto frontier.
Theory-versus-measurement: predicted against measured half-life and steady-state flicker variance.
Calibration of σ: NLL, sparsification/AUSE and reliability diagrams against ground-truth depth.
PSNR / SSIM / LPIPS on held-out rig cameras; ColorVideoVDP as an existing differentiable perceptual video metric.
Moving-viewer protocol: smooth head-like trajectories between rig cameras, with pseudo-GT from a per-scene 4DGS fit, and stereo-eye consistency.
Runtime breakdown, with depth estimation included.
key_ablations: Feedback: none vs base η-capped vs covariance intersection. This is the central double-counting test, run under lighting events and textureless motion.
Innovation gate: geometric χ² gate vs colour-difference mask vs both, under lighting change, flames and auto-exposure.
Motion compensation: on/off (equivalent to static-only filtering, as in the base) vs flow quality (RAFT-small vs full RAFT vs ground-truth flow).
Variance use: 1/σ² weights only, adaptive τ only, both, or neither (the base heuristic 7x7 variance with τ = 0.02 m).
Front end: noisy per-frame stereo vs temporally consistent video stereo vs sensor depth. Reports how much of the gain survives.
Closed-form Kalman gain vs learned ConvGRU gain, with teacher-forced vs on-policy rollout training.
Blend net trained on single instants (as in the base) vs 8-frame clips with temporal loss, separating the geometry-state gain from the blending gain.
Horizon: 100 frames vs 1 min vs 5-10 min.
experiments.capture_notes: No custom capture is needed for the core claim. Panoptic Studio provides real synced RGB-D over minutes. ActorsHQ, DNA-Rendering and MVHumanNet++ provide many-camera RGB, from which stereo pairs can be chosen. Synthetic Blender sequences provide the ground-truth ghost and lag measurements that no real dataset offers. The main data risks: (1) Panoptic's Kinect v2 depth is noisy and only loosely synchronised with the HD cameras (a real-world noise case, but sync must be checked); (2) the RGB-only datasets need per-pair stereo, which confounds results unless the front end is held fixed across methods. A small 4-6 camera RGB-D rig (about $3-5k) with scripted light switches and 5-minute conversations would make the telepresence claim much more convincing for IEEE VR/TVCG reviewers. Build it only if the 2-week test passes.

review.first_two_week_test: A geometry-only test, with no blend network and no training. (1) Days 1-4: reimplement the base paper's per-camera colour-gated EMA, image-space TSDF raymarch and η-capped previous-novel-view feedback in PyTorch/CUDA or plain PyTorch; real-time speed is not needed. Also implement the per-camera motion-compensated Kalman state with RAFT flow, 1/σ² weights, τ = cσ, a χ² gate and a covariance-intersection feedback. For measurement variance, use a simple heuristic σ (stereo left-right consistency, or the Kinect z² model); learning comes later. (2) Days 5-8: data. (a) 3-4 synthetic Blender sequences (scanned humans in a room, 4 cameras, 1-2 min) with ground-truth depth and injected events: light switch, object removal, textureless moving box. (b) 2 Panoptic Kinect sequences of about 2 minutes each. (3) Days 9-12: render TSDF depth at held-out cameras and on a moving virtual trajectory for three pipelines (base swept over β ∈ {0.5, 1, 2} and η ∈ {5, 15, 30}, stateless, and ours with and without CI feedback), each with raw stereo depth and with a temporally consistent video-stereo front end. Measure dynamic-region (face/hands) flow-warped depth error, ghost half-life after each event, lag at motion onset, and the flicker-lag frontier. Compute the closed-form predicted half-life. (4) Days 13-14: decision. Continue if ours dominates the base frontier (at least 25% lower dynamic-region flicker at equal lag, or clearly shorter ghosts at equal flicker), keeps at least 15% of the gain with a video-stereo front end, shows a measurable ghost or overconfidence failure in the base feedback under at least one event type, and has predicted half-life within ±30% of measured. Using TSDF depth rather than RGB is deliberate. It is cheaper, and if the geometry-state gain is absent there, the blend network will not create it.
review.kill_criteria:
Drop the method paper, or fold the analysis into a benchmark or perceptual-metric paper, if any of the following holds after the 2-week test.

(a) With a temporally consistent video-stereo front end (Stereo Any Video / TC-Stereo), the recursive state reduces dynamic-region TSDF-depth flicker by less than 15% at matched lag compared with the stateless pipeline. Video stereo would then have absorbed the problem.

(b) Across the β/η sweep, the base recursion already lies on or within 10% of our frontier and shows no event-type where its feedback produces measurably longer ghosts than CI or no-feedback. The double-counting diagnosis would then be empirically irrelevant.

(c) Measured ghost half-life and flicker deviate from the closed-form predictions by more than 50% on synthetic sequences even with ground-truth flow. The theory would then be decorative and the paper collapses to CODD+Khan'23+Starline.

(d) Minute-scale runs show no drift or ghost accumulation in any pipeline. Then 'long horizon' is not a problem worth a paper.

Also kill if, by month 4, rendered-RGB flicker gains (flow-warped error, ColorVideoVDP) are under 10% while depth gains exist, since the blend net would be masking geometry improvements. Re-check arXiv monthly for a Starline/Meta/Google follow-up that analyses feedback in image-TSDF pipelines.

reviewer_objections.objection: This is Kalman filtering of depth, textbook since Matthies-Kanade. CODD and Khan et al. CVPR'23 already do motion-compensated or uncertainty-weighted temporal depth fusion, and FILT3R does Kalman state updates for streaming 3D. What is new?
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We claim none of those components and cite all three prominently. What is new: (i) the double-counting diagnosis of feeding rendered novel-view geometry back into a multi-view fusion state, with a covariance-intersection fix that provably prevents overconfidence; (ii) one posterior variance jointly setting TSDF weight, truncation and a geometric gate in a cross-camera image-space TSDF; (iii) closed-form flicker, lag and ghost predictions validated against injected events at real frame rates over minutes. An ablation plugs a CODD/Khan-style per-camera filter into the same TSDF without cross-camera consistency or CI feedback and shows the residual gain.

reviewer_objections.objection: The 'theory' is a scalar steady-state Kalman gain. That is trivial, and a linearisation that ignores occlusion and topology change says nothing about real failures.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: The scalar case is deliberately simple so its predictions can be falsified. The non-trivial parts are the switched system (the gate resets, the K-nearest-view set changes with viewer motion, and the mask false-negative rate p drives persistence) and the proof that η-capped feedback acts as a positive confidence loop. Occlusion and topology change are handled explicitly as resets triggered by the innovation gate, and we report the regime (fast hands, thin structures) where predictions break down. The paper's evidence is the predicted-versus-measured plot, not the algebra.

reviewer_objections.objection: Temporally consistent video stereo and depth foundation models make explicit temporal state unnecessary. The whole contribution will vanish with a better front end.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We make this a first-class experiment rather than hiding it. Every method is run with raw per-frame stereo, video stereo and sensor depth. Per-pair video stereo is consistent over time but not across cameras, so view-set switching under viewer motion and cross-camera inconsistency still produce flicker in the fused TSDF. Our kill criterion requires a gain of at least 15% to survive this front end. Sensor-depth rigs (Kinect/Orbbec, Starline-like) have no temporal model at all.

reviewer_objections.objection: This is a niche pipeline (Starline-style image TSDF plus the base paper, which has no public code). The reimplementation may be unfaithful, and the relevance beyond one method is unclear.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: The reimplementation will be released, and we reproduce the base paper's reported DyNeRF/ENeRF/D3DMV numbers to within a stated tolerance before any claims. The state module is pipeline-agnostic. It outputs per-camera (μ, σ²) and a fused TSDF depth with variance, and we plug it into a second, stateless feed-forward renderer (GPS-Gaussian+-style) to show transfer. Starline-class RGB-D telepresence systems, the target application, all share this recursive-fusion structure.

reviewer_objections.objection: The gains show up only in custom temporal metrics. PSNR is unchanged, and there is no evidence that viewers notice.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We report established metrics (TCC/STED, flow-warped error, ColorVideoVDP) alongside the new ghost and lag metrics. We also run a small 2AFC preference study (n ≈ 15-20, desktop plus HMD) on minute-long clips with face and hand close-ups. Unchanged PSNR is expected and is itself informative: it explains the base paper's null TSDF ablation (31.17 vs 31.16 dB), since per-frame metrics are blind to what the temporal state buys.

effort.months: 6-8 (2 weeks go/no-go; about 2 months reimplementation and filter; 2 months long-horizon benchmark and theory validation; 1-2 months blend-net video training, user study and writing)
effort.people: 1 PhD student full-time plus 1 part-time (theory/estimation or a CUDA-savvy engineer); an advisor with state-estimation background helps
effort.compute: 1-4 GPUs with 24-48 GB (RTX 4090/A6000/A100 class). The filter is training-free. The variance-head fine-tune and the 8-frame blend-net training take about 1-3 GPU-days per run, plus about 1-2 TB storage for the Panoptic/ActorsHQ/MVHumanNet++ subsets. An optional RGB-D rig costs about $3-5k.

review.venue: Primary: ICCV 2027 or 3DV 2027 (method plus analysis). Fallback or alternative: IEEE TVCG / IEEE VR 2027 if the HMD user study and custom RGB-D capture are strong. Not SIGGRAPH unless it is merged with the perceptual-metric work.
review.synergies: (1) Perceptual/HMD flicker metric (idea 3 of this cluster and any psychophysics cluster). The calibrated TFV metric would replace the ad-hoc flicker proxies here and turn the Pareto frontier into a perceptual one; together they could make a TVCG/IEEE VR paper, or two papers sharing data. (2) Long-horizon telepresence benchmark / dataset cluster. The event-injected synthetic suite and the minute-scale protocol are natural benchmark components, and a benchmark paper could come out of this project. (3) Video-stereo / geometry-foundation-model front ends for calibrated rigs. The per-camera σ output is exactly what a rig-aware depth model should provide. (4) Moving-viewer / stereo-HMD rendering and latency compensation. The Kalman prediction step gives forward-extrapolated depth for motion-to-photon compensation, and the source-camera state is viewer-independent, so two eyes and multiple viewers share it. (5) Streaming and compression. The posterior variance and innovation maps are a natural signal for rate allocation or keyframing of depth and Gaussian streams. (6) Hybrid explicit-plus-learned memory (an NSTM-style TTT memory conditioned on explicit geometry state). The explicit posterior can serve as the stable anchor that implicit memories lack.

threats.title: Eventful Transformers: Leveraging Temporal Redundancy in Vision Transformers
threats.what_overlaps: This is exactly the core compute mechanism of both ideas. Per-token gating modules monitor temporal change, recompute only the changed tokens, and apply delta-sparse updates to the query-key and attention-value products, reusing the rest from the previous frame. Compute is adaptive to change at runtime and can be retrofitted to pretrained ViTs.
threats.what_remains_different: It targets video recognition and detection on single-camera video, with no geometry, no multi-camera calibrated attention and no novel-view output. Its gate is a thresholded feature difference, not a head trained against a teacher's feature drift. Any 'compute proportional to change' claim must be framed as applying and extending Eventful-style gating to multi-view geometry and NVS transformers, not as a new mechanism.

threats.title: VLA-Cache: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Manipulation via Adaptive Token Caching
threats.what_overlaps: Identifies minimally changed patch tokens between adjacent frames from a fixed or robot camera, reuses their cached KV, and adapts the reuse ratio per layer. This is the 'per-camera-patch KV reuse across time' idea, already published in robotics, and a line of follow-ups exists (VLN-Cache 2603.07080, Neural Introspection Gating 2608.10824).
threats.what_remains_different: Single camera, LLM-style VLA backbone, action outputs. There is no cross-view global attention (where one camera's stale KV is consumed by other cameras' queries), no geometry or depth outputs, and no learned drift-trained gate. Neural Introspection Gating's gate is training-free, based on the logit margin.

threats.title: RnG: A Unified Transformer for Complete 3D Modeling from Partial Observations
threats.what_overlaps: Treats a geometry transformer's KV cache as an implicit 3D representation that arbitrary target poses query to produce novel-view RGB-D. This overlaps directly with RigStream's 'target-ray depth head over shared scene tokens' and with GeoLVSM's 'encode once, decode many targets from cached KV'.
threats.what_remains_different: Static scenes, completion and generation focus, and no temporal reuse. It has no geometry-biased or epipolar-restricted target attention and no fixed-rig calibration. The new part left for RigStream is an all-N-camera target-ray depth head over a temporally persistent, change-gated KV table, used to remove K-nearest switching.

threats.title: KV-Tracker: Real-Time Pose Tracking with Transformers
threats.what_overlaps: Caches the global-attention KV pairs of a multi-view geometry network (pi^3) over keyframes and reuses them as the scene representation for real-time online processing, with about a 15x speedup and no retraining.
threats.what_remains_different: Single moving monocular camera, keyframe-level caching for pose tracking. There is no per-patch change gating, no synchronized multi-camera rig, no dynamic-content refresh and no depth/NVS temporal consistency.

threats.title: OVGGT / StreamCacheVGGT / STAC / InfiniteVGGT (bounded and compressed KV caches for streaming geometry transformers)
threats.what_overlaps: All of these give streaming geometry FMs with fixed-budget or constant memory, token importance scoring, eviction and merging. STAC organises evicted tokens in a voxel grid for spatial reuse. This removes 'bounded memory instead of StreamVGGT's growing cache' as a contribution.
threats.what_remains_different: All are single moving camera, and all concern which past tokens to keep, not skipping recomputation of current-frame tokens that are unchanged. None exploits the stable identity of a (camera, patch) token under a fixed rig.

threats.title: DriveVGGT: Calibration-Constrained Visual Geometry Transformers for Multi-Camera Autonomous Driving
threats.what_overlaps: A calibrated, synchronized multi-camera video geometry FM with per-camera temporal attention, calibration-injected multi-camera attention and metric scale. It covers 'rig-conditioned multi-camera temporal geometry FM' in general.
threats.what_remains_different: Outward-facing driving rig with a moving ego vehicle, so no static-patch identity and no token reuse. It offers no novel-view depth, no inward-facing dynamic humans and no telepresence latency budget.

threats.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis (NSTM)
threats.what_overlaps: A streaming multi-view LVSM-style transformer for dynamic humans with a persistent memory. Synthesis cost is amortised by decoupling memory updates from per-frame synthesis. This is the closest prior for GeoLVSM-Stream's 'streaming, dynamic, calibrated extension of view-synthesis transformers'.
threats.what_remains_different: It has no explicit depth or epipolar attention prior and no per-patch change-gated input-KV reuse. It works at 256-512 px, does not amortise across many simultaneous viewers or eyes, and does not evaluate TCC/EPI view consistency.

threats.title: RaySt3R: Predicting Novel Depth Maps for Zero-Shot Object Completion / Z3D
threats.what_overlaps: Feed-forward novel-view depth via cross-attention from query rays to multi-view features (RaySt3R), and novel-view depth from VGGT tokens (Z3D). This weakens any claim that a 'target-ray depth head' is itself new.
threats.what_remains_different: Both are static, object- or scene-completion, and non-real-time. Neither uses depth-biased epipolar sampling over all N rig cameras, and neither addresses temporal consistency or K-switch popping.

threats.title: ResidualViT / Gated Residual Tokenization (temporal-redundancy token skipping for dense video encoding)
threats.what_overlaps: More evidence that skipping static-region tokens using a gate driven by motion or residuals, including learned residual encoders, is an established way to accelerate video ViTs.
threats.what_remains_different: Video understanding and retrieval features only, with no geometry, multi-view or rendering component.
