novelty.remaining_novel_angle:
What is taken is the mechanism: change-gated per-token recomputation with cached KV reuse across frames. Eventful Transformers (ICCV 2023) did it for ViTs, and VLA-Cache (NeurIPS 2025) did it for static patches' KV across frames. Querying a cached geometry-transformer KV as a scene representation for novel-view RGB-D is also taken (RnG, CVPR 2026; KV-Tracker, CVPR 2026). So is bounded-memory streaming geometry (OVGGT, STAC, StreamCacheVGGT).

What remains, as I found no paper doing it, is the specific combination for a fixed, calibrated, synchronized, inward-facing rig with dynamic content:
- A persistent per-(camera, patch) KV table inside a cross-view global-attention geometry FM (or view-synthesis encoder). Stale static tokens from camera A are consumed by fresh queries from camera B.
- A gate trained against teacher feature drift (and robust to illumination and exposure), rather than training-free thresholds.
- An all-N-camera, depth-biased epipolar target-ray depth head fed by that temporally persistent table, shown to remove K-nearest-view switching and to give static geometry that is bit-stable by construction.
- For the GeoLVSM variant: temporal input-KV reuse in a decoupled view-synthesis transformer on dynamic scenes, with the encoder amortised across many simultaneous viewers or eyes. NSTM, Efficient-LVSM and SVSM each have one piece, but none has the combination.

The claim must be framed as a systems-and-architecture contribution with strong measurements, not as a new mechanism. Useful measurements: compute against the fraction of the scene in motion; the failure modes of cross-view staleness and error propagation; a learned vs Eventful-style vs RGB-difference gate; lighting robustness; and full-pipeline latency including depth. Eventful Transformers and VLA-Cache must be cited and ablated against.
novelty.best_variant:
RigStream (idea 1) has the more defensible novelty, and its target-ray depth head should be merged with GeoLVSM's multi-target amortisation.

Why RigStream:
- Its geometry-FM setting (multi-camera, calibrated, inward-facing, dynamic, streaming) has no direct occupant. DriveVGGT is outward-facing with no reuse; StreamVGGT and OVGGT are single-camera; Forge4D and NoPo4D are uncalibrated with state tokens and no reuse.
- It is testable with clear metrics: flicker, cross-view reprojection error, and compute against motion fraction.

Why GeoLVSM-Stream is weaker:
- Its 'geometry-biased epipolar attention around a depth estimate' is a long-established inductive bias in generalizable NeRF/IBR and in epipolar-attention transformers. It is also the opposite of LVSM's stated design.
- Its streaming-LVSM framing is partly occupied by NSTM.
- It is riskier in compute (LVSM-scale training).

Its multi-viewer, shared-KV decoding claim (sub-linear cost per extra viewer or eye) is the one piece worth keeping. The strongest combined paper is a rig-native streaming encoder with change-gated per-camera-patch KV reuse. It would expose a single temporally persistent token table queried by both a target-ray depth head and a light RGB decoder for M viewers, with Eventful Transformers, VLA-Cache and RnG as the explicit baselines to beat.

sharpened.title: RigCache: Change-Gated Persistent Token Tables for Streaming Multi-View Geometry on Fixed Camera Rigs
sharpened.one_liner: On a fixed, calibrated, inward-facing rig, a geometry transformer can keep a persistent per-(camera, patch) token and KV table. A stale-aware, 3-tier learned gate refreshes only the tokens whose deep features would actually drift, including drift caused by changes in other cameras. The result is metric multi-view depth whose cost tracks scene motion, with temporal stability built in. The same table is queried by an all-N-camera target-ray depth head for every viewer.
sharpened.core_claim: Setting: synchronized, calibrated, inward-facing rigs (8-16 cameras) with dynamic humans. Under teleconference-like motion (at least 70% of patches static), RigCache meets all of the following against the same student recomputed densely every frame. (i) At least 3x lower backbone FLOPs and at least 2x lower wall-clock time. (ii) Depth accuracy within 5% relative AbsRel and delta1 within 1 point. (iii) At least 30% lower temporal depth flicker (TAE/OPW) on static regions. At equal compute, it beats three training-free reuse schemes (Eventful-style thresholding, VLA-Cache-style static-token KV reuse and an RGB-difference gate) on depth error and false-refresh rate under injected exposure and illumination changes. Its all-N target-ray depth head reduces novel-view depth popping along a sweeping viewer trajectory by at least 40% compared with K-nearest TSDF fusion (the base paper). If the oracle-gate simulation in the 2-week test cannot hold the depth error at 70% reuse, the claim is false.
sharpened.key_insight: In a fixed rig, a patch token (camera c, location u) keeps its identity over time, so the natural streaming memory is a table indexed by camera and patch, not a sequence cache indexed by time. The non-obvious problem, which Eventful Transformers and VLA-Cache never face, is cross-view staleness. In a global-attention geometry model, a pixel-static patch in camera A still has deep features that depend on patches in cameras B-N that did change (for example the person moving in front of the background it observes). So 'the input did not change' does not mean 'the token does not need updating'. The research question is how far such change propagates through cross-view attention, and whether a gate trained against teacher feature drift, together with a cheap attention-only refresh tier, can capture that propagation at a fraction of full cost. The answer decides whether compute can track motion in multi-view geometry models at all. A secondary consequence: the persistent, mostly frozen table is a stable scene representation. Novel-view depth read from it by attending to all N cameras has neither the flicker of per-frame recomputation nor the popping caused by the K-nearest view set switching.
sharpened.method:
Backbone (student).
- About 300M parameters, initialized from a multi-view DA3-Base-class or VGGT-distilled model.
- Alternating per-camera and global attention on 14 px patches at about 518x294 per camera (about 780 tokens per camera, roughly 6-12k tokens for 8-16 cameras).
- Calibration injected as Plücker ray-map tokens. Optional sensor-depth prompt tokens for RGB-D rigs.
- DPT head outputs per-camera metric depth and confidence.

Persistent table.
- For every layer l and every (c, u), store the token state x_l, its K_l and V_l, and a staleness age.

Three-tier gate.
- The gate is a small conv and MLP on exposure-normalized shallow features: patch embedding difference, per-camera gain-compensated RGB difference and a log-chromaticity difference. It also reads the table's age and confidence.
- It outputs, per token, one of three tiers:
  - T0 freeze: reuse x_l, K_l and V_l at all layers (no cost).
  - T1 attention refresh: reuse the token's own projections and MLP, but recompute its global-attention output against the fresh keys, in Eventful delta form. Cost is about 1/4 of a full token. This tier handles cross-view contamination.
  - T2 full recompute through all layers.
- A forced round-robin refresh touches every token at least every R frames (R about 30), and confidence decays with age.

Gate supervision.
- The target is teacher drift: run the dense student offline and label a token T2 or T1 if its layer-l feature change exceeds eps_input or eps_ctx at designated layers.
- Loss: cross-entropy on the tier labels plus a Gumbel straight-through budget loss on the expected FLOPs.

Stale-aware training.
- 8-frame truncated rollouts with the gate on-policy, so the student learns to consume stale KV entries.
- Distillation losses at every frame against an offline bidirectional teacher: windowed DA3 or MapAnything given the known calibration, with a temporal-smoothing pass (Video-Depth-Anything-style window alignment).
- Additional losses: cross-view reprojection consistency, temporal warp consistency on flow-warped dynamic regions, and scale-invariant plus metric L1 with a gradient term.

Target-ray depth head.
- Each target patch token is a Plücker embedding plus a coarse depth reprojected from the previous frame's target depth, or a sweep at initialization.
- It performs deformable cross-attention to s = 8 samples per camera along the epipolar segment at plus or minus k·sigma, over the final-layer tokens of ALL N cameras, plus 32 global tokens.
- Output: depth, normal and uncertainty at 1/4 target resolution, then joint-bilateral upsampling guided by the splatted RGB.
- Per-viewer cost is only this head (under 3 ms), so M viewers or eyes share one backbone pass.
- Supervision: held-out-camera teacher depth, plus sensor depth where it exists.

Rendering.
- Plug into the base pipeline: forward-splat pixel Gaussians from the student depth (confidence-gated), then the base U-Net blender, which now also receives the target-ray uncertainty.
- A LVSM-style renderer is deliberately NOT built (it is out of compute scope, and NSTM occupies that space).

Training data: DNA-Rendering, MVHumanNet++, Panoptic Studio (HD plus Kinect), PackUV-2B training sequences and N3DV training scenes.

Compute: about 2-4k GPU-hours on 4-8 A100/H100 GPUs (LoRA or partial fine-tuning of the student, frozen teacher run offline once).

Runtime target (RTX 4090 or A100 class, 8 cameras):
- Backbone at most 20 ms at 30% motion, against about 60-80 ms dense.
- Target head at most 3 ms per viewer.
- End-to-end, including depth, at most 50 ms. The base paper excludes depth from its runtime; this target does not.
sharpened.why_not_engineering:
The paper answers a question the prior work never had to ask: in a model where every token attends to every camera, does a local change stay local? Eventful Transformers and VLA-Cache work on a single camera, where a static input patch means a static token up to self-attention context. Here the thing to measure and model is contamination of static tokens in other cameras through cross-view attention. The paper would contribute:
(1) An empirical characterization, per layer and per camera, of change propagation in multi-view geometry transformers. This is a new analysis and holds regardless of the method's final numbers.
(2) A tiered gate supervised by teacher drift, with an attention-refresh tier designed for that contamination.
(3) Stale-aware on-policy training, showing that a student can be taught to tolerate stale KV entries. Training-free reuse cannot do this, and the paper shows it by comparison.
(4) A falsifiable accuracy-compute-stability trade-off curve against motion fraction, with the prior gating schemes as baselines.

If cross-view propagation turns out to be negligible, the paper's honest conclusion is 'Eventful-style reuse transfers to rigs'. That is a workshop result, and the kill criteria are set to catch it early.
sharpened.differentiation:
- Eventful Transformers (ICCV 2023) and VLA-Cache (NeurIPS 2025): single-camera, training-free or threshold gating, and no cross-view consumers of stale tokens. They are adopted as baselines, not claimed against. The new parts are the cross-view staleness tier, the drift-supervised gate that is robust to exposure changes, and on-policy stale-aware training.
- StreamVGGT, OVGGT, StreamCacheVGGT, STAC and InfiniteVGGT: they address which past tokens to keep for one moving camera. RigCache addresses which current tokens to skip computing when camera identity is fixed. The two are orthogonal, and bounded memory is not claimed as new.
- KV-Tracker and RnG (CVPR 2026): cache or query a geometry model's KV as a scene representation, but keyframe-level, static and single-camera. RigCache's table is persistent and dynamic, and it is refreshed per patch.
- RaySt3R and Z3D: novel-view depth from ray queries exists. The target-ray head is presented as a component. Its specific claim is the removal of K-switch popping through all-N epipolar attention over a temporally persistent table, measured with a new trajectory-popping metric.
- DriveVGGT and Rig3R: calibrated multi-camera, but outward-facing, ego-moving and without token reuse. There, no patch is static, so the premise does not apply.
- NSTM, Efficient-LVSM and Tele360: renderer-side or per-frame. RigCache is a geometry front end, and NSTM or a U-Net can consume its output.

datasets: Neural 3D Video / DyNeRF (N3DV): public. The base-paper test protocol is used, with a clean scene split because training scenes share the kitchen.
ENeRF-Outdoor: public, outdoor lighting variation.
D3DMV (compressed): base-paper comparability.
Panoptic Studio: public HD cameras plus synchronized Kinect depth. The only large public source of real sensor depth on a dynamic multi-camera rig. Used as the depth-accuracy ground truth.
DNA-Rendering: public on application, 60 cameras. Main training source and minute-long evaluation.
MVHumanNet++: public on application. Training and the NSTM-comparable minute-long protocol.
PackUV-2B (CVPR 2026 release): 50+ synchronized cameras, up to 30 minutes. Long-horizon drift and staleness tests. Verify licence and download size before relying on it.
ScanNet++ (static): absolute depth accuracy sanity check against laser-scan ground truth.
baselines: Base paper pipeline: RAFT-Stereo plus colour-difference-gated TSDF with K-nearest views. Reimplement, since no code is released.
Fast-FoundationStereo plus the base TSDF; Stereo Any Video plus the base TSDF (the strong 'just swap the depth module' baseline).
Per-frame dense student (same weights, no reuse); per-frame DA3 or MapAnything with calibration (the teacher, as an upper bound).
StreamVGGT and OVGGT adapted to multi-camera input (cameras flattened into the stream).
Eventful Transformers gating applied to the same student (training-free, threshold per layer).
VLA-Cache-style static-token KV reuse (training-free) and an RGB-difference gate (the base paper's formula as the gate).
RnG / RaySt3R-style ray-query depth over K-nearest cameras, as a check on the target-head variant.
metrics: Depth: AbsRel, delta1 and RMSE against Panoptic Kinect or ScanNet++ ground truth; against teacher pseudo-GT only as a secondary measure.
Temporal: TAE/OPW depth flicker, reported separately for static and dynamic masks.
Cross-view: reprojection depth-consistency error between cameras.
Compute: backbone FLOPs, wall-clock ms and GPU memory against measured motion fraction (binned); refresh rate per tier.
Gate quality: false-refresh rate under injected exposure, gain and flicker; miss rate on slow motion (ghosting); cross-view contamination error of frozen tokens.
Long-horizon: depth error and ghosting against time over 1-10 minutes, with and without forced refresh.
Novel view: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, TCC, STED, SDT, SDV and EPI with the base-paper protocol; MEt3R.
New trajectory-popping metric: temporal derivative of novel-view depth and colour along a smooth virtual camera sweep over a static frame. It isolates K-switch artifacts.
End-to-end latency including depth, and per-viewer marginal cost for M = 1, 2, 8 and 32 target views.
key_ablations: Gate type (equal FLOPs): learned drift-supervised vs Eventful threshold vs RGB difference vs oracle teacher-drift.
Tier structure: 2-tier (freeze or full) vs 3-tier with an attention-refresh tier. This is the core cross-view contamination test.
Stale-aware on-policy training vs the same gate applied at test time only.
Reuse budget sweep (50/70/85/95%) and forced-refresh period R.
Calibration tokens on vs off; sensor-depth prompt on vs off.
Target-ray head: all-N vs K-nearest cameras; epipolar-biased vs full attention; head vs TSDF raymarch vs hybrid with a one-step TSDF refinement.
Number of cameras (4/8/16), to show how contamination and savings scale with N.
Lighting robustness: synthetic global gain and auto-exposure steps, local lamp toggles, and flame-like flicker (N3DV Flame Steak).
experiments.capture_notes:
The core claims can be tested on public data. Panoptic Studio provides real sensor depth on a dynamic rig; DNA-Rendering, MVHumanNet++ and PackUV-2B provide long, many-camera sequences; lighting and exposure changes can be injected synthetically.

A small optional capture (6-8 synchronized machine-vision or RGB-D cameras, auto-exposure ON, controlled lamp toggles, 5-minute sessions) would add three things: a real-world lighting-robustness result, an end-to-end live latency demo, and a real telepresence motion-fraction distribution (seated talking vs standing). It strengthens an IEEE VR / SIGGRAPH Asia submission but is not needed for a CVPR/ICCV paper.

Privacy caveat: human-subject datasets require the application agreements. Do not redistribute derived depth of identifiable subjects.

review.first_two_week_test:
Training-free oracle study on off-the-shelf models, needing 1 GPU and no training.

Step 1: dense runs.
- Run VGGT (or multi-view DA3) densely per timestep on 100-frame, 8-camera clips from N3DV (Coffee Martini, Flame Steak), 2-3 Panoptic HD+Kinect sequences and 2 DNA-Rendering sequences.
- Log every layer's token features.

Step 2: characterize drift.
(a) The fraction of tokens per layer whose feature drift between frames falls below eps, split by whether their own input patch changed.
(b) Cross-view contamination: for pixel-static tokens, how drift grows with depth and correlates with the amount of change in OTHER cameras.
(c) How well RGB-difference and Eventful thresholds predict the drift (AUROC), under the original frames and under injected global gain or exposure steps.

Step 3: simulate reuse at 50/70/90% reuse. Freeze tokens and reuse their KV using three gates: the oracle drift gate, the RGB-difference gate and the Eventful gate. Also simulate the 3-tier variant, where frozen tokens still re-attend at global layers. For each, measure:
- depth AbsRel against Kinect and against dense output;
- static-region flicker;
- FLOPs.

Also time a block-sparse implementation of one global layer at 70% reuse (FlashAttention varlen gather) to check that the savings survive on real GPU hardware.

The idea is validated if all four hold:
1. More than 70% of tokens are reusable at acceptable error with the oracle gate.
2. The 3-tier variant clearly beats the 2-tier variant, which shows that cross-view contamination is real and addressable.
3. The oracle gate beats the RGB-difference and Eventful gates by a clear margin, especially under exposure changes, leaving room for a learned gate.
4. The block-sparse layer shows at least 2x measured wall-clock speedup.
review.kill_criteria:
Kill or pivot if any of these holds:
(1) Even the oracle gate cannot keep relative AbsRel degradation under 5% at 70% reuse on Panoptic or DNA-Rendering. This means global attention spreads change too widely for a rig to exploit.
(2) Training-free Eventful or RGB-difference gating comes within about 1% AbsRel and about 10% flicker of the oracle at equal reuse, including under exposure changes. Then the learned gate and stale-aware training have no headroom, and the paper reduces to 'Eventful applied to VGGT'.
(3) Block-sparse wall-clock speedup at 70% reuse is under 1.5x on the target GPU.
(4) At month 3, Fast-FoundationStereo or Stereo Any Video plus TSDF dominates the student on the accuracy / flicker / latency Pareto front at N = 8.
(5) A paper appears doing change-gated multi-camera token reuse in a geometry FM. The field moves fast, so re-run the arXiv check monthly.

If (1) fails but a smaller 4-camera setting works, consider narrowing to a workshop or 3DV paper.

reviewer_objections.objection: This is Eventful Transformers or VLA-Cache applied to VGGT, a known mechanism in a new backbone.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We adopt their gating as baselines and do not claim the mechanism. The new, measured phenomenon is cross-view staleness: pixel-static tokens drift because other cameras changed. We quantify it per layer and per camera count and show that single-camera gates misfire on it. We address it with an attention-refresh tier and stale-aware on-policy training, and show gains over both methods at matched FLOPs. The layer-wise propagation analysis is a standalone contribution.

reviewer_objections.objection: FLOP savings from token sparsity rarely become wall-clock speedups on GPUs, and gather and scatter overhead eats them.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We report measured latency (not only FLOPs) using block-sparse, variable-length attention kernels and patch-granular gathers, binned by real motion fraction from the datasets. The two-week test includes a kernel timing gate (at least 2x at 70% reuse) before any training investment.

reviewer_objections.objection: Freezing static tokens freezes their errors and creates ghosting when the gate misses slow motion. 'Bit-stable' is a bug, not a feature.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We use forced round-robin refresh, confidence decay with age and a drift-trained gate, and we evaluate over minute-long (up to 10 min) sequences with explicit ghosting and miss-rate metrics. Consistent static error is perceptually far less harmful than flicker, which is supported by TCC and STED in the NVS evaluation. The refresh period is swept to expose the trade-off honestly.

reviewer_objections.objection: Real-time stereo foundation models plus a TSDF already give accurate, fast, consistent depth, so a new geometry FM is unnecessary.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Fast-FoundationStereo and Stereo Any Video plus TSDF are primary baselines with depth time included, which the base paper omitted. RigCache offers what pairwise stereo cannot: no pair selection, all-N cross-view consistency, calibration-conditioned metric scale, a per-viewer target-ray head that removes K-switch popping, and cost that falls with static content. If the baselines dominate the Pareto front, that is a stated kill criterion.

reviewer_objections.objection: Supervision and evaluation against a teacher's pseudo-GT is circular, and held-out rig cameras test only interpolation.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Primary depth metrics use real sensor ground truth (Panoptic Kinect, ScanNet++ laser scans). Cross-view reprojection and flicker metrics need no teacher. Novel-view evaluation adds a virtual-trajectory popping metric and minute-long sequences beyond the base paper's 100 frames and held-out cameras.

effort.months: 8-10 (about 1 month for the oracle study and kernels, 3-4 for the student and gate with stale-aware training, 2 for the target-ray head and pipeline integration, 2 for evaluation and writing)
effort.people: 2 (one PhD student on the model and training, one on kernels, the pipeline, the evaluation protocol and optional capture)
effort.compute: 4-8 A100/H100-class GPUs; about 2-4k GPU-hours total. Teacher pseudo-GT is generated offline once (the largest single cost, about 500-1000 GPU-hours for DNA-Rendering and MVHumanNet++ subsets). No LVSM-scale training.

review.venue: ICCV 2027 (primary; CVPR 2027 in November 2026 is too soon for the full system). Fallbacks: 3DV 2027 for the propagation analysis plus a reuse method; IEEE VR 2028 or SIGGRAPH Asia 2027 if paired with a live-rig demo and a real capture.
review.synergies:
- Motion-proportional streaming diffusion or flow fixer for online 3D video: the same gate and tier masks can drive latent and KV caching in the enhancer, so one change-signal serves the whole stack.
- Depth uncertainty as a first-class input: the target-ray head's uncertainty and token-age confidence feed the blender or fixer.
- Multi-viewer and light-field display amortization: one backbone pass, then M cheap target-ray heads. This is the part of GeoLVSM-Stream worth keeping.
- Gaussian and volumetric streaming codecs: the per-(camera, patch) refresh mask is a free delta-coding and bandwidth mask for transmitting only changed geometry.
- Long-horizon telepresence benchmark (minute-long, sensor depth, head-tracked trajectories, popping metric): this paper can seed it.
- NSTM-style renderers: RigCache's persistent depth table could supply the geometry prior NSTM lacks.
- A paper series is possible: (1) the propagation analysis plus RigCache geometry; (2) a geometry-biased streaming renderer on top of the table; (3) end-to-end live-rig telepresence at IEEE VR or SIGGRAPH Asia.

cited_work_check.title: Real-time 3D Visualization of Radiance Fields on Light Field Displays
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed. Pre-optimized radiance fields (3DGS, sparse voxels) are converted to shared sweeping planes and composited into 45 views: 200+ FPS at 512p on a Looking Glass. The abstract says it trades away view-dependent colour for speed. No live capture and no learned blending.

cited_work_check.title: LentiAvatar: Pseudo-Multiview Reconstruction and Subpixel Prism Rendering for Real-Time Stereoscopic Communication
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed. Monocular Gaussian head avatar, 32 views subpixel-encoded to a 4K lenticular panel, 10.65 FPS live and 38.49 FPS distilled. The characterisation is accurate.

cited_work_check.title: ViewSplat: View-Adaptive 3D Gaussian Splatting for Feed-Forward Synthesis
cited_work_check.note: It exists, but the ideator understates it. ViewSplat predicts per-scene View MLP weights feed-forward. From the target-view coordinates they give view-dependent residuals for all Gaussian attributes, including opacity, not only colour. This is already a learned, per-primitive, view-conditioned visibility and weighting that is evaluated cheaply per view. It is static and unposed-image only, with no temporal model and no multi-view-display study.

cited_work_check.title: 3DTV: A Feedforward Interpolation Network for Real-Time View Synthesis
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed. Delaunay triplet selection, pose-aware depth pyramid and occlusion-aware blending, done per target view. It is a valid target-space baseline.

cited_work_check.title: GPS-Gaussian: Generalizable Pixel-wise 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-time Human Novel View Synthesis
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: Gaussian parameter maps on the source views, regressed feed-forward. This already gives render cost = rasterization only for any number of views. So the claim that extra views cost only rasterization is not new; what is new is only the learned directional cross-camera weighting.

cited_work_check.title: VirtualCube: An Immersive 3D Video Communication System
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed: V-Cube View with MVS depth and Lumi-Net blending, rendering a separate view for each participant to keep mutual gaze. The claim that it uses per-view blending matches the abstract.

threats.title: No Pose, No Problem in 4D (NoPo4D): Feed-Forward Dynamic Gaussians from Unposed Multi-View Videos
threats.what_overlaps: This paper implements the core mechanism. From synchronized multi-view video on a static rig, a feed-forward network predicts per-pixel Gaussians for each source camera. Their opacity is parameterised as order-k spherical harmonics, not a scalar. The paper says the opacity SH 'act as a learned confidence metric' that makes misaligned Gaussians from a camera transparent from viewpoints where cross-camera geometry disagrees. That is a per-source-pixel directional cross-camera blend-weight field, and rendering any view is pure rasterization. The ablation without opacity SH loses 7.5 dB PSNR. It is evaluated on N3DV (DyNeRF) and Immersive Light Field, and its limitations section notes the static-rig assumption.
threats.what_remains_different: No amortization, multi-viewer or light-field-display framing, and no views-per-second scaling study. It is pose-free and does not use calibrated RGB-D or a TSDF, and is not built for real-time telepresence latency. Its temporal model is velocities and motion, not coefficient filtering in source space. There is no distillation from a target-space IBR blender, no explicit occlusion handling through a shared TSDF visibility, no persistent background plate, and no evaluation of K-set popping, EPI or light-field-display quality.

threats.title: ViewSplat: View-Adaptive 3D Gaussian Splatting for Feed-Forward Synthesis
threats.what_overlaps: Feed-forward pixel-aligned Gaussians plus predicted per-scene View MLPs. The MLPs map target-view coordinates to view-dependent residuals of opacity, colour, position, scale and rotation. The network runs once, and each extra view is a cheap per-primitive evaluation plus rasterization (90 FPS rendering). This is the same 'predict once in source/primitive space, evaluate directionally per view' decomposition, with a more expressive basis than SH.
threats.what_remains_different: Static scenes, unposed images and no video. No temporal consistency, no many-view or light-field-display amortization study, and no telepresence or RGB-D rig.

threats.title: CoherentRaster: Efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting for Light Field Displays
threats.what_overlaps: Amortizes 3DGS rasterization across the many views of a light-field display, with cross-view coherent attribute reuse and subpixel-level rasterization, in real time on consumer GPUs. This covers the 'O(#views x raster)' half of the proposed cost model and the light-field-display rendering contribution.
threats.what_remains_different: Per-scene optimized static 3DGS. It has no live multi-camera capture, no learned cross-camera blending and no temporal consistency. It is complementary: it could be the rasterizer back-end of the proposed method.

threats.title: Real-time 3D Visualization of Radiance Fields on Light Field Displays
threats.what_overlaps: Shares intermediate computation (sweeping planes) across 45 light-field-display views for real-time rendering: 200+ FPS, up to 22x faster than rendering each view separately.
threats.what_remains_different: Static, optimized radiance fields. It explicitly drops view dependence. No live capture, no learned IBR blending and no temporal stabilization.

threats.title: DirectL: Efficient Radiance Fields Rendering for 3D Light Field Displays
threats.what_overlaps: Subpixel repurposing for rendering light-field displays directly from NeRF or 3DGS, avoiding the full 45-view render cost.
threats.what_remains_different: Static per-scene radiance fields. No live IBR, blending or temporal model.

threats.title: VoD-3DGS: View-opacity-Dependent 3D Gaussian Splatting
threats.what_overlaps: View-dependent opacity (a symmetric-matrix term) that suppresses Gaussians from some viewpoints. The primitive is the same one the idea uses for directional weights.
threats.what_remains_different: Optimized per scene and aimed at specular effects. It is not feed-forward, not multi-camera blending and not temporal. 6DGS, 7DGS and Augmented Radiance Field (2602.19916) are similar per-scene view-dependent-opacity variants.

threats.title: GPS-Gaussian / GPS-Gaussian+
threats.what_overlaps: Source-view Gaussian parameter maps regressed feed-forward, so every additional view costs only rasterization.
threats.what_remains_different: Scalar opacity with no directional cross-camera weighting, no temporal model and no multi-view-display study.

threats.title: Tele-Aloha: A Low-budget and High-authenticity Telepresence System Using Sparse RGB Cameras
threats.what_overlaps: Live sparse-camera Gaussian telepresence on an autostereoscopic display with iris tracking.
threats.what_remains_different: It uses a target-space neural rasterizer plus weighted blending per eye view, so it is not amortized in source space. It renders eye-tracked views only, not a dense light field.

threats.title: Omni-Recon: Harnessing Image-based Rendering for General-Purpose Neural Radiance Fields
threats.what_overlaps: A lightweight branch predicts source-view blending weights, and the geometry is baked into meshes for real-time rendering.
threats.what_remains_different: Static generalizable NeRF. Blend weights are still evaluated per target ray, not stored as a directional field on source pixels, and there is no temporal or multi-view-display angle.

novelty.remaining_novel_angle:
The mechanism itself is already published, so it cannot be the headline claim. NoPo4D (arXiv 2605.22190, May 2026) predicts per-source-pixel Gaussians with SH-parameterised view-dependent opacity, feed-forward from static-rig multi-view video, and uses them explicitly as learned cross-camera confidence/blend weights. ViewSplat (2603.25265) predicts per-primitive view-conditioned opacity and colour residuals once and evaluates them cheaply for each view. Pixel-aligned feed-forward Gaussians (GPS-Gaussian) already make extra views cost only rasterization.

What is still defensible is a systems-and-evaluation contribution for live telepresence displays:
(1) The first real-time (<50-100 ms), temporally consistent live-capture IBR that drives a 32-45-view light-field or lenticular display, or P-1 gaze-correct multi-party views. It would include a measured quality vs. views-per-second Pareto front against per-view target-space blenders (the base paper, 3DTV, VirtualCube-style).
(2) Temporal stabilization as confidence-gated filtering of directional coefficients in the fixed source-pixel frame. This is invariant to viewer motion, and no prior work does it; NoPo4D models velocities, not coefficient filtering.
(3) Distillation of a target-space, occlusion-aware IBR blender (Ha et al. style, TSDF visibility) into source-space directional fields, with a quantified gap between teacher and student.
(4) An explicit study showing that soft all-N directional weights remove K-set popping, measured with EPI/MEt3R across dense display views.
(5) Coupling with a coherent LFD rasterizer (CoherentRaster or sweeping-plane) so both halves of the cost are amortized.

Reviewers will ask for NoPo4D-style opacity SH as the direct ablation baseline, so the paper must show that the gains come from the telepresence-specific parts (temporal source-space filtering, TSDF visibility, distillation, display pipeline) and not from directional opacity itself.
novelty.best_variant: The cluster has only one idea, "One Capture, Many Eyes". Its most defensible sub-claim is not the source-space directional reparameterization, which NoPo4D and ViewSplat already cover. It is the combination of three parts: temporal filtering of directional weight coefficients in the static source frame, independent of viewer motion; distillation from an occlusion-aware target-space IBR teacher; and an end-to-end live multi-view-display and multi-party demonstration with a views-per-second scaling analysis. It is best framed as a SIGGRAPH Asia / IEEE VR systems paper, "amortized, temporally stable live IBR for light-field telepresence". NoPo4D-style opacity SH should be credited as prior art and used as an ablation baseline. It should not be claimed as a new representation.

sharpened.title: Blend Once, View Many: Viewer-Invariant Source-Space Blending for Temporally Stable Light-Field Telepresence
sharpened.one_liner: On a static calibrated rig, move learned IBR blending from the target image into a low-order directional field on the source pixels. The field is predicted once per frame and filtered in the fixed camera frame. Every extra eye, viewer or light-field view then costs only a rasterization pass, with no K-set popping and no flicker induced by viewer motion.
sharpened.core_claim: On a static calibrated RGB-D/stereo rig, the per-camera blend weights learned by a geometry-guided target-space IBR blender (Ha et al. style) are low-bandwidth in target direction once visibility is handled by z-buffered rasterization. Per-source-pixel directional fields with at most 16 coefficients per camera (SH order 3 or 8 spherical lobes), predicted feed-forward once per frame, get within 0.5 dB PSNR and 0.015 LPIPS of the per-view teacher at held-out real cameras. They render at least 45 display views at 30 fps or more (512p per view, one consumer GPU). Across views and under viewer motion they are strictly more consistent than per-view target-space blending: EPI/MEt3R inter-view error and flicker along a moving-viewer trajectory are both lower by 30% or more. This holds even when the target-space baselines get soft all-N weighting and K-set hysteresis. The claim is falsified if the fitted oracle field needs more than 16 coefficients to reach 0.5 dB of the teacher, or if a hysteresis-augmented target-space blender matches the consistency gains.
sharpened.key_insight: Separate visibility from preference. Which source samples are visible from a target ray is a geometric question. The z-buffer (plus a shared TSDF computed once per frame) answers it exactly and cheaply for every view. Once visibility is removed, the rest of a learned blender's output, which camera to prefer for a visible surface point, is a smooth, low-frequency function of target direction. This is plenoptic-sampling intuition: the bandwidth is set by camera spacing and surface reflectance, not by the viewer. Because the rig is static, each source pixel is a persistent entity. The preference field can live there: it is computed once, shared by all viewers, and filtered over time in a frame that never moves. Target-space pipelines cannot do this, because their blending frame moves with every viewer and their weights change abruptly when the K-set switches. The viewer pose enters only at rasterization, so it can be late-latched, which also reduces motion-to-photon latency.
sharpened.method: Inputs: N (4-10) calibrated, synchronized RGB-D streams; depth from a sensor or a real-time stereo front-end, with its cost reported. (1) A shared per-frame geometry stage runs once: pixel-sized Gaussians per source view (as in Ha et al.), a low-resolution image-based TSDF fused over all N cameras (not the K nearest), and per-source visibility and confidence maps from TSDF consistency. (2) The source-space preference net is a light 2D CNN per camera with epipolar or cross-view attention to the 2-3 geometrically nearest cameras. Inputs are RGB, depth, depth-confidence, TSDF-consistency residual, surface normal, and rig geometry encoded as the directions to the other cameras. For each source pixel it outputs a directional preference field w_n(p, d): SH order 2-3, or M=8 spherical lobes whose axes are initialized to the rig's camera directions. It also outputs a small SH colour residual (order 1-2) and an edge-softness/opacity term to suppress flying pixels. (3) Rendering is per view, with no neural network. Rasterize all sources' Gaussians with a z-test (soft depth-test band). Accumulate colour times alpha times softplus(w_n(p, d_target)) and normalize over cameras. Fill disocclusions from a persistent, TSDF-gated background plate (possible because the rig is static) plus one shared low-resolution hole-filler per display frame. The back-end is a coherent LFD rasterizer (CoherentRaster-style attribute reuse or LFDPR-style point splatting) that renders 32-45 views or subpixel-interleaved output directly. (4) Temporal: a confidence-gated EMA filters the coefficients (not the colours) per source pixel. The gate is learned from the TSDF residual, the depth change and the colour change. Background pixels get long-horizon averaging. (5) Training: distil from a re-implemented Ha-style target-space U-Net teacher (K=4, with TSDF and depth feedback). Use about 100 virtual targets per frame sampled in and slightly beyond the rig hull, with a per-camera weight-matching loss and a photometric loss. Add a photometric loss at held-out real cameras, an EPI-gradient smoothness loss across adjacent virtual views, and a temporal warping loss on 4-8 frame clips. The teacher is dropped at test time. Runtime budget on an RTX 4090/5090: under 15 ms for the per-frame source stage (N=8, 512x384 per source), plus about 0.3-0.6 ms per view of rasterization, so 45 views fit in about 40 ms.
sharpened.why_not_engineering: The paper contributes three things beyond a faster pipeline. First, a measurable empirical claim with a principled explanation: the angular bandwidth of learned IBR blending once visibility is factored out. It is quantified by an oracle SH/lobe fitting study (coefficients needed vs. error, as a function of camera baseline and material specularity) and connected to plenoptic sampling theory. Nobody has measured how many angular degrees of freedom learned blenders actually use. Second, a new failure mode and metric for target-space IBR: flicker induced by viewer motion, which K-nearest pipelines cause even on static content. The paper shows that source-space parameterization removes it by construction. Third, a representation-level argument for temporal filtering: in the static source frame, filtering requires no reprojection and is independent of the viewer. It is compared against target-space depth feedback under viewer motion. The system (45-view live LFD, multi-party) is the demonstration, not the claim. Every claim has a kill condition.
sharpened.differentiation: NoPo4D (arXiv 2605.22190) already predicts per-source-pixel Gaussians with SH view-dependent opacity from static-rig multi-view video, as a learned cross-camera confidence. We credit it as the representation's closest prior art and use it as a direct ablation baseline (opacity SH trained end-to-end, no distillation, no source-space temporal filter, no TSDF visibility). NoPo4D is pose-free, not real-time and not evaluated on multi-view display consistency. Our contributions are the bandwidth study, the viewer-invariance and temporal-filtering analysis, and the live multi-view display system. ViewSplat (2603.25265) predicts view-conditioned attribute residuals for static, unposed scenes; it has no temporal model and no multi-view-display study, and its View-MLP is a baseline for the choice of basis. GPS-Gaussian/GPS-Gaussian+ (2312.02155, 2411.11363) already make extra views cost only rasterization but have scalar opacity and no cross-camera preference; they show the quality we add at equal cost. Sweeping-plane LFD rendering (2508.18540), CoherentRaster (2605.04509), DirectL (2407.14053) and LFDPR (2601.19901) amortize rasterization for static optimized scenes and drop or ignore learned view-dependent blending. We use them as back-ends and claim none of their contribution. Target-space live IBR includes Ha et al. (2505.18932), 3DTV (2604.11211), VirtualCube (2112.06730) and Tele-Aloha (2405.14866). We compare at equal views per second and give them hysteresis and soft all-N weighting, so the gain is attributable to the source-space parameterization. LentiAvatar (2606.10550) is avatar-specific and monocular; ours is general-scene, multi-camera and authentic.

experiments.capture_notes: The core scientific claims (angular bandwidth, teacher-student gap, inter-view and viewer-motion consistency, views-per-second scaling) can all be run on public data. Technicolor and ActorsHQ/DNA-Rendering give dense held-out views, and Panoptic gives Kinect RGB-D. Custom hardware is needed only for the live claim: a 6-8 camera synchronized rig (e.g. hardware-triggered machine-vision or ZED/RealSense units) plus one Looking Glass panel (about 16-32 inch, a few thousand USD), for an end-to-end latency measurement and a small user study (about 15-20 participants, IRB). Without it, the paper drops to a CVPR-style method paper and loses its strongest selling point for SIGGRAPH Asia or IEEE VR.

review.first_two_week_test: Oracle bandwidth fit, no student network yet. (Days 1-4) On DyNeRF (2-3 scenes) and Technicolor (2 scenes), with offline stereo or provided depth, train or re-implement a simplified Ha-style target-space U-Net blender (K=4, depth plus camera-feature inputs; a few GPU-days). If time is short, use ENeRF's per-source blending weights as a stand-in teacher. (Days 5-8) For 10 frames, render the teacher over about 150 virtual targets densely sampled in the rig hull. For every target pixel, attribute each camera's weight to the source pixel it was splatted from (the z-buffer winner), then fit per-source-pixel SH (orders 0-4) and 8 lobes by weighted least squares. (Days 9-12) Re-render held-out real cameras and a dense virtual sweep with the fitted fields using the z-tested Gaussian rasterizer only. Measure: (a) PSNR/LPIPS gap to the teacher; (b) EPI error and viewer-motion flicker along the sweep, compared with the teacher with and without K-set hysteresis; (c) raster ms for 45 views at 512p with 8 x 512x384 source Gaussians. (Days 13-14) Plot coefficients vs gap and decide. GO if order at most 3 (16 coefficients) lands within 0.5 dB and 0.015 LPIPS, flicker drops by 30% or more over the hysteresis-augmented teacher, and 45-view raster fits in under 50 ms. This is an upper bound on what the feed-forward student can reach, so a failure here kills the idea cheaply.
review.kill_criteria: Kill or re-scope if any of these holds. (1) The oracle fit needs more than 16 coefficients per camera per pixel to get within 0.5 dB PSNR / 0.015 LPIPS of the target-space teacher. Learned blending would then not be low-bandwidth in direction, and the core premise fails. (2) A target-space teacher strengthened with soft all-N weights plus K-set hysteresis reaches within 10% of the source-space EPI/MEt3R and viewer-motion-flicker numbers. The consistency claim would then be a tuning trick. (3) After 3 months, the feed-forward student stays more than 1 dB below the teacher at held-out cameras, even with the teacher's inputs. (4) NoPo4D-style opacity SH trained end-to-end in the same backbone matches the full method within noise on quality, EPI and temporal metrics. The telepresence-specific parts (distillation, source-space temporal filtering, TSDF visibility) would then add nothing, and the paper would be a re-implementation. (5) Even with a coherent LFD rasterizer, 45 views at 512p cannot run at 30 fps or more on one consumer GPU at useful source resolution. The amortization headline would then be empty, and only the consistency result would remain, perhaps as a workshop paper.

reviewer_objections.objection: This is NoPo4D's view-dependent opacity SH, plus GPS-Gaussian's 'extra views are just rasterization', applied to a light-field display: an engineering combination.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: We credit both explicitly and do not claim the representation. The contributions are: (i) the first measurement of the angular bandwidth of learned IBR blending after factoring out visibility, with a camera-baseline and specularity analysis that tells practitioners how many coefficients a rig needs; (ii) viewer-motion flicker as a failure mode of target-space IBR, with a metric and a by-construction fix; (iii) source-frame coefficient filtering, which needs no reprojection and is independent of the viewer. The ablation that swaps in NoPo4D-style opacity SH with everything else fixed isolates what our telepresence-specific parts add. The live 45-view display result with measured latency does not exist in prior work.

reviewer_objections.objection: Directional weights on source pixels cannot represent occlusion that depends on the target view. Distillation from a target-space U-Net that sees all K warped images jointly must lose quality at depth edges and disocclusions.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: This is exactly what the visibility/preference split addresses. Occlusion is resolved per view by the z-tested rasterizer and the shared TSDF, which cost nothing extra per view. Only the smooth preference is amortized. We report the gap separately inside edge bands and disocclusion masks, and we include a shared low-resolution hole-filler per display frame. If the gap is concentrated at edges, the result is itself informative, and the per-view cost of the filler is reported honestly in the Pareto plot.

reviewer_objections.objection: Just add hysteresis or soft weighting to the target-space blender and run it at lower resolution; there is no need for a new parameterization.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: This baseline is included by design: Ha et al. with soft all-N weights plus K-set hysteresis, and additionally amortized with sweeping planes. Hysteresis reduces popping but makes weights depend on viewer history. So different viewers of the same instant see inconsistent content, and the network cost still scales with the number of views. We compare at equal views per second and equal resolution, and a kill criterion covers the case where this baseline matches us.

reviewer_objections.objection: Specular and high-frequency view-dependent effects will not fit into order-2 or order-3 SH, so quality will collapse on real telepresence content (glasses, skin sheen, screens).
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: The bandwidth study is stratified by a specular mask and by camera baseline, and it reports where low order fails. The model keeps a separate SH colour residual, and the lobe basis is initialized to the rig's camera directions, which concentrates the capacity where it is needed. For sparse rigs, the observed angular signal is itself band-limited by camera spacing (plenoptic sampling), so a higher-order basis cannot recover content the cameras never saw. We show this empirically with ActorsHQ subsets of varying density.

reviewer_objections.objection: The evaluation is mostly on held-out rig cameras, which are sparse; claims about 45-view light-field quality and user-perceived popping are not supported by ground truth.
reviewer_objections.rebuttal: Technicolor's 4x4 array and dense ActorsHQ/DNA-Rendering subsets give ground-truth angular sampling at display-like baselines. EPI and MEt3R measure inter-view consistency without ground truth. The live Looking Glass demo includes a controlled 2AFC user study on popping and flicker at equal frame rate, plus measured motion-to-photon latency. We also release the rendered view sets so others can check the consistency metrics.

effort.months: 6-8 (2 weeks oracle study; about 3 months student network plus temporal filtering on public data; about 2 months live rig, LFD back-end integration and user study; 1 month writing)
effort.people: 1 PhD student full-time plus 1 part-time student or engineer for the rig, LFD rasterizer and user study
effort.compute: 2-4 GPUs with 24-48 GB (RTX 4090/5090 or A6000-class) for teacher and student training; one consumer GPU for the live demo; hardware about USD 5-12k (Looking Glass 16-32 inch plus 6-8 synchronized cameras, or re-use an existing rig)

review.venue: SIGGRAPH Asia / ACM TOG (systems plus analysis framing with the live LFD demo). Fallbacks: IEEE VR or ISMAR (TVCG track), emphasizing multi-viewer and multi-party gaze and user study. A CVPR submission is possible only without the live demo, and would be weaker because of NoPo4D overlap.
review.synergies: (1) Streaming and compute split for multi-party calls: the per-frame source-space coefficient maps are a compact, viewer-independent payload. The sender computes them once and every receiver only rasterizes, which gives a natural sender/receiver split and fits viewer-adaptive, per-camera bitrate allocation; a strong companion paper. (2) Persistent background and long-term memory for static rigs: the same 'static rig means persistent source pixel' argument supports the background plate and memory-based disocclusion filling (cf. arXiv 2607.15271). (3) Learned real-time depth front-ends (Fast-FoundationStereo, temporally consistent stereo such as PPMStereo), whose confidence feeds the visibility and temporal gate. (4) Low-latency or HMD telepresence: viewer pose enters only at rasterization, so late-latching and binocular-consistent rendering come for free. This can be combined with stereo-consistent generative fixers, which must also be amortized across views. (5) Coherent LFD rasterizers (CoherentRaster, LFDPR, sweeping planes) as back-ends: this cluster supplies the live, learned, temporally stable front-end they lack. A paper series could run: oracle bandwidth study and method (this paper), then source-space streaming and compression, then multi-party gaze-correct deployment.

cited_work_check.title: LiVo: Toward Bandwidth-adaptive Fully-Immersive Volumetric Video Conferencing (Proc. ACM Netw. / CoNEXT 2025)
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed through the Semantic Scholar API (DOI 10.1145/3768981; Ghosh, Shin, ..., Ortega, Rao, Rowe, Govindan). The abstract describes composing multi-camera scenes into several 2D-codec streams, a new geometry encoding, dynamic apportioning of bandwidth between streams, and culling of out-of-view content. The ideator's summary is accurate. The ACM full text returned 403, so I could not check how the apportioning works (whether it uses a rendered-view quality model or a heuristic). That point needs checking before claiming 'renderer-derived' allocation as new.

cited_work_check.title: GSStream: 3D Gaussian Splatting based Volumetric Scene Streaming System
cited_work_check.note: Mar 2026. Collaborative viewport prediction plus DRL bitrate adaptation for 3DGS scene data, i.e. an output representation rather than live RGB-D inputs. Accurate.

cited_work_check.title: AirGS: Real-Time 4D Gaussian Streaming for Free-Viewpoint Video (INFOCOM 2026)
cited_work_check.note: Dec 2025, INFOCOM 2026. 4DGS packed into 2D channels, keyframe selection, ILP plus pruning for transmission size. Characterising it as viewport/DRL-driven is loose: the abstract describes ILP and pruning, not DRL. Its core point, that it streams a representation rather than RGB-D inputs, is correct.

cited_work_check.title: ReVo: A Cross-Layer Reliable Volumetric Videoconferencing System
cited_work_check.note: Apr 2026, UMass. Decoupled RGB and depth WebRTC streams, selective network-layer FEC and post-decode neural recovery. Not viewer-adaptive. Accurate.

cited_work_check.title: One-Click Upgrade from 2D to 3D: Sandwiched RGB-D Video Compression for Stereoscopic Teleconferencing
cited_work_check.note: Confirmed from the full HTML. Processes 'each frame in the video independently', uses a disparity-warping (novel-view) loss and a JPEG proxy, and reports no flicker or temporal metric. It does learn implicit 'smart bit-allocation' between views and modalities. The ideator's 'per-frame, no temporal objective' is accurate.

cited_work_check.title: A Single Atlas is All You Need: Decoder-Side Gaussian Splatting for Immersive Video
cited_work_check.note: May 2026 (Mieloch and Perry). The abstract does say lossy compression acts as an implicit low-pass filter that stabilises feed-forward splat prediction. It sends no depth. Accurate.

cited_work_check.note: May 2026, 2D video only (AV1/HEVC/VP9/H.264). Reports non-linear degradation of temporal consistency. Accurate.

cited_work_check.title: GS-SCNet: Generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting enabled Semantic Coding for Real-Time Immersive Video Communications
cited_work_check.note: Apr 2026. Disparity-guided stereo semantic codec driving a receiver-side 3DGS predictor. No temporal handling is mentioned. Accurate.

cited_work_check.note: Confirmed through the Semantic Scholar API. Uses RGB and depth frames to find temporal changes and sends only the deltas (up to 71% bandwidth reduction). This directly pre-empts the 'don't resend static regions' part of Idea 1.

threats.title: LiVo: Toward Bandwidth-adaptive Fully-Immersive Volumetric Video Conferencing
threats.what_overlaps: Live multi-camera RGB-D conferencing over standard 2D codecs and RTC transport, with dynamic bandwidth apportioning between colour and depth streams and viewer field-of-view culling. This is the system skeleton of Idea 1 (camera and stream allocation driven by the viewer). The co-authors (Ortega) come from the view-synthesis-distortion rate-allocation tradition, so its apportioning may already use a rendered-quality model; I could not verify this because the full text returned 403.
threats.what_remains_different: No learned IBR renderer. Importance is geometric culling, not the renderer's back-projected blend-weight sensitivity. There is (as far as the abstract shows) no per-CTU QP shaping inside a stream, no temporal-consistency or flicker term, and no persistent TSDF receiver state used for concealment or skipping.

threats.title: Adaptive Streaming in Interactive Multiview Video Systems (Zhang, Toni, Frossard et al.), plus the earlier IMVS line (e.g. arXiv 1506.07823)
threats.what_overlaps: The core conceptual insight of Idea 1 is already there: choose which camera views and quality levels to send so as to maximise expected synthesised-view quality over the user's navigation distribution under a bandwidth budget, trading coding artifacts against synthesis artifacts. Idea 1's 'integrate importance over the predicted viewer-pose distribution and do Lagrangian allocation' repeats this formulation.
threats.what_remains_different: DIBR with analytic or measured view-synthesis distortion (VSD), per-view granularity, offline or pre-encoded content, and no learned renderer, no per-CTU sensitivity, no flicker term and no live 6DoF HMD pose prediction.

threats.title: View-synthesis-distortion (VSD) estimation for 3D video coding and rate allocation (Bi and Liang 2025; auto-weighted layer VSD 2022)
threats.what_overlaps: Models how texture and depth coding errors propagate into DIBR-synthesised views, including a region-based blending estimate, explicitly 'for optimizing resource allocation in real-time applications' such as interactive FVV. The idea that 'depth errors are harmless where the renderer ignores them, so shape rather than minimise them' is the long-standing 3D-HEVC VSO/VSD principle and weakens Idea 2's rate-control component.
threats.what_remains_different: Training-free analytic DIBR models with two reference views. They do not use a learned blend network or TSDF fusion, have no temporal or flicker component, and do no end-to-end learned pre- or post-processing.

threats.title: Sandwiched RGB-D Video Compression / Sandwiched Video Compression (Hu, Guleryuz, Chou et al.)
threats.what_overlaps: Idea 2's architecture is exactly this: neural pre- and post-processors around HEVC/H.264, trained through a differentiable codec proxy with a novel-view (disparity-warp) rendering loss, learning implicit bit allocation across views and modalities for telepresence. The companion paper arXiv 2303.11473 does the same for video.
threats.what_remains_different: Frame-independent processing, no flicker or temporal loss, a simple warp rather than a learned IBR plus TSDF renderer in the loss, no recurrent post-filter using decoder state, and no explicit CTU-level rate control.

threats.title: PD-4DGS: Progressive Decomposition of 4D Gaussian Splatting for Bandwidth-Adaptive Dynamic Scene Streaming
threats.what_overlaps: Explicitly puts flicker into a rate-distortion objective: a 'Gaussian-entropy attribute rate-distortion loss together with a temporal mask consistency regulariser ... suppressing low-bitrate flicker'. Together with V^3 (temporal loss in Gaussian-video coding), this means 'rate-distortion-flicker' as a concept is not new on the representation side.
threats.what_remains_different: Offline 4DGS representation coding for ABR. Not live, not RGB-D input coding, and no IBR renderer sensitivity or viewer-pose-driven allocation.

threats.title: DeltaStream: 2D-Inferred Delta Encoding for Live Volumetric Video Streaming
threats.what_overlaps: Live RGB-D volumetric streaming that finds temporal changes from 2D RGB and depth and sends only block-based deltas, i.e. 'static regions need not be resent'. LiveVV (arXiv 2310.08205) likewise reuses static content with saliency decimation.
threats.what_remains_different: Point-cloud delta coding by change detection, not concealment by a persistent TSDF or IBR state weighted by renderer contribution. No flicker objective and no learned rendering.

threats.title: GSStream (viewport-predictive DRL bitrate adaptation for 3DGS); Adaptive 3DGS Video Streaming with saliency tiling and meta-learned ABR (arXiv 2507.14454)
threats.what_overlaps: Viewer-pose-predictive bitrate adaptation for volumetric content.
threats.what_remains_different: Streams a pre-built 3DGS representation tile by tile. Not live multi-camera RGB-D, and not tied to a renderer's source-pixel sensitivity.

threats.title: Foveated Compression for Immersive Telepresence Visualization
threats.what_overlaps: Per-block QP modulation inside a standard codec, driven by the viewer (eye tracking), for telepresence streams. This is the same codec-side mechanism as Idea 1's per-CTU QP maps.
threats.what_remains_different: Driven by 2D gaze on a single stream. No multi-camera or novel-view mapping.

threats.title: CAGS: Color-Adaptive Volumetric Video Streaming with Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting (SIGGRAPH 2026)
threats.what_overlaps: Bandwidth-adaptive volumetric streaming for telepresence, with receiver-side correction of compression artifacts using reference images.
threats.what_remains_different: Gaussian levels of detail. Not pose-driven, no flicker objective, not RGB-D IBR.
